Dustfall.name: Dustfall
Dustfall.basicInfo: Dustfall is the broad settlement itself: stacked cargo homes, patched environmental towers and salvaged plating strung along a single working strip. It stands in tropical coastal desert near volcanic Ignivex, with ocean access and no major freshwater river serving as a settlement-wide supply artery, so the air is dry, the wind scores every exposed surface and the daylight arrives hard and flat off pale ground. The place is built from cargo modules, alien metal, old stone, reinforced glass and salvaged infrastructure, lit by practical work lamps, gate light, strip lighting and that desert daylight, and personalised throughout with house fragments, paint, fabric, tools, signs and family objects. Nobody rules it, so the strip carries the town's civic life instead, from the water station to the job rail to the communal meal yard. Nothing here is technologically backward: advanced Starian machinery stands inside hand-built repair, and shortage turns on cost, compatible parts, maintenance and coordination rather than on primitive equipment. Households tell different accounts of when the accumulation became home and agree on no founding date. It is dry, armed, worn and genuinely inhabited, with weapons rests standing beside family tables, childcare shared across doorways and shopkeepers sweeping dust off good machinery before opening.
Dustfall.hiddenInfo: The settlement hub deliberately does not absorb the specialised work of its bars, repair district, housing, gate, perimeter or routehead, and the gap shows most when something breaks. A Corsair shipment of Contair equipment has failed to arrive, so ammunition, medical stock, spare parts and Lunar Gate components are all short at once, and no major house is coming to sort it out. Prices along the strip are already moving. Public arguments about who is hoarding, who is feeding undeclared arrivals and whether the gate should be shut for a while surface here before they reach the Long Shot's dispute table. Draxen Sol organises town-wide response without holding any office, Sennra Sol's reputation spills out of her bar into the street, and Kell Ardan is reliably somewhere he is not supposed to be. Maressa Oryn keeps an immaculate garment-cleaning storefront here and accepts contract killings elsewhere, which the strip knows and does not discuss. Temporary incident delegates can be authorised by affected households, businesses and crews during an emergency; their mandate expires with the incident and creates no permanent authority.

Main Settlement Strip.description: The settlement's spine: a wind-scored run of reinforced shopfronts, cargo-module frontage and hard-worn paving under strip lighting and work lamps. It is open to the sky, and the desert daylight comes down hard enough that most frontage carries improvised shade in whatever materials a household had spare. Everything civic passes along it, from deliveries to arguments to first arrivals. Carriers work loads along the paving, shopkeepers clear their thresholds before opening, children are sent along it on errands, and crews back from a route walk it slowly so that people can see them. No one holds an office here and no one directs the traffic; precedence is settled face to face and then honoured. The dust gets into everything, and every doorway has a seal somebody has repaired at least twice.

Public Water and Environmental Station.description: A patched treatment and distribution point where households draw potable supply, top up collectors and argue about contribution and maintenance. It is a squat block of plating and reinforced glass with tanks braced against the wind, humming at a pitch residents stop hearing within a week of moving in. Filter stacks and control panels are advanced machinery wrapped in hand-built repairs. Ocean water can be processed with the technology available, but no authority has held Dustfall long enough to sustain a settlement-wide coastal supply, so local treatment, recycling, storage and purchased deliveries cover the difference unevenly. Households bring their own containers and take their turn. Queue conversation is almost always about whose turn it is to pay for the part that failed last month.

Shared Cargo Court.description: An open square of stacked containers and sling frames where incoming freight is broken down and divided among carriers and crews. The container walls make the only real shade in the middle of the day, and the ground between them is packed hard and scarred by years of dragged crates. Loads are sorted by terrain, warning and passenger need rather than by any schedule. Dustfall is a transshipment point rather than a destination, so much of what lands here is bound elsewhere before long, and the division is argued out among operators who have handled one another's freight for years. Fragile stock, medicine, restricted cargo and ordinary household goods pass through the same frames. On a good day the court smells of hot metal and packing foam; on a bad one it sits conspicuously empty.

Open Carry Walk.description: The stretch where Dustfall's weapons culture is simply visible: sidearms worn openly, rifles slung, nobody remarking on it. Weapons stay visible unless someone has a reason to hide one, and the people carrying them are cooks, teachers, parents, haulers and boarding-house keepers as often as they are crew. Patched armour plates, flight-safe holsters and repaired field kit pass along the walk beside shopping and lesson bags. Custom rather than law governs behaviour here, and the custom is strict about muzzle discipline near children. Nothing about the display is theatrical; it is compensation for the plain fact that the settlement offers no guarantee danger will wait for a defender. Newcomers who overreact to an armed passerby are identified within the first hour.

Informal Job Rail.description: A length of railing and posted scrap where day work is offered and taken without contracts: hauling, digging out a buried housing, standing a night watch. The rail is a welded run of salvaged bar, polished bright along the top by the forearms of people waiting, with slates and scrap panel hung off it carrying whatever is on offer this morning. Payment is agreed face to face and remembered publicly, in credits or in a favour whose terms both sides can state. People are free to refuse a job, and everyone else is free to remember the refusal. Householders come here for an afternoon's help as readily as crews come for a body to fill out a run. Standing at the rail is not shameful in Dustfall, but standing there too many days running gets noticed.

Dustfall Meal Yard.description: The communal kitchen yard: cooking stations, a shared serving line, household tables, a container-return point and a preservation-and-wash workspace. It is walled enough to break the wind and roofed in sections against the glare, and the cooking equipment is sophisticated, repeatedly repaired and kept scrupulously clean. Resident cooks assemble a substantial mixed grill from whatever actually arrived, with Messa Taar and Brask Hollan often involved. Households that cannot each run a full kitchen eat here as routine rather than charity, children are fed first and watched by whoever is nearest, and a crew coming back intact is reason enough for the yard to fill. During real shortage the temporary-sharing custom takes over and debts resume afterwards, which everyone understands going in.

Public Repair Board.description: A weathered display of open repair requests, parts wanted, warnings and settled jobs, updated by anyone with a marker and a grievance. The board is a panel of salvaged plate under a shade hood, its surface written over so many times that old entries show faintly through the new ones. It is the closest thing the settlement has to public works. Breaking essential infrastructure means helping repair it or paying someone who can, and this is where that obligation becomes public: a household names what failed, a technician names what it would take, and the gap between the two sits there in front of everybody. Longstanding entries that nobody will fund become a running joke and, occasionally, a genuine emergency.

Mixed-House Housing Edge.description: Where the strip frays into housing: cargo modules painted with fragments of half a dozen house colours, none of them ruling anything. Stairs run up the outsides, walkways bridge between roofs, and the gaps between modules are strung with drying laundry and cable runs somebody has labelled by hand. Small-house survivors, refugees and unaffiliated workers live side by side with their old banners cut down into curtains. Some marks are displayed proudly, some cut away, some painted over and still legible underneath, and the neighbours know which is which without discussing it. Doors stand open in the cooler hours and the households mind one another's children as a matter of course. Children fly short hops between roofs while somebody shouts about landing distances.

Quiet Thread storefront.description: Maressa Oryn's public counter for garment cleaning, residue removal and formal repair, with everything returned in better condition than it arrived. The room is sealed properly and lit evenly rather than harshly, and the equipment behind the counter is well-maintained current work rather than anything improvised. The shop is quiet, precise and noticeably free of dust, which in Dustfall reads as a considerable and deliberate expense. Ordinary customers bring mourning clothes, a child's coat to be let out, armour-cloth whose weave needs restoring, and they are served with the same exactness as anyone else. Customers who bring in clothing with awkward stains are asked no questions, which is part of what they are paying for.

General Arrival Shelf.description: A broad open landing shelf with worn flight markers where travellers set down and orient themselves. The surface is plated, swept and scoured pale by wind-driven dust, the markers repainted often enough to be read and never often enough to look new. Arrivals are met by nobody official; the shelf simply faces the strip and lets people work out where to go. There is no checkpoint, no registration and nobody asking for documents, which is the first thing most arrivals notice and the second thing they distrust. Water sits at the edge of the shelf and a first container is not charged for. Newcomers usually stand here a moment too long, which locals read as accurately as a manifest.

The Held Seat.description: A small café on the strip with repaired fittings, an effective dust seal and seats people actually want to use: a brew-and-order counter, inside tables, a waiting bench and a wash-and-service compartment. The seal is the selling point; inside, the air is still and the light softer than the glare outside, and people linger well past what they ordered. Cyrra comes straight or with Selka, alongside Terva bread and whatever cooked stock exists. A clear display shows what is genuinely available rather than an impossible menu, and it is amended through the day as things run out. Off-shift workers, parents waiting on lessons and crews killing an hour before a load is ready all use the same tables, and the bench by the door is where people sit when they are early for something they are dreading.

The Long Shot.name: The Long Shot
The Long Shot.basicInfo:
The Long Shot is Sennra Sol's bar and the closest thing Dustfall has to a civic hall without ever officially becoming one. It is a low reinforced building of cargo plating, old stone and salvaged frontage, sealed hard against the dust, lit by work lamps and strip lighting that leave the corners dim while the counter stays bright. Jobs are posted, disputes are heard, reputations are made and refugees are introduced to people who might help. None of that carries legal force: Dustfall has no mayor, sheriff or council, and Sennra's standing is earned rather than granted, holding only as far as the room. The trade is ordinary for most of the day, with meals served, rooms rented above, off-shift workers arguing about a repair and somebody's children doing lesson work at a corner table until they are collected. In the evening the room fills with crews, technicians, hauliers and household heads, weapons set down at the door by house rule rather than by law. It is public, dry, armed and extremely observant, and the shelf of names by the wall makes it clear what the settlement has already paid.

Work on offer here: Dustfall — The Yard Protection Debt (ask Della Vossik).
The Long Shot.hiddenInfo: Sennra's authority here is earned rather than granted, and it holds only as far as the room. She refuses to recognise warrants backed solely by Dravon authority, and Ravik Rusk has not yet tested how far the town would actually defend that refusal — a confrontation everyone can see coming and nobody has scheduled. The Town Memory Shelf is the settlement's real record of who died, who left and who is still owed something, and Sennra quietly sends grieving families on to Ovar Kethrin when a name needs formally recording. Hearings at the Dispute Table have no legal force; they work because the people present agree to be bound, and a refusal to accept a ruling is itself a public act. Buying a drink buys neither a hearing nor social acceptance. Kell Ardan has been banned seven times and treats the count as an attendance record. During the current supply failure the job board fills with work that is really about the missing shipment, and who volunteers without payment is being noted as carefully as who demands it up front.

Main Bar.description: A long reinforced counter under practical lighting, salvaged plating polished smooth by years of forearms. The room behind it is deeper than it looks from the street, floored in mismatched plate, with tables that have each been repaired by a different hand and a ceiling of exposed structure hung with lamps. Sennra works it herself most evenings, with relief servers when the room fills. Kessar alcohol, Cyrra and Crisped Terva are the reliable orders; the kitchen's longer meals depend entirely on what the shelves currently hold. Conversation runs loud and stops short when somebody unfamiliar comes through the door, then resumes a little more carefully. A board behind the counter lists what has actually run out, and it is updated more honestly than most things in Dustfall.

Job Board Wall.description: A panelled wall of posted work: escorts, hauling, searches, repairs and contracts that never quite say what they are. The panels are salvaged sheet, scored and rewritten so often that the surface has a grain to it, and the lighting above them is the brightest in the building because Sennra got tired of people misreading terms and blaming her. Postings are taken down by whoever accepts them, which makes the empty spaces as informative as the filled ones. Ordinary work outnumbers the dangerous kind: a household wanting a collector rehung, a shop wanting a night's watch, a family wanting someone found. Arguments about a misdescribed job usually end up at the Dispute Table within a week.

Back Booths.description: Deeper seating for smaller groups, screened enough for a private conversation and open enough that nobody can pretend they were not there. The screens are salvaged panel and stretched fabric, the benches rebuilt more than once, and the light drops off enough that faces read as outlines from the main room. Crew business, hiring and difficult family talks happen in roughly equal measure, along with a good deal of eating, flirting and complaining about parts that have not arrived. Sennra keeps the booths in her sightline and does not pretend otherwise. A quiet booth in the Long Shot does not automatically contain a criminal negotiation, whatever newcomers assume.

Dispute Table.description: A heavy fixed table kept clear for hearings: salvage claims, broken contracts, protection debts, questions of whether someone stays welcome. It is bolted down, scarred across the top, and surrounded by enough floor for the people who will want to stand and listen. Sennra sets the order of speaking and will pause music or a performance to make room. Nothing decided here has legal force; hearings work because the people present agree to be bound, and refusing a ruling is itself a public act that everyone in the room witnesses. A warrant from outside is not automatically recognised at this table, and neither is refugee status as proof of anything. When no hearing is running and she permits it, it is simply the best table in the house.

Weapons Rest.description: Racks and clamps just inside the door where sidearms and longer weapons are set down under Sennra's house rules. The rack is welded salvage, each position numbered by hand, with a shelf underneath for field kits and a bin for anything leaking. Nothing here is confiscated and nothing is a law; it is her establishment and her conditions, and a guest who dislikes them is free to drink elsewhere. Weapons stay visible in Dustfall unless someone has reason to hide one, so the rest is about the room rather than about concealment. Which weapons stay on a person, and whose, is one of the fastest reads of standing available in Dustfall.

Upper Sleeping Rooms.description: Rented rooms above the bar with patched environmental sealing, reached by a narrow stair behind the counter. The rooms are small and plain, cargo-module partitions with a window each, a strip light, a shelf and a hook, and the dust seals are checked more often than in most paid lodging in the settlement. Sennra lives on this floor, which is why the rooms are quiet and why nobody tries much up here. Travellers, crews between contracts and families waiting on a decision all take them, sometimes for a night and sometimes for considerably longer. Guests get clean bedding, a working lock and the noise of the room below until closing.

Rear Cargo Exit.description: A wide service door onto the back lane, used for stock, deliveries and people who would rather not cross the main room. The lane behind is unlit and narrow, and the door itself is heavy plate on rebuilt runners that complain when the wind has been blowing grit into them. The threshold is scuffed down to bare metal from crates dragged over it. Deliveries come through here at odd hours, the kitchen's waste goes out, and a person arriving in poor condition can reach the stair without being seen by the whole bar. Sennra knows exactly who uses it and lets the knowledge sit unmentioned unless she needs it.

Town Memory Shelf.description: A shelf of small objects and marked plates for the dead, the missing and the departed, kept from becoming either a shrine or party scenery. It runs along a stretch of wall at standing height, lit by one plain lamp, holding tools, fragments of house marking, a child's toy, plates cut and scratched by whoever brought them. People add to it without ceremony and stand at it without explaining, and nobody is asked to move along. Sennra quietly sends grieving families on to Ovar Kethrin when a name needs formally recording, since the shelf keeps no list and makes no claim to be a record office. It is the nearest thing Dustfall has to a public record of its own cost.

Front Entrance Watch.description: The step and awning where Yarek Suld or whoever is on the door watches the street and the people approaching it. The awning is salvaged sheet on braced poles, the step worn concave, and the position gives a clear view along the frontage in both directions while staying out of the worst of the daylight. He is not a municipal officer and has no authority past the frame. What happens here is mostly greeting: regulars named, newcomers looked over, a crew told the room is full tonight, a parent asked to collect a child who has been sitting inside too long. Most trouble is stopped here by being noticed early rather than by anyone laying hands on it.

Grit and Supply.name: Grit and Supply
Grit and Supply.basicInfo:
Veyra Corsair's supply house is Dustfall's most dependable connection to broader Nexaran trade, which is not the same as a reliable one. It occupies a long building of cargo modules and reinforced frontage with a high roll-door bay at the back, lit by hard overhead lamps that leave nothing on the shelves flattering. Ammunition, secondhand Contair stock, medical supply and gate components pass across its counters when they arrive at all. Corsair shipments come irregularly and never cheaply, so stock is deep in some lines and simply absent in others, and regulars learn to buy the compatible part rather than the ideal one. None of the equipment here is primitive; the constraints are cost, compatibility, maintenance and whether a load reached the settlement. The floor is crowded, commercially sharp and irregularly stocked, and the people working it range from crews resupplying for a route to a parent buying a replacement seal for a child's room. Veyra runs it without ceremony, prices it without apology, and keeps a posted sign about her relative that has become a landmark in its own right.

Work on offer here: Dust On The Route (ask Veyra Corsair).
Grit and Supply.hiddenInfo: A Corsair shipment carrying Contair equipment has not arrived, and it held ammunition, medical stock, spare parts and Lunar Gate components on one manifest. Veyra reported it missing and may be carrying a Corsair-side contract complication she has not described to anyone in Dustfall. The Gate Component Cage is the part that matters most: if the missing component is not locally replaceable, the Lunar Gate begins failing and the settlement's argument turns from prices to isolation. The shop also runs a Bent Halo counter for genuinely legitimate parts, a boundary the smugglers observe because losing the supply relationship would cost them more than the deception would gain. Hidden humanitarian cargo, counterfeit goods, Corsair route politics and equipment bound for outer Quilrath buyers all move through the same rear bay, and Veyra prefers not to know which is which until a ledger entry forces her to. Dravon inspection pressure reaches her through intermediaries rather than directly.

Main Supply Floor.description: Crowded aisles of shelving, crates and hanging stock under hard overhead lighting, with a posted sign forbidding Xyren Corsair from inspecting, borrowing, testing, improving or emotionally supporting any merchandise on the property. The aisles are narrow enough that two loaded customers have to negotiate, and the stock runs from domestic seals and heating elements to field kits, tool sets and armour fittings. Dust comes in with every customer and is swept out several times a day. Prices move with supply and are never apologised for. Households, crews and technicians shop the same shelves, and a shortage shows here before it shows anywhere else in Dustfall. Regulars check the shelves before asking, because asking wastes Veyra's time.

Ammunition Counter.description: A reinforced service counter where munitions are sold by type, condition and quantity, with nothing left on open shelf. Everything is behind plate and lock, drawn out on request and checked in front of the buyer, including the converters and adapters that let one household's weapon feed on another's stock. Stock levels here are the town's most honest anxiety indicator. Buyers are ordinary: patrol volunteers, householders, crews heading out, a parent replacing what a training session consumed. During the current shortage the counter is thinner than anyone remembers, and Veyra has started rationing by relationship rather than by credit, which she states openly and argues about daily.

Secondhand Contair Shelves.description: Used consoles, housings, interface strips and control modules of Contair manufacture, most already repaired once by somebody else. The shelves are racked by generation and compatibility, each item tagged by hand with what is known about it and what is not, because Dustfall's infrastructure runs on hardware with no local supplier and a wrong guess strands a household's systems. Buyers test before purchase and Veyra expects them to; a bench and a power feed sit at the end of the aisle for exactly that. The shelves are also where a knowledgeable customer can spot a component whose serial markings have been stripped rather than worn away.

Shipment Ledger Desk.description: Veyra's working desk of manifests, receipts and outstanding deliveries, all of it digital and none of it shown to browsers. The desk sits where she can see the floor, the rear bay and the door at once, backed by the cages and the locked cabinet, and she works it standing more often than sitting. This is where a missing shipment becomes a documented problem instead of a rumour. Credits are the common currency, but barter, sponsorship and personal credit are settled here too, and a household short this month is dealt with privately rather than at the counter. She answers questions about it in order of who is actually owed something, which is not the same order as who is asking loudest.

Locked Medical Cabinet.description: A sealed cabinet behind the counter holding the medicines, sterile stock and treatment consumables that the Frontier Care House cannot obtain elsewhere. It is a heavy unit set into the wall, climate-held and alarmed, with its contents listed only in Veyra's ledger. Access is Veyra's decision alone, and she has refused people with money and released stock to people with none on the same afternoon. Withdrawals move by hand to the Care House rather than by any delivery arrangement, usually carried by whoever is trusted and going that way. Every withdrawal is recorded, because medical supply theft in Dustfall is the kind of act that ends a person's welcome permanently.

Gate Component Cage.description: A caged section for Lunar Gate stabiliser parts, calibration modules and the specific fittings the patched gate consumes faster than it should. The mesh is doubled, the lock is good, and what sits inside is labelled in two hands, Veyra's and Halvora's, because the two of them keep separate counts and compare them. Stock is thin, expensive and watched, and none of it has a local manufacturer, which is the whole difficulty: the technology is not beyond the settlement, the supply chain is. Halvora Orvantis checks it personally whenever a delivery lands, and her face after looking is a settlement-wide signal.

Rear Cargo Bay.description: A high roll-door bay where loads are received, broken down and re-sorted for local carriers. The door faces away from the strip onto hard standing wide enough for a hauler to turn, and the light inside swings between glare and shadow as the door goes up and down through the day. Dust drifts in constantly and is swept out constantly. Incoming freight is divided by cargo type, terrain, current warnings and passenger need, and honest and criminal work pass across the same floor without the floor distinguishing them. Crews wait here rather than on the shop floor, which keeps arguments about delivery condition away from paying customers.

Unclaimed Package Rack.description: Shelving for consignments whose recipients never came, never paid or are no longer alive to collect. The rack is plain salvage, each item tagged with a date and a name, some of the tags faded almost to nothing. Veyra holds them longer than she is obliged to, and refuses to sell off the contents while anyone is still asking after the person. Families come and read the tags, which is not a service she advertises and not one she has ever refused. The rack is quietly one of Dustfall's better sources of missing-person information, since a package with nobody to claim it usually means something happened on a route.

Bent Halo legitimate-parts counter.description: A separate counter where Saevik Ruun's smuggling crew buys components entirely above board, at posted prices, with receipts. It stands apart from the main floor with its own counter and its own queue, and the crew members who use it behave impeccably, which regular customers find funnier than the crew does. The arrangement is public and slightly absurd, and both sides protect it, because losing the supply relationship would cost the Halo more than any deception would gain. Fuel cells, charge modules, sling hardware and structural fittings move across it. Anything the Halo would rather not have on a receipt is bought somewhere else, which is exactly the point.

Black Dust.name: Black Dust
Black Dust.basicInfo: Black Dust is Tessik Luxaryn's low-lit establishment on the settlement's less legible edge, where criminal, mercenary and covert business gets done over a table rather than at gunpoint. The building is old stone and cargo plating with deadened walls and few windows, and the light inside is shaded down to lamp pools at the tables while the hard desert glare stops at the door. Gang negotiations, refugee movement, informants and stolen technology all pass through the same room. It is quietly dangerous because people make dangerous decisions here, not because violence is constant; the room is generally orderly, drinks arrive without commentary, and a dispute that starts inside is expected to finish somewhere else. No crew owns the place and no crew is allowed to behave as though it does, which is the condition on which everyone is served. Ordinary business happens here too, since a smuggler may be the only person able to move medicine and a known killer may run a transport service that completes every contract it takes. Tessik sells introductions rather than loyalty, prices both, and is candid about the difference to anyone who mistakes one for the other.
Black Dust.hiddenInfo: Tessik's value is that he sells introductions rather than loyalty, and he keeps the room functional by making sure no single faction can treat it as theirs. A Dravon contact has a seat here, which the Accord-sympathetic patrons tolerate because knowing where the contact sits is worth more than driving him out. Nyra Sorel's claimed history does not match Ovar Kethrin's missing-person records or Miren Tal's identity files, and at least one of those three accounts is a deliberate construction. False safe-passage offers are sold in this building alongside real ones and are not distinguishable by price. Selka Vaereth negotiates here for the Black Pennant and distrusts Nyra on instinct she has not justified. With the Corsair shipment missing, Tessik or Nyra can supply a route toward the cargo network, and either will attach conditions that only become clear afterwards. Refugees in the quiet corner are not automatically innocent of unrelated conduct, and the staff do not ask.

Main Floor.description: A low room of mismatched tables under shaded lamps, the walls deadened enough that conversations do not carry. The floor is plate laid over plate, the ceiling low enough to keep sound down, and the only bright thing in the room is the serving hatch. Drinks are served without commentary and nobody is greeted by name in earshot of strangers. People come in alone, sit where they can see the door, and wait to be noticed by whoever they came for; others eat a plain meal and leave without speaking to anyone. The staff clear tables, refill water and remember faces without appearing to. The floor is busiest in the hours when the strip has gone quiet, which is deliberate.

Tessik's Booth.description: Tessik Luxaryn's fixed corner, angled so he sees the entrance and the rear passage at once. The booth is built up from salvaged panel with a table that has been resurfaced rather than replaced, and the lamp above it is shaded so that his face is the least well-lit thing in the conversation. He takes meetings in order of usefulness and tells people plainly when their business is not worth his. What he actually sells is introductions, covert routes and information, none of it accompanied by loyalty, and the distinction is stated rather than implied. Regulars know that being invited to sit is a service being priced, not a friendship being offered.

Rear Deal Room.description: A sealed back room with a heavy door and no windows, used when a transaction needs to be finished rather than discussed. It holds one table, hard chairs, a single overhead lamp and a power feed for testing whatever is being sold. Goods are inspected on the table before credits move, and either party can call the deal off up to the moment the transfer completes, which is one of the few house rules Tessik enforces personally. Stolen components, restricted cargo and salvage of uncertain origin all cross the same surface. The room is cleaned thoroughly and often, which regulars have decided not to think about too carefully.

Unmarked Storage.description: Racked crates and cases with no labels, no manifest and no stated owner, held for a fee and a deadline. The racking is welded salvage bolted to the floor, the air is dry and still, and a single strip light runs the length of the ceiling above rows of containers that have been stacked, shifted and restacked for years. Tessik does not open what he stores and does not extend the deadline; the terms are given once, in full, and he repeats them to anyone who tries to talk them down. What sits here ranges from a household's records and salvaged family objects to components nobody wants found in their own building. Unclaimed goods become his, which is stated up front and has never once been renegotiated.

Smuggler Exit.description: A narrow service cut through the rear wall onto a lane the strip lighting does not reach. The cut is just wide enough for a person and a case, with the plating around it reinforced, the floor worn smooth in a single track and the hinges kept quiet by somebody's regular attention. It is used for departing cargo, departing people and departures that need to look like they never happened. Nobody guards it and nobody logs it, which is the arrangement: Tessik keeps the room functional by not being the person who knows who left, and by being able to say so honestly. The lane outside is unlit and open at both ends. The door has been replaced three times and reinforced each time.

Gang Table.description: A long table by the wall where crew business is conducted semi-openly: Jackals, Pennant, Halo and unaffiliated operators, rarely all at once. It is the largest piece of furniture in the building, built from a single salvaged panel on welded legs, and it is never given to ordinary drinkers even when it stands empty. The seating order is its own argument. What crosses it is mostly practical: territory, hauling, protection terms, which crew is flying what and whether a route is worth the fuel. Disputes that start here are expected to finish outside, and the expectation is enforced by the room rather than by staff.

Quiet Refugee Corner.description: A shadowed nook near the rear cut where people who have just left Quilrath sit while somebody negotiates on their behalf. There are benches, a low table and a screen that can be pulled across, and the corner is deliberately positioned so that nobody sitting in it has their back to the room. Water arrives without being ordered. Some occupants are exhausted civilians with children asleep against them, some are fighters, and the staff do not ask which. An outside classification proves nothing here, and neither does an outside warrant. What happens next depends entirely on who agrees to move them and whether that person is telling the truth about where.

Dravon Contact Seat.description: One specific seat, known to the room, where a Dravon-aligned intermediary conducts business without pretending otherwise. It is a single chair at a small table against the wall, unremarkable in itself and left conspicuously empty when its occupant is absent. Nobody acknowledges him and everybody tracks him. Dravon pressure reaches Dustfall through intermediaries, informants and route arrangements rather than through open authority, and this seat is the visible end of that. Tessik permits the arrangement because a visible contact is a manageable one, and has said so to people who objected loudly.

Privacy Booths.description: Screened booths with signal-deadened panelling, rented by the hour for conversations that cannot be overheard. The panelling is genuine current equipment rather than improvised shielding, fitted into frames of salvaged plate, and each booth holds a table and facing benches with a curtain that closes the last gap. The deadening is genuine but bounded, and Tessik makes no promise beyond the equipment's actual capability; the rate and the limits are posted together. Crews, brokers and ordinary households settling something delicate all use them. People still assume more secrecy than the panels provide, which has cost at least two of them badly.

Refit Row.name: Refit Row
Refit Row.basicInfo:
Refit Row is Dustfall's repair, salvage and modification district, anchored by Halvora Orvantis's bench and Korrik Caelthorn's Bolt n Break. It runs as a working lane of open frontage, gantried yards and roofed bays built from cargo modules, alien metal, old stone and reinforced glass, lit by work lamps and cutting light under hard desert daylight, with the dust kept down by hosing that nobody can quite justify. Weapons work, armour refitting, drone repair and salvage identification happen alongside the Iron Jackals' Vossan Yard compound and quieter specialist shops. The technology is not crude: advanced Contair and Starian hardware is opened, tested and rebuilt here by people working around missing parts rather than missing knowledge, and the constraint is always compatibility, cost and what the last shipment actually contained. Households come for domestic systems as often as crews come for weapons, apprentices are taught on the floor, and families live above several of the working yards. It is loud, inventive, indispensable and home to the settlement's least defensible interpretation of safety standards.

Work on offer here: Dustfall — Patch It Before Dark; Trade — Parts That Can Take the Heat (ask Halvora Orvantis).
Refit Row.hiddenInfo: The Row's technical knowledge is its real asset and its real exposure. Halvora can identify Dravon integration hidden inside modified Contair gear, which makes her bench the place where a supply theft turns into a political problem. Sura Venn, working behind the Dead Signal Bay, removes trackers and strips serial markers; she has recently pulled a device that reports to somebody other than Dravon, meaning a second party has learned the same control architecture. She insists she was a technician rather than an enforcer, and refugees point out that the systems she maintained still confined people. Korrik may have bought a component matching the missing Corsair manifest without realising it. The Iron Jackals may be auctioning stolen parts in complete good faith, and Kaedra Vossan's protection of local families is real at the same time as the debts it creates. Iven Torris's finds arrive here mislabelled often enough that Halvora audits everything he brings. Refit Row refers domestic work to Pella Mox and customers to Hana and Velan Pelorr's business, whose home and workshop stand in Dustfall Residential Rows; the Row contains no second Pelorr Stack.

Halvora's Main Bench.description: The district's centre of competence: a long illuminated bench with diagnostic gear, fine tooling and components sorted by a system only Halvora fully understands. The bay around it is clean by Refit Row standards, sealed against blown grit, and quiet enough to hear a fault before seeing it. She takes the work nobody else can do and refuses the work nobody should, and she says which is which in front of the customer. Gate parts, damaged field armour, questionable salvage and household systems all reach this bench, and the queue is ordered by consequence rather than by payment. Apprentices stand at her shoulder and are made to explain what they are looking at. Her verdict on a questionable part is treated in Dustfall as close to proof.

Bolt n Break.description: Korrik Caelthorn's weapons modification shop, where the walls are hung with test pieces and the tolerances are described as guidelines. The shop is a roofed bay open at the front, its benches buried under converters, dampeners, housings and half-finished ideas, and the noise coming out of it is a fair warning of what goes on inside. Custom work is fast, inventive and occasionally alarming, and he argues about the distinction between what can be repaired safely and what can merely be repaired. Customers are told the risk, loudly, and sign nothing. Korrik regards Pella Mox's refusal to modify weapons as a tragic waste of a genuinely good technician.

Salvage Identification Stall.description: An open stall where recovered parts are checked against known designs, markings and failure patterns before anyone pays for them. It is a counter under a shade hood with reference material, a test feed and a set of scales, positioned where the whole lane can watch a verdict being delivered. Sellers bring in wreckage by the crate and leave with a verdict they may not like. A current Dravon mark does not prove who built a thing, and a stripped marking does not prove theft, so the stall works from wear, design and failure rather than from stories. Disputes over identification are common and are settled by test rather than argument.

Drone Repair Cage.description: A meshed enclosure where survey, hauling and observation drones are stripped, repaired and flight-tested without endangering the street. The mesh runs floor to roof on a welded frame, patched where test flights have found the weak panels, and the light inside is flat and bright enough to work a fine joint under. Rotor wash kicks the dust into standing spirals, and anyone standing at the door gets a share of it. Work here is ordinary as often as not: a household's survey unit, a hauler's lifting drone, a shop's stock counter brought in with a seized bearing, an apprentice's first rebuild flown badly and brought back sheepishly. Units brought in with their identifiers removed are worked on at a higher price and a recorded note.

Armor Refit Platform.description: A raised platform with adjustable supports where personal armour is fitted, resized and repaired to actual bodies rather than assumed ones. Customers stand in the supports while plating is checked for balance, clearance and the points where a repair has stiffened something that should flex. Flight clearance and load balance matter more here than appearance, and the technicians will refuse a fit that looks better than it moves. Growing children are brought in for resizing as routinely as crews are refitted after damage. The plating racks are a museum of house patterns cut down and reissued to people with no house left.

Contair Parts Lockers.description: Secured lockers of Contair-manufactured components, sorted by generation and compatibility, since Dustfall's infrastructure runs on hardware that has no local supplier. The lockers are a wall of salvaged cabinets refaced in matching plate, each drawer labelled by hand, standing in the coolest and driest corner the bay can offer. Nothing here is new. Every item carries its known history on a tag, including what it was pulled from and whether it has already been repaired once. Halvora keeps the key list short and the inventory accurate, because a wrong entry here strands somebody's home systems for a month.

Dravon Component Bin.description: A quarantined bin for recovered Dravon hardware awaiting identification, stripping or destruction. It is a heavy open-topped container set apart from the working benches, marked in paint rather than in any official notation, with a lid that is supposed to stay closed. Some of it is ordinary infrastructure; some of it is control equipment nobody wants reconnected. Inferior components turn up hidden inside better housings often enough that anything arriving in good condition is opened before it is believed. The bin is checked by more people than have any business checking it, and Halvora has stopped pretending otherwise.

Test-Fire Barrier.description: A heaped berm of packed rock and salvage plate backing a short firing lane where modified weapons and repaired drives are proved. The berm is rebuilt after anything that takes a serious bite out of it, and the material going into it has come from three different structures that failed somewhere else first. The barrier has absorbed more than its designers intended, and the plate facing it is dished and silvered where it has been struck. Testing is announced by shouting rather than by any system, and the lane is cleared by whoever is nearest and loudest. Apprentices are made to watch a full test before they are allowed to run one. Bystanders stand behind a painted line that has been repainted further back twice.

Mox Patchworks.description: Pella Mox's low-cost domestic systems shop with her family's back rooms behind the counter: household power cells, heaters, water units, doors and child-safe equipment. The front is a plain counter and a wall of tested spares; the workshop behind it smells of hot insulation, and a door at the rear stands open onto rooms where a meal is usually in progress. She refuses weapon work and charges criminals extra when they pretend weapon damage came from a household fault. Most of her trade is collectors, seals and failed heating elements brought in by people who cannot afford to be without them for long. The shop is honest, affordable and permanently busy.

The Dead Signal Bay.description: Sura Venn's concealed tracking-removal and signal-suppression workshop, with a sealed room behind the service bay where she lives. From the lane it reads as a closed service frontage; inside, it is shielded, quiet and equipped to a standard that sits oddly beside the rest of the district. Devices are removed, remote locks disabled and serial markers stripped, with the client present and told what is being taken out of them or their equipment. She insists she was a technician rather than an enforcer, and refugees point out that the systems she maintained still confined people. Tessik sends clients here without using her name, and Halvora audits every job that leaves the bay.

Vossan Yard.description: The Iron Jackals' layered salvage compound: a walled, gantried yard that is simultaneously a business, a neighbourhood and a home. The wall is patchwork hull plate and structural offcuts, the gantries carry cutting light over stacked wreckage, and cargo homes rise along the inner face with laundry lines and painted doors. Kaedra Vossan runs processing, auctions and heavy hauling from here, along with protection arrangements that are genuinely protective and genuinely expensive. The Jackals are embedded residents rather than outside raiders, which is why a neighbour can be shielded and indebted by the same arrangement. Work runs in shifts, children cut through the yard on their way to lessons, and meals come out of the compound kitchen at fixed hours. Families live above the working floor.

Main Salvage Floor.description: The open working floor where wreckage is cut down, sorted and graded under salvage gantries. Cutting light throws hard shadows across stacked hulls and stripped housings, and the noise is constant enough that people speak in the gaps rather than over it. The ground is compacted metal dust that turns to a fine grey slick when anyone hoses it. Jackals work it in shifts, sorting by material, by compatibility and by what Halvora's stall is likely to certify, with apprentices learning cuts on the least valuable pieces. Protective gear is worn properly here, which is not universally true of Refit Row. A hauler arriving at an odd hour is the compound's most reliable sign that something has happened on a route.

Jackal Auction Rail.description: A railed lane where graded salvage is called and sold to Dustfall's technicians, crews and households. Lots are laid out along the rail under shade sheet, tagged by grade, and walked by buyers before the calling starts, with a power feed at one end for anyone who insists on testing before bidding. Bidding is fast, loud and largely honest, settled in credits or against standing accounts, and the occasional lot goes to a household at a price everyone present understands to be a favour. The crowd is half business and half entertainment, and the running commentary from the rail is part of what people come for. It is also where stolen components can enter local circulation without a single person in the chain knowing they are handling someone else's manifest.

Messa's Kitchen.description: Messa Taar's compound kitchen, feeding Jackals, their families and anyone she has decided is owed a meal. It is a long room of well-used cooking equipment, preservation units and a serving counter, opening onto tables that fill and empty through the day, and it is the warmest and least dusty space in the yard. Her informal food and shelter agreement with the Nhalor household runs out of this room, carried across by whoever is going that way. Children are fed first, argued with, and sent out again. She also works communal sessions at the Dustfall Meal Yard, and refuses to let either obligation swallow the other.

Ralven's Ledger Room.description: Ralven Nox's accounts room, where protection payments, salvage shares and outstanding debts are tracked with uncomfortable precision. It is a small sealed room off the working floor, quiet by design, with a desk, a secure terminal and a chair for whoever has been asked to come in and explain themselves. He trades debt information with Tessik Luxaryn while withholding names, a distinction he considers principled. Households come here to renegotiate rather than to default, and he is more willing to restructure than his reputation suggests. The room's numbers are the Jackals' real weapon and everyone in the yard knows it.

Rooftop Lookout Walk.description: A railed walkway across the compound roofs with sightlines over Refit Row and out toward the perimeter. It is welded grating and salvaged rail bolted across module tops, with a shade panel at one end that is always occupied and a set of optics clamped to the rail beside it. It is a watch post, a smoking spot and where arguments go to be had privately. Off-shift Jackals sit along it through the cooler hours, children are chased off it and come back, and someone is always leaning out to shout something down into the yard. From up here the whole district reads as roofs, gantries and collector tanks. In the evening the dust turns the light orange and half the yard ends up leaning on the rail.

Orenik's Training Corner.description: A matted corner where Orenik Sol drills younger Jackals and neighbourhood kids in flight control, falls and basic equipment safety. The mats are salvaged padding, relaid often, under a shade frame that keeps the worst of the daylight off, with a rack of practice equipment against the wall and a water container that is refilled by whoever empties it. Sessions run in the cool hours and anyone's child can join, which is how half the district's parents know him. He works beside Draxen Sol during emergencies and argues with him afterwards about method. Nothing taught here is framed as preparation for gang work, which is a line he defends loudly and in front of the parents.

Family Cargo Homes.description: Stacked cargo modules converted into households, personalised with paint, fabric, tools and salvaged fittings. Access runs by external stair and short flights between roofs, doors carry hand-painted numbers and the odd cut-down house mark, and every unit has a collector on top and a seal somebody is arguing about. Children, elders and off-shift workers live here inside a compound that is also a criminal enterprise. Evenings are ordinary: meals, lessons finished at kitchen tables, somebody's music through a thin wall. Laundry lines cross above a yard where stolen goods are graded, and both facts are simply true at once.

Locked Component Cage.description: The compound's secured cage for high-value salvage held back from open auction: control modules, powered assemblies, anything with markings worth examining. The cage is doubled mesh on a welded frame inside the working floor, lit separately, with its contents logged in Ralven's ledger rather than on any public list. Access runs through Kaedra and Ralven together, and neither will open it alone even when it would be quicker. Items sit here while somebody works out where they came from, who might recognise them and what selling them would start. What sits in here longest is usually what nobody has yet decided how to sell safely.

South Scrapwall Court.description: A courtyard against the compound's scrap wall where hauled loads are staged and neighbours come to negotiate protection terms. It is open ground with a shade frame, a weighbridge plate set into the surface and benches along one side where people wait their turn. The wall is a patchwork of hull plate and structural offcuts, welded by three generations of different hands. Conversations here are conducted in the open and in front of witnesses, which suits both sides: the Jackals want their terms heard, and the households want their agreement remembered. It is the compound's public face and deliberately less guarded than it looks.

Dustfall Perimeter.name: Dustfall Perimeter
Dustfall Perimeter.basicInfo:
The Perimeter is Dustfall's immediate defensive edge: beacon lines, warning markers, barrier controls and a volunteer patrol yard that Draxen Sol organises without holding any rank. It is the most exposed ground in the settlement, open desert scrub and broken pale rock running out toward the corridor, with the wind carrying grit across everything and nothing overhead but hard daylight and, at night, the beacons. Structures here are welded salvage, old stone footings and cargo modules braced against the weather, lit by work lamps and strobes rather than by anything decorative. The Last Line Company's fortified barracks sits against it, and refugees arriving on foot come up the approach lane. Nothing here is a wall: the edge works through observation, warning and the speed with which volunteers can be raised, and town defence stays voluntary until danger reaches the street. Dustfall claims no corridor territory beyond its own edge, recognises no outside warrant automatically, and keeps water and shade at the head of the lane because people arrive needing both. It is exposed, watchful and improvised out of whatever the settlement could weld together.

Work on offer here: Dustfall — The Contract Tavra Dropped (ask Tavra Korrin).
Dustfall Perimeter.hiddenInfo: Nothing here is a wall, and everyone defending it knows that. The perimeter works through observation, warning and the speed with which volunteers can be raised, not through fortification, and it claims no corridor territory beyond the settlement's own edge. Draxen has confirmed that the missing Corsair shipment was taken by an organised interception rather than lost to route conditions, which changes the question from recovery to who supplied the intelligence. Tavra Korrin's company is reliable, expensive and willing to break a contract when the work becomes indefensible — she recently abandoned an escort after learning the client intended to raid refugee housing, and the client has gone to the Claimants instead. That decision is still generating enemies. Bent Halo crews cross the line here on smuggler departures under an understanding nobody has written down. The Captured Equipment Rack holds Dravon hardware whose presence Dustfall has never formally explained, and Iven Torris keeps adding to it from checkpoint shells he should probably leave alone.

Northwatch Platform.description: A raised salvaged-steel platform facing the northern approach, fitted with optics and a warning horn. The structure is braced against the wind and reached by a welded stair, with a shade hood over the standing position and a bench that is too short for comfort on purpose. Two volunteers stand it in rotation, longer in bad dust, and the shift is passed over with a spoken handover rather than any log. From up here the route toward Quilrath is a smear of broken mesas, and everything moving on it has to be judged before it arrives: a carrier, a family on foot, a crew coming back early, a patrol that has no business this far south. Most of what is sighted turns out to be ordinary, which is the part newcomers find hardest to learn.

Perimeter Beacon Line.description: A strung line of dust-scored beacon towers marking where Dustfall considers itself to begin. The towers are mismatched, some of them old route infrastructure reused, some welded up locally, each with its own history of repair painted or scratched onto the base. Half of them work at any given time and the settlement argues about funding the rest, which is a maintenance and cost argument rather than a technical one. Their real function is social: crossing the beacons means local custom now applies to the traveller. Volunteers walk the line to check power feeds, children are told not to go past it, and crews use the working towers to fix their line in poor visibility.

Volunteer Patrol Yard.description: An open yard of parked transports, equipment crates and a duty board where Draxen Sol assigns patrols to people who show up. The ground is hard standing swept clear of drift, the crates are stacked to break the wind, and a single shade frame covers the board and the water. There is no roster, no pay and no rank; people arrive, put their names up and are given something to do or sent home. Shifts are worked around other jobs, and several of the regulars bring children who sit in the shade with lesson work. Who turns out in a given week is one of the more accurate measures of what Dustfall currently believes about its own danger.

Emergency Barrier Controls.description: A hardened console operating the movable barriers and lane blocks that can close the settlement's ground approaches. It sits in a squat plated housing with a lid that has to be unlatched by hand, positioned so that whoever uses it is standing in plain view of the yard. Using it is a settlement-level decision that nobody has the authority to make alone, which has never fully been resolved; in a genuine townwide emergency, affected households, businesses and crews can authorise temporary delegates whose mandate expires with the incident. The panel is tested monthly and the test is the loudest scheduled event in Dustfall.

Flight Warning Markers.description: Worn aerial markers and strobes indicating where approach under flight is expected, and where it will be treated as hostile. They are mounted high on braced poles and on the tops of structures, their paint scoured back by wind-driven dust and repainted in whatever was available. Starian flight is ordinary here, so the markers are about intention rather than capability: they tell an arriving flier where to be seen coming in and where not to be. Crews teach the pattern to newer members before a first approach, and parents teach it to children along with landing distances. Fresh scoring on several of them records arguments that were settled before anyone reached the ground.

Refugee Approach Lane.description: A marked ground lane for people arriving on foot, exhausted, carrying children or unable to fly the last distance. It is a cleared run of hard ground edged with painted stone and low markers, wide enough for a group, with shade frames set along it at intervals. Water and shade are kept at the head of it, and a first container is not charged for. Arrivals are not automatically trusted and are not automatically returned; an outside classification proves nothing and neither does a warrant, so what happens next is worked out by the people present. Volunteers meet arrivals here rather than at the barrier, because the difference between the two has consequences people remember for years.

Captured Equipment Rack.description: Racked gear taken from raiders, abandoned patrols and stripped checkpoints: restraints, optics, inspection hardware, the occasional Dravon housing. The rack stands in the open at the edge of the yard under a shade sheet, each item tagged with where it came from in whatever hand did the tagging. Some of it is usable, some is evidence, and nobody has agreed which is which. Technicians come out from Refit Row to look at anything with control architecture in it, and more than one item has been identified as ordinary infrastructure with a current mark that proves nothing about its builder. Draxen keeps it visible on purpose.

Road Condition Board.description: A weather-sealed display of current route warnings: dust conditions, sightings, closures, which crews came back and which have not. It is mounted where the yard and the lane both see it, glazed in reinforced panel against the grit, with a stylus on a cord that has been replaced more often than the board. Entries are attributed and dated, because an old sighting passed off as current gets people killed. The shared route is not regularly patrolled, so what the board holds is intermittent and contradictory by nature, and readers are expected to weigh it rather than trust it. Departing crews read it without being asked to.

Torris Salvage Camp.description: Iven Torris's temporary camp beside a stripped checkpoint shell: a shelter, a sorting tarp and whatever he has dragged out of the ground this month. The shell beside it is a hollow of plating and collapsed footings with its markings still legible, which tells nobody anything reliable about who built it. The camp has been temporary for a long time and shows it, with a cooking rig, a water container and a sleeping space walled off by stacked finds. He can sense powered components through debris and has poor judgement about whether they should be removed. He owes Kaedra Vossan first choice of everything he finds.

Last Line Barracks.description: The Last Line Company's fortified compound: part contract base, part home, built into the perimeter's strongest existing structure. Old stone footings and heavy plating carry newer cargo modules and a sealed roof, and the whole thing is maintained to a standard the rest of the perimeter finds slightly pointed. Tavra Korrin's crew is respected, costly and known to walk away from indefensible work, which makes the compound both trusted and resented depending on who was refused. Inside, the noise is domestic as often as operational: meals, arguments about maintenance shifts, somebody's child underfoot in a corridor. Families visit, children are fed here, and the contract table sits three rooms from the kitchen.

Contract Table.description: The company's negotiating table, where terms, refusals and conditions are set out in front of the client rather than behind them. It is a plain heavy surface in a room with good light and no comfortable chairs, with the route deck through one door and the equipment wall through another so that a client can see what they are hiring. Tavra states what the crew will not do before discussing price, and a Dravon-backed contract is not automatically recognised at this table. Terms are settled in credits, sponsorship or practical obligation, and the refusals are written down alongside the acceptances. Clients who object to the conditions are welcome to hire the Claimants, and are told so.

Equipment Wall.description: A racked wall of company kit maintained to a standard the rest of Dustfall finds slightly excessive: weapons, armour, breaching gear, field medical packs. The rack is purpose-built rather than salvaged, lit properly, with each position labelled and a working surface below it for strip-downs. Everything is signed out and signed back, and a member who returns something dirty hears about it from whoever inherits it next. Patched plates and repaired housings sit beside newer stock, since the company's advantage is maintenance rather than supply. Maintenance shifts are shared, including by the people who complain hardest about them.

Shared Kitchen.description: The barracks kitchen, where Brask Hollan cooks for the company and anybody a member has brought home. It is a wide room of well-used equipment and long tables, the warmest space in the compound, with a preservation store off one side and the coffee-and-brew end permanently occupied. Meals run at fixed hours and are kept back for anyone still working. It is the compound's actual social centre and the reason recruits stay: people eat together, argue about repairs, teach each other things and let visiting families take the good seats. Arguments about a contract tend to reach their honest version here rather than at the table.

Maela's Treatment Room.description: Maela Drin's clinical room inside the barracks: examination support, clean storage and a recovery corner, maintained better than most of the compound. The lighting is good, the surfaces are properly sealed against dust, and the equipment is current work kept in order rather than improvised. She treats company wounds and, quietly, civilians the Care House cannot reach in time, with stabilisation coming first and referral discussed afterwards according to what is actually available. Consent is asked for and explained, and a person who brought a patient in does not thereby speak for them. Her supplies run through the same shortage as everyone else's.

Joric's Route Deck.description: Joric Pell's planning deck of route overlays, timing notes and accumulated sightings, all of it dated and sourced. The overlays are projected and annotated over a wide working surface, with the older paper-and-plate material he refuses to discard racked along the wall behind. He builds escort plans around what is actually known rather than what would be convenient, and marks the gaps as gaps: the shared route is not regularly patrolled, so a quiet week proves nothing. Crews are walked through the plan before departure and are expected to argue with it. Draxen consults him before any coordinated perimeter response.

Brask's Heavy Bay.description: A high bay for the company's heavy transport, support weapons and lifting gear, with Brask Hollan usually underneath something. The roller door opens onto the perimeter side, the floor is stained dark with years of spilled coolant, and the lifting frames overhead are rated, inspected and argued about. He handles transport and heavy support for the Frontier Care House when they need a patient moved, which he treats as part of the job rather than as a favour. Vehicles come back damaged and go out repaired, and he narrates the repair to anyone who lingers. The bay smells of coolant and, on good days, of whatever he has left cooking next door.

Tavra's Office.description: A small hard room where Tavra Korrin keeps contracts, refusals and the company's record of who it has disappointed. There is a desk, a secure terminal, two chairs and nothing on the walls, and the door shuts properly, which is rarer in the compound than it sounds. She reviews every job against the line she will not cross, and writes down why when she breaks one. The record is available to clients who ask, which is the point of keeping it. She holds no authority in Dustfall beyond her own company and says so whenever anyone tries to give her some. That written record is the reason clients trust her and the reason some of them hate her.

Sleeping Quarters.description: Partitioned crew quarters with personal strips, repaired lockers and blackout curtains for people who work rotating hours. The partitions are salvaged panel, each bay personalised with paint, fabric, family objects and whatever house fragment the occupant still keeps, and the air handling is maintained properly because the alternative is dust in the bedding. Quiet periods are enforced by the crew rather than by rule, which works until it does not. Between contracts the room is ordinary: letters written, equipment cleaned on a bunk, somebody reading aloud to nobody in particular, an argument about whose turn it is to reseal the door. Somebody is always asleep at an inconvenient time, and somebody is always resenting it.

Family Visitor Bunks.description: A separate bunk room for partners, children and relatives staying while a member is on contract or recovering. It is plainer than the crew quarters and better sealed, with bunks, storage, a table under a good lamp and a strip of wall where visiting children's drawings accumulate and are not taken down. It is deliberately outside the working areas, so nobody staying here has to walk past the equipment wall to reach a meal. Visits run long when a contract does, and lesson work gets done at the table while somebody's parent is away. The company treats the room as proof that mercenary work here is a job rather than a life sentence, and the argument mostly holds.

Lunar Gate Yard.name: Lunar Gate Yard
Lunar Gate Yard.basicInfo: The Lunar Gate Yard holds Dustfall's connection to the wider world: a patched, dust-scored gate with confirmed links to Relstaris, Ignivex and Helvyra. The yard around it is open plated ground bounded by salvaged structures and old stone footings, scoured by wind off the desert, with the gate's own light washing across everything when it cycles and hard daylight doing the rest when it does not. It works intermittently and is kept running by local improvisation rather than by any operator: Contair maintains no permanent presence, no one person is the official gatekeeper, and repair is a standing negotiation between local expertise, rare contracted visits and whatever components can be obtained. The gate moves travellers with personal effects and bounded accompanied consignments; ordinary commercial stock remains logistics traffic handled elsewhere, and the handling strip beside the platform does not change that. Nobody checks documents, which arrivals notice immediately. Arrivals, departures and the settlement's quiet anxiety about isolation all collect on its platforms, along with people waiting on somebody who was due back and has not come through yet.
Lunar Gate Yard.hiddenInfo: Contair maintains no permanent presence here and no one person is the official gatekeeper, which means gate repair is a standing negotiation between Halvora Orvantis's expertise, Tiva Nhalor's smaller work, Sura Venn's tracking knowledge, rare contracted technicians and whatever components Veyra Corsair can obtain. The missing Corsair shipment included gate components, and if the failed part is not locally replaceable the gate will begin degrading in a way nobody here can arrest. That raises the question no one calls a vote: whether Dustfall should deliberately close the gate for a period under Dravon pressure, isolating itself to stay unmonitored. Respected locals, gangs, households and crews would all have to live with the decision and none of them can make it. The Unregistered Arrival Bench exists because people arrive who cannot be recorded anywhere, and the settlement has chosen not to build a process that would make them recordable. The Cargo Transfer Strip handles luggage, handoffs and mode transfers only; it establishes no bulk-freight Gate service, and attempts to treat it as one are refused.

Main Lunar Gate.description: The gate structure itself, its plating scoured pale by decades of wind-driven dust and patched in a dozen visibly different materials. It stands over the yard with the mismatched repairs plainly legible: alien metal against salvaged plate against something cut from an entirely different machine, each seam the record of a different technician and a different shortage. When it cycles, the light changes across the whole yard, the air moves, and everybody on the platform stops talking for a moment without meaning to. Between cycles it is simply a large old structure people walk past on their way somewhere else. When it does not cycle, people stand and look at it as though that has ever helped.

Patched Stabilizer Ring.description: The stabiliser assembly, rebuilt in sections by successive technicians with whatever was compatible at the time. The ring carries its own history in materials and finish, and the access walkway around it is worn smooth on the side people actually use. Its tolerances are documented only in Halvora's head and one shared file, which is a known and unresolved problem that gets raised whenever she is ill. Checks are done by hand and by feel as much as by instrument, because the assembly no longer matches anything a manual would describe. A fault here is the difference between an intermittent gate and no gate, which is why the ring is checked before every scheduled cycle.

Arrival Platform.description: A broad plated platform where travellers step through and take their first look at Dustfall, usually while recalibrating their expectations. It is open to the sky, swept daily and never clean, with benches along one edge and a water point that is not charged for. Personal effects and bounded accompanied consignments come through with them, carried or slung rather than handled by any service. Arrivals range from crews returning to families come to collect somebody to travellers who intended to stay one night. Nobody checks documents, and the absence of a checkpoint is the first thing most arrivals notice.

Local Repair Console.description: A modified Contair console, rehoused twice, from which the gate's cycles, faults and improvised workarounds are managed. The housing is welded plate with the original panel set into it at a slightly wrong angle, and the display carries local annotations stuck to its frame in three different hands. Its interface is half original and half locally written, and the locally written half is documented nowhere except in use. Whoever is working it draws a small audience whenever the gate is behaving badly. Anyone competent to use it is recognised in Dustfall as holding a kind of standing, without that ever being made official.

Unregistered Arrival Bench.description: A plain bench off the platform for people who arrive without documentation, without a destination or without anyone expecting them. It is welded salvage under a shade panel, set far enough from the platform edge to be out of the traffic and close enough to be seen from it. There is water and there is shade and there is no process; the settlement has chosen not to build one that would make these arrivals recordable. People sit here with children asleep across their knees, or alone with a single bag, sometimes for hours. Volunteers drift over when someone has been sitting there too long, which is as formal as the arrangement gets.

Cargo Transfer Strip.description: A handling strip beside the platform for luggage, inspection, secure handoff and transfers between transport modes. It is a run of hard standing with sling frames, a weighing plate and shade enough for people to wait under while a handover is worked out, with the dust swept off it several times a day because a load set down in drift comes up filthy. Carriers meet passengers here and loads change hands under the strip lighting, with terms agreed face to face and condition checked before anything is signed off. A traveller with a mobility aid or an accompanied consignment is handled here rather than on the platform. It is not a freight gate service and Dustfall's operators enforce that distinction more strictly than any regulation would.

Emergency Shutdown Lever.description: A physical isolation lever in a marked housing, deliberately mechanical, deliberately ugly and deliberately reachable. The housing is painted a colour nothing else in the yard is painted, mounted at a height a child could reach and fitted with a cover that takes two hands and no tools. It exists because a console can fail in ways a lever cannot, and because the people who built it did not trust any single operator to be present when it mattered. It is tested by inspection rather than by use, and the inspection is one of the few pieces of gate maintenance nobody argues about funding. Pulling it has consequences for everyone mid-transit, which is painted on the housing in three languages.

Old Contair Service Alcove.description: A disused service alcove from when Contair technicians visited regularly, still fitted with mounting points and a dead diagnostic feed. It is a recess in the yard's old stonework, roofed and shaded, noticeably cooler than anywhere else out here, with brackets on the walls holding nothing and a bench surface long since repurposed for whatever needed putting down. It is now storage, shelter and an occasional meeting spot, and in the worst of the daylight it fills with people who have twenty minutes to spare and no better idea. Children treat it as a place to hide. The faded service schedule on the wall lists visits that stopped long before most current residents arrived.

Gate Component Lockup.description: A secured store for the stabiliser parts and calibration modules the gate consumes, holding far less than anyone is comfortable with. It is a plated room with a good lock, shelved and labelled, its contents counted against a list that several people keep independently because nobody entirely trusts a single count. Withdrawals are recorded and argued over, and a part taken out for a repair that then fails becomes a settlement argument rather than a technical one. None of this hardware has a local manufacturer. During the current shortage the lockup has become the most closely watched cupboard in the settlement.

Dustfall Residential Rows.name: Dustfall Residential Rows
Dustfall Residential Rows.basicInfo:
The Residential Rows are where Dustfall actually lives: converted cargo homes, shared kitchen courts, rooftop water collectors and a children's flight yard, plus the compounds of households and houses that failed elsewhere. Modules are stacked several high and joined by external stairs, bridges and short flights between roofs, built from cargo shells, alien metal, old stone and reinforced glass, sealed and resealed against a dust that gets into everything. The light is hard overhead and the lanes hold shade, so life moves outdoors in the cooler hours and indoors in the middle of the day. The Nhalor refugee shelter, the Black Pennant's Old Banner Hall, Marrik Hall's training business and the Pelorr family's vertical workshop all stand within it. Ordinary life runs through all of it: cooperative lessons, shared childcare across households whose adults work dangerous jobs, meals cooked in common, homes improved a panel at a time, arguments over the last compatible power cell. Every roof carries its own collector and its own maintenance dispute. It is worn, crowded, heavily personalised and fiercely protective, and the household marks on the doors are address rather than authority.

Work on offer here: Dustfall — Marrik's Invitation (ask Sev Marrik); Corridor — The Name on the Wrong List (ask Ovar Kethrin).
Dustfall Residential Rows.hiddenInfo: This district is what the perimeter is actually defending, and several of the organisations sheltering here are also recruiting here. The Black Pennant preserves House Vaereth identity and trains displaced youth in Old Banner Hall while its Locked Recruitment Chamber records commitments that are hard to withdraw from; a young survivor asking to leave is currently testing whether Rhex Vaereth sees betrayal faster than Selka sees the risk of recreating Dravon control.
