A locker found short during a check is a serious matter in this district, treated as a failure of the house rather than of an individual.

Fortified Neighborhood Corridors.description: Reinforced corridors threading through the district's built fabric, letting crews and residents move under cover between gates, depots and shelters. They carry the daily traffic of the Wallworks. The corridors run broad enough for two crews to pass with a stretcher between them, roofed, reinforced and lined with the district's emblems and posted guidance. Daily traffic moves through them constantly: shift changes, deliveries, families taking a covered route between errands. They are swept and inspected the way a wall is inspected, because that is what they are. Thermal shutters punctuate them at intervals, and the muted red lighting never quite goes out.

Defender Memorial Stones.description: Set memorial stones naming defenders who died holding breach points, placed along the corridors where people pass them daily rather than in a dedicated hall. Names are added with little ceremony. The stones are set flush into the corridor walls at head height, cut plainly with names and nothing else, sited where the district's daily traffic passes them rather than in any dedicated hall. New names are added by the same crews who repair the gates. The house's philosophy is that the wall remembers who stood there, and these stones are how the wall does it. Responders touch or pass them without comment, and the habit is taught to new crews by example.

Maedra’s Gate Workshop.description: Maedra Caldris's design workshop, where firebreak gate mechanisms are drafted, modelled and tested against local conditions. Her work is deliberately not Contair-trained. The workshop is part drafting room and part test floor, drawings pinned in layers, component stock racked by size, and a rig built into the far wall where mechanisms are cycled against local conditions until they fail. Maedra Caldris works late and alone by preference. Her gates are heavier and rougher than Contair designs and she says so first, before anyone else gets the chance. Prototype gate sections stand along one wall in various states of failure, kept as evidence of what she has already ruled out.

The Armor Racks.description: Racks of maintained defensive gear standing ready near the depots and halls, each set marked with the Caldris emblem. Crews draw from them at the start of a shift. They stand in the open rather than in a store, sets hung by size with maintenance benches alongside and a log for damage and repair kept where anyone drawing gear can read it. Ignivex's standardized sets are fitted, treated and maintained locally, and a piece that comes back damaged is on a bench before the responder who wore it has finished reporting. Armor here is repaired and reissued rather than retired, and a well-scarred set is considered better than a new one.

Meravil Ash Hall.name: Meravil Ash Hall
Meravil Ash Hall.basicInfo:
Meravil Ash Hall is House Meravil's district and Ignivex's civic-administrative quarter, handling casualty records, continuity planning, ration forecasting and political meetings. Ash-gray stone, black glass, muted bronze and pale ember lighting give it a cooler, more controlled feel than the Volen and Caldris districts, helped by cooling channels that make it easier on outsiders. The district is built low and screened, lit in a pale ember light that never reaches the brightness of a Volen plaza, and its cooling channels give a relief outsiders notice within a few steps. Its ordinary business is paperwork with consequences: casualty records consulted daily by families searching for a name, continuity offices planning what still runs after a bad week, ration and displacement scenarios modelled against damage reports, archive vaults holding proceedings sent on from across the city. The thin red ring and pale ash spiral of the Meravil emblem mark record halls, archive doors and administrative seals, while public Volen emblems still stand in the district's city-facing spaces. The district does not feel cowardly; it feels exhausted, and the suspicion attached to it is about its politics and its Dravon ties rather than its comfort. Where Volen districts shout and Caldris districts brace, Meravil calculates.

Work on offer here: Ignivex — Rows After the Raid (ask Ilvara Meravil).
Meravil Ash Hall.hiddenInfo: The district does not feel cowardly; it feels exhausted. House Meravil's surrender-leaning politics come from casualty lists, grieving families, damaged homes, civilian exhaustion and ration forecasts rather than from treachery by default — and the house is not a monolith. Seralyne Meravil leads it as a mother afraid resistance will kill her child. Vennik Meravil operates politically. Auralis Meravil dissents against surrender from inside the house, which makes the Controlled Meeting Rooms genuinely contested ground rather than a rubber stamp. Caevan Meravil's marriage to Nyssara Dravon makes the whole district a living pressure point, and suspicion in Ignivex attaches to exactly that tie and to Meravil's politics — not to the district's physical comfort, whatever people say in the Emberward. Ilvara Meravil keeps the casualty records and the civic continuity function, so families searching for a name come here, and the numbers they are given become the argument.

Meravil Family Hall.description: The house's principal hall in ash-gray stone and black glass, where Seralyne Meravil receives and the family's formal business is conducted. Public Volen emblems still appear in its city-facing spaces. The hall is broad and low, its ash-gray walls broken by panels of black glass, seating arranged for conversation rather than for audience and no raised position anywhere in the room. Seralyne receives here and is careful in public. Staff move quietly out of habit, and guests are offered water and cooled seating before anybody asks what they have come about. The room is deliberately calm, and the calm is doing considerable work for a family under this much strain.

Casualty Record Chambers.description: Chambers holding Ignivex's casualty records, maintained under Ilvara Meravil's authority and consulted daily. Families come to search for a name. The chambers are lined with record cases in muted bronze, palely lit and kept cool, reading tables set apart from one another so that nobody searching has to do it beside a stranger. Requests are made at a counter and fetched rather than browsed. Ilvara Meravil's people keep the ordering exact, because the only thing worse than a family finding a name is a family being told to come back tomorrow. Staff have learned to hand over a record and then simply wait, because there is nothing useful to say in the interval that follows.

Civic Continuity Offices.description: Offices planning for the city's continued function through siege, raid and loss — services, staffing, replacement and succession of civic roles. The work is unglamorous and relentless. The offices are plain working rooms with wall boards tracking services, staffing and the succession of civic roles, and they are busiest in the days after a raid rather than during one. Officers work in pairs and check each other's assumptions out loud. The planning is deliberately unheroic, and the phrase these rooms use is not victory but what still runs. Continuity officers think in terms of what still runs after a bad week, which colours how they hear every Volen speech.

Ration And Displacement Planning Rooms.description: Planning rooms where ration forecasts and displacement scenarios are modelled against damage and population figures. Projections cover the walls in pale ember light. The rooms are large, screened and quiet, with working tables and stacks of damage reports cross-checked against housing records before anything is modelled at all. Planners argue over assumptions at length and in detail, and treat an unexamined assumption as worse than a bad one. Volen visitors read the same figures and reach different conclusions from them, and the planners have stopped expecting that to change. These numbers are the raw material of the surrender argument, which is why people from outside the house ask to see them and are rarely refused.

Quiet Negotiation Salons.description: Cooled salons furnished for small, careful conversations that are not meetings of record. Talks happen here that could not happen in the Emberward. The salons are small cooled rooms with soft seating and screened doors, arranged so that two or three people can talk without any of them facing an audience. Water and food arrive without being asked for. Nothing said here is minuted, which is what the rooms are for, and everyone who uses them understands that the absence of a record protects both sides of a conversation equally. The comfort is calculated hospitality — an outsider relaxing in a Meravil salon is a person slightly easier to read.

Heat-Moderated Interior Courtyards.description: Interior courts served by the district's cooling channels, planted and shaded, noticeably kinder than core Volen areas. Staff take meals in them. The courts are enclosed and planted, with low walls to sit on and shade across most of the paving, and the air in them is the kindest in the district. Clerks, planners and record staff take their meals out here in shifts, and families waiting on a record are directed to them rather than left standing in a corridor. The planting is kept by the house's own staff and is the one thing in the district nobody has ever argued about. Visitors from other districts enjoy the relief and then feel obliged to make a joke about it, which residents have heard many times.

Archive Vaults.description: The city's archive vaults, holding records, proceedings and rulings sent on from across Ignivex including the Smoke Court's. Access is controlled and logged. The vaults are sealed rooms behind bronze-fitted doors, cooler and drier than anywhere else in the district, cases stacked floor to ceiling with narrow aisles between them. Nothing leaves without a signature and a stated reason. Clerks retrieve on request while the requester waits outside, and the waiting is where most people first understand how much of this city is written down in here. The vaults are the reason people say the house that counts the dead also holds everything anyone has ever said under pressure.

Memorial Record Walls.description: Walls carrying the recorded names of the city's losses, thin red ring motifs marking the entries by year. Families come to stand rather than to search. The hall exists for nothing else: ash-gray stone faced smooth, the names cut in rather than posted, lit palely and cooled like the record chambers, with no seating, no attendant and no ceremony attached to coming. Families arrive and stand, sometimes for a long time, and the district's staff have learned to take the long way round rather than pass behind them. The walls have been extended more than once, and the joins are visible enough that people count them.

Controlled Meeting Rooms.description: Formal meeting rooms for political business, sealed and minuted, where the surrender question is argued inside the house and with the city. Auralis Meravil dissents in these rooms. The rooms are sealed and plain, a table, a clerk's position and doors that close properly, and everything said in them is minuted as a matter of course. Sessions are scheduled and run long. Auralis Meravil dissents against surrender from inside her own house in these rooms, which is tolerated, recorded, and quietly used by both sides of the wider argument as evidence that House Meravil is not a monolith. Sessions run long, and the arguments made here are calculated rather than shouted.

Intermediary Corridors.description: Discreet corridors used by political intermediaries moving between salons, meeting rooms and the family hall without crossing public space. Traffic through them is quiet and constant. They are narrow, dim and unmarked, finished plainly and lit only enough to walk by, turning often enough that a corridor is never visible along its whole length, and no door along any of them cannot be closed. Ordinary staff use them for ordinary errands as well, which is the cover that makes them usable at all. Nobody keeps a record of who passes through. Being seen entering one is information in itself, which is why some people take the long way instead.

Ilvara’s Record Desk.description: Ilvara Meravil's own desk, where casualty records and civic continuity work meet in one set of ledgers. She works methodically and late. The desk is heavy and bronze-fitted, covered in open ledgers kept in an order only she maintains, set where she can see both the chamber doors and the people waiting at them. Casualty records and continuity work meet on the same surface because to her they are one piece of work. She does not hate House Volen; she hates funerals becoming ordinary, and she says so to anyone who asks her which side she is on. People who come expecting a clerk find someone who can recite what the city has lost from memory, and would rather not have to.

The Ash Spiral Court.description: The district's central court, its floor laid in an ash-gray spiral with thin red rings worked through it, cooled and unhurried. Everything in Meravil Ash Hall opens off it. It is broad and open, wide enough that crossing it takes a moment, and the pale ember light falls evenly over every part of the pattern. Staff, families and visitors all cross it, and the district's halls and offices open off it on every side. There is nothing posted on its walls and nowhere provided to sit down, and both of those are decisions. Crossing it, people lower their voices without being asked, which is the clearest statement the district makes about itself.

The Red Forges.name: The Red Forges
The Red Forges.basicInfo:
The Red Forges is Ignivex's forge and craft district, and it is culturally prestigious rather than merely industrial. Metalwork houses, thermal crafting lines and heat-channel machinery run advanced thermal engineering at district scale, turning out shaped weapons, treated armor and fine craft work. The district is built around its heat rather than merely subjected to it: heat-channel machinery runs beneath and through the workshops, thermal crafting lines hold temperatures no hand can judge, and the metalwork houses stand tall-roofed under extraction hoods and shielding. Basalt-black walls carry copper-bronze bracing, the light is the working light of open metal, and the noise is constant and layered. An ordinary day is masters, journeymen and apprentices sharing floors by rotation, masters taking on apprentices by word and handshake, buyers arriving for commissions, and rare material released only on a master's say-so. Local fitting, thermal craft and armor treatment happen here, which is what gives Ignivex's standardized sets their working identity. The district's standing tension is that when a piece fails nobody can prove whether it was rivalry, a Dravon hand or plain bad work, and all three get said aloud. Guild standing, apprenticeships and family workshops set the social order here.

Work on offer here: Ignivex — Keep the Fires Lit; Ignivex — The Remade Commission (ask Tavren Halessin).
The Red Forges.hiddenInfo: When a piece fails in the Red Forges, nobody can tell immediately whether the cause was a rival, a Dravon agent or simply bad work — and all three accusations get made, often the same day. That ambiguity is the district's live tension: standing Dravon pressure targets systems rather than open walls, so sabotage is a real possibility, but so is wounded pride looking for somewhere to land. The Rivalry Yard is where those arguments surface publicly; the Rare Materials Store is where they get expensive. Inside the Halessin workshop the same pattern runs in miniature. Maeron, Nessa and Tavren Halessin make window panes for the trade and take one commission at a time for pride, and a ruined commission is being quietly remade after hours. All three hold competing private theories about whose fault the ruin was, and none of them has said theirs aloud — which is the only reason the family is still working smoothly.

Metalwork Houses.description: The district's core workshops, tall-roofed halls where metal is worked at scale under extraction hoods and heat shielding. Masters, journeymen and apprentices share the floor by rotation. The halls run high and open, roofed for extraction, furnaces banked along one side and working floors laid in heat-rated stone that stays warm through the night. Overhead rigging carries pieces too heavy to lift by hand. Water, salt and somewhere to sit are kept at every entrance, because heat adaptation is not immunity and the houses gave up pretending otherwise a long time ago. The noise is constant and layered, and craftspeople here read a piece's readiness by colour and sound long before an instrument confirms it.

Thermal Crafting Lines.description: Engineered production lines that hold precise temperatures across a whole run, used for work that cannot tolerate variation. Operators watch readouts as closely as they watch the metal. The lines are enclosed runs with instrumented stages, fed from the district's heat channels and monitored from standing positions along their length where operators watch the readouts and the metal in the same glance. Nothing on a line is hurried and nothing is left unattended. A stoppage is logged with the name of whoever called it, which makes calling one a small act of courage for an operator still building standing. A line that drifts even slightly is shut down immediately, because in this district a flawed batch is never allowed to be only a technical problem.

The Heat-Channel Machinery.description: The machinery that routes and regulates working heat through the district — channels, regulators and transfer assemblies threaded under and through the workshops. Engineers service it constantly. The assemblies run under the workshop floors and up through the walls in copper-bronze runs, with valves, regulators and transfer housings reachable from maintenance gratings that people cross a dozen times a shift without looking down. Engineers service them in rotation and keep their own separate log. The machinery is local work, locally maintained, and the district says so often enough that visitors notice the emphasis. Standing on the maintenance gratings, the throb of the channels comes up through the soles of the boots before it is audible.

The Artisan Guild Halls.description: The guild halls where craft standing is recorded, apprenticeships are registered and masters argue over standards. Commissions are brokered here as well as judged. The halls are formal in a plain way, long tables, record walls, bronze-framed boards listing registered apprentices and open commissions, and the doors stay open to the district's noise rather than shutting it out. Masters attend because absence is read as a position. Rulings are posted where anyone can read them, and the crowd that gathers around a contested one is larger than the crowd that sat through the hearing. A guild ruling on whether a failed piece was bad work or bad luck carries real weight, which is why the arguments in these halls are rarely calm.

Weapon Shaping Floors.description: Open floors dedicated to shaping weapons, with anchored forms, shaping presses and quench assemblies set in the stone. The work is methodical and unhurried. The floors are anchored heavily, forms set into the stone, shaping presses standing in line and quench assemblies plumbed straight into the district's supply. The work is done by pairs and small teams who have worked together long enough not to need to speak. Pieces are tested before they leave, and a smith who declines to test in front of a buyer has effectively withdrawn the commission. Ignivex weaponry is expected to survive being used badly, and a smith who cannot explain their tolerances does not get a second commission.

Armor Treatment Baths.description: Treatment baths where armor is heat-cycled and finished, sunk into a shielded floor and worked with long bronze rigging. Pieces come out darkened and hard. The air above them shimmers even by this district's standards, and the floor around each one is kept clear and dry as a matter of standing discipline. Treatment runs in cycles that cannot be interrupted, so crews work in shifts and hand over mid-process. Ignivex's standardized sets come through here for fitting and finishing, and local treatment is what gives equipment obtained from Contair its Ignivex working identity. The chemical smell carries further than the heat does, and armorers claim they can tell a good batch by that smell alone.

Family-Run Workshops.description: The district's smaller family shops, each with its own furnace, bench line and household living space behind or above the work floor. Skills pass down inside these walls. Each shop is a single working room with the household's rooms adjoining it, furnace at one end, bench line down the side, and a door onto the lane that stands open whenever work is on. Children grow up on the floor and are given real tasks early. Meals happen at the bench as often as at a table, and a household's entire standing rests on work that leaves by that one door. Custody of a family's technique matters more here than guild rank, and a workshop losing its last trained child is a quiet local tragedy.

The Apprentice Benches.description: Long shared benches where apprentices do repetitive work under supervision until their hands stop arguing with them. Failures are kept and displayed. The benches run long and shared under plain light, the day's repetitive work set out in quantity: forms to be matched, fittings to be finished, the same joint made again until the hands stop arguing. Supervisors walk the line and say very little. Water is compulsory and taken at a called interval, which is one of the few rules in this district nobody treats as negotiable. Being allowed to take a bench nearest the working floor is the district's first real promotion, and everyone at the benches knows the order exactly.

The Rare Materials Store.description: A secured store holding rare and difficult materials, issued against guild authorisation and logged on release. Buyers wait while a request is checked. The store is a secured room with a counter, a logbook and shelving behind a grille, kept cooler than the workshops so that what it holds behaves predictably. Requests are made in writing against guild authorisation and checked before anything crosses the counter. The keeper releases by weight and signature and does not care whose commission is waiting, which makes this simultaneously the most orderly and the most resented room in the district. When a commission fails, the first argument is almost always about what came out of this store and who signed for it.

The Halessin Workshop.description: The Halessin glasswright shop: window panes for the trade by day, one pride commission at a time on the side. Maeron, Nessa and Tavren work it as a family. The shop is small and scrupulously clean, panes racked by size, the working bench set under the best light and a kiln line at the back running off the district's heat supply. Trade work pays for the room; the pride commission sits under cloth whenever there are customers in it. Maeron, Nessa and Tavren speak to one another in a shorthand nobody else in the lane can follow. A ruined commission is being quietly remade after hours, and the three of them keep three competing theories about whose fault the ruin was, none of them spoken.

The Rivalry Yard.description: An open yard between the larger workshops where competing craftspeople settle standing in public — comparisons, accusations and the occasional formal wager over quality. Work gets carried out and laid side by side. The yard is open, hard-floored and deliberately public, with benches and a set of trestles anyone may claim for laying work out. Comparisons are made piece against piece in the open rather than by argument alone. The district treats this as legitimate and even useful, and the guild halls quietly prefer a rivalry settled out here to one that arrives on their tables. A sabotage accusation made in this yard is heard by the whole district within the hour.

Geothermal Core Facilities.name: Geothermal Core Facilities
Geothermal Core Facilities.basicInfo:
The Geothermal Core Facilities are the player-facing access point to Ignivex's geothermal power network — heat tunnels, pressure chambers, thermal conduits, turbine halls and maintenance routes built into and beneath the city. This is local power, heat regulation, defensive pressure systems, transit support and emergency infrastructure, maintained by Ignivex crews. What can be reached here is the accessible face of a larger distributed system, and the rest stays as it is: the network's extent, depth, capacity and interconnections are not published, not drawn, and not discussed with people who have no business knowing them. The accessible portions are shored in heat-rated material and lit in low amber, marked at every junction with posted limits that crews treat as absolute, and loud enough in the turbine halls to force hand signals. Work is continuous: inspection rotations, conduit checks logged twice, pressure readings taken by gauge and by feel, repair teams living in the maintenance routes for the duration of a fault. Rated gear is mandatory and heat adaptation is no substitute for it. This is also the city's largest single exposure, which is why an unexplained pressure drop is treated as a possible act before it is treated as a fault. Tharen Volen oversees major parts of the network.

Work on offer here: Ignivex — Heat Below the Streets (ask Tharen Volen).
Geothermal Core Facilities.hiddenInfo: This is why Ignivex can refuse Contair-managed infrastructure and refuse Dravon in the same breath, and the city's pride in that self-sufficiency is real — resilience under siege is built into the design. It is also the city's largest single exposure. Geothermal sabotage can threaten entire districts, and standing Dravon pressure targets systems rather than open walls, which is why the Sabotage Watch Points exist and why a cracked conduit is investigated as a possible act before it is written off as wear. Tharen Volen's battlefield is underground: heat tunnels, pressure chambers, thermal gates, sabotage points and geothermal engines that would kill most outsiders in minutes. Caldris Wallworks connects here, tying the power network directly to the city's defense. What a player can reach is the accessible face of the network, not the network — its plant count, topology, depth, capacity and full underground extent are undefined, and parts of the system stay hidden.

The Heat Tunnels.description: The main working tunnels driven into the geothermal formation, shored in heat-rated material and lit in low amber. Crews move through them in rated gear on fixed rotations. The tunnels run rough-walled and shored, wide enough for two crew in gear and no wider, cable and conduit bracketed overhead and the amber lighting set low enough that a crew's own lamps do most of the work. Air moves through them constantly and dries everything it touches. Rotations are called in at the head of the tunnel and called out again on return, and a crew running late generates a response before anyone asks whether it was necessary. Time limits are posted at every junction, and nobody down here treats them as advisory.

The Pressure Chambers.description: Chambers where working pressure is held, stepped and released, walled in reinforced shielding and instrumented at every seam. Engineers read them by gauge and by feel. The chambers are heavily shielded rooms with stepped inlets, relief assemblies and instrument clusters at every seam, entered through doors that take two people to work. Readings are taken standing at the gauges rather than remotely, because the remote feed is the second opinion and never the first. Nothing in here is adjusted alone, and the rule holds for the engineers who have worked the chambers longest. The chambers make a deep irregular knocking as they cycle, and crews learn the healthy rhythm within a week.

The Thermal Conduits.description: The conduit runs distributing heat out to the districts, the forges and the transit system, inspected on a continuous schedule. A cracked conduit is a citywide problem. The runs are bracketed housings that shift and settle as they load, following the walls and roofs of the service ways where crews can reach them. Inspectors walk them section by section with lamps and instruments, checking seams, brackets and shielding. A section under repair is isolated and announced, because a district losing supply without warning is a civic incident and not merely an engineering one. Inspectors photograph and log every fault twice, because the second record is the one asked for when sabotage is suspected.

The Turbine Halls.description: Halls of geothermal turbines converting the city's underground heat into usable power, loud enough that crews work by hand signal. Output boards line the walls. The halls are the loudest rooms in Ignivex, machinery standing in ranks beneath gantries, the air moving hard and the floor carrying a vibration that never stops. Crews wear ear protection and speak by hand, and any conversation that needs words happens in the sealed side rooms. The boards are read at a glance by people who have read them for years and can tell from a single needle that something upstream has changed. This is the machinery Ignivex points to when anyone suggests it accept Contair-managed infrastructure instead.

The Maintenance Routes.description: Service routes threading between the halls, chambers and conduits, narrow and heavily marked. Repair teams live in them during a fault. They are narrow enough that two crew pass sideways, marked at every branch with colour, symbol and posted limits, with kit, water and rated gear cached along them at intervals and a call point wherever a branch could be taken wrongly. The relays work around the clock and sleep where they stop, and food carried down from the surface arrives cold and is warm by the time anyone opens it. The routes are mapped in detail for crews and deliberately not published anywhere else, which is a choice rather than an oversight.

The Emergency Access Paths.description: Dangerous emergency paths running through the facility, kept passable for reaching failures fast when the ordinary routes are compromised. They are genuinely hazardous. The paths run where nothing else does, alongside live runs, through sections that are not shut down for anybody, past shielding that is rated rather than generous. They are marked and maintained and never made comfortable. Crews train on them in full gear and in sequence, which is the reason they get used correctly by people who are frightened at the time. Crews are trained on them anyway, because the alternative is losing a district while waiting for a safer way in.

The Thermal Gates.description: Heavy gates isolating sections of the network so a failure in one part can be cut off from the rest. Operating one commits the crews on the far side. The gates are massive shielded assemblies set at section boundaries, worked from control positions beside them and from the overseer station, with a manual backup that takes two crews and a great deal of time. Indicators above each one show its state to anyone passing. Closing a gate isolates a failure and seals in whatever is on the wrong side of it, and the crews on both sides know exactly what a changing indicator means. The decision is taken quickly and argued about afterwards, sometimes for years.

The Geothermal Engines.description: The core engines of the accessible network, massive and locally maintained, running the heat regulation and defensive pressure systems the city depends on. Their sound carries through the rock. They sit deep in the accessible portion, built into the rock and serviced from platforms that ring them, with instrument positions set close enough that a reading can be taken by hand. Everything about them is local: local maintenance, local parts, local crews, and no imported power anywhere in the arrangement. Their note is a constant that people on the surface stop hearing until a shutdown makes it absent. Engineers speak about them with an ownership that outsiders consistently underestimate.

The Sabotage Watch Points.description: Monitored positions covering the network's known vulnerable junctions, staffed and logged continuously. Watchers record anomalies rather than judge them. The points are small staffed positions covering known vulnerable junctions, each with instrumentation, a log and a line to the overseer station, kept lit and occupied continuously rather than only during alerts. Watchers record what they see without interpreting it for anyone. Their logs are what people reach for when the question stops being what failed and becomes who was near it. Under standing Dravon pressure, an unexplained pressure drop is treated as a possible act until the evidence says otherwise.

Tharen’s Overseer Station.description: Tharen Volen's station, a working overseer post hung with live network readouts and cracked conduit sections kept as reference pieces. He runs the network from here and from the tunnels themselves. The station is a working room rather than an office, readouts covering one wall, cracked conduit sections racked as reference along another, and a table carrying route notes, rotation lists and somebody's abandoned meal. Tharen Volen is as often in the tunnels as at the desk. His pride is that the city is powered without Contair-managed systems or imported supply, and he will explain that to anyone who stands still long enough to hear it. Visitors are welcome only as far as the door until he decides otherwise.

Ignivex Lunar Gate.name: Ignivex Lunar Gate
Ignivex Lunar Gate.basicInfo: The Ignivex Lunar Gate is the city's gate, with direct destinations to Relstaris and Dustfall only. Heat-armored security, a Volen civic presence and emergency lockdown systems make it heavily monitored and politically sensitive. The gate complex is built heavy and watched: a heat-armored platform, a layered security line with controlled chokepoints, a Volen civic post carrying the city's formal face, staging approaches for each of the two destinations, and a lockdown control able to seal the platform and the approach at short notice. The materials are basalt-black and copper-bronze under muted red lighting, and the armoring on the fittings is not decorative. Traffic is steady rather than heavy, travellers, delegations, cargo and returning residents, and every one of them is checked, noted and, if anyone is waiting to meet them, noted again. The limit on destinations is deliberate and reinforces what Ignivex already is: connected, but not widely open, and dependent on controlled movement. Gate staff ask more than travellers expect and explain considerably less than travellers would like. Arrivals and departures happen under watch, and Cinderline Transit provides the protected access that carries traffic inward.
Ignivex Lunar Gate.hiddenInfo: A gate with two destinations shapes a city's politics. Ignivex is connected but not widely open, and that limitation reinforces its isolation, its military readiness and its dependence on controlled movement — while giving Relstaris and Dustfall an outsized importance in Ignivex logistics and political calculation that neither city necessarily earned. Meravil Ash Hall connects here, which means the surrender-leaning house has standing business at the one monitored point where people and information leave, and everyone including House Volen is aware of that. The watch rooms are not decorative: under standing Dravon pressure, who arrives, who departs and who meets them is treated as intelligence. What the gate is not is the only physical way into or out of Ignivex — no such exclusivity is established, and people who assume it make poor assumptions about how goods and travellers actually reach the city.

The Gate Platform.description: The gate's working platform, heat-armored and open to the transit approach, where travellers assemble for departure and arrivals first set down. Movement is orderly and watched. The platform is broad, armored and open toward the transit approach, with marked standing areas, equipment stations at the edges and overhead fittings shielded against heat and impact alike. Staff work it in visible numbers rather than discreetly. Departures assemble by destination and arrivals are moved along instead of being allowed to gather, so the space rarely feels as full as its traffic suggests it should. The platform is quieter than its traffic would suggest, because nobody here conducts business they would rather not have overheard.

The Heat-Armored Security Line.description: The screening line, built in layered heat armor with controlled chokepoints, where every arrival and departure is checked. Security here is thorough rather than theatrical. The line runs through layered armor in a sequence of chokepoints, each narrowing traffic to a pace the staff set, with inspection positions, holding alcoves and a supervisor's post overlooking the whole run. Baggage and cargo are opened. Questions are repeated at different points by different people, and the repetition is the method rather than an accident of staffing. Travellers who have passed through other Nexara gates notice immediately that this one asks more and explains less.

The Volen Civic Post.description: The Volen civic presence maintained at the gate, handling official reception, civic authority and the formal face Ignivex shows to anyone arriving. Banners hang inside the post. It is a formal room off the platform, banners hanging inside it and the triple flame in its broken heat ring worked into the fittings, furnished well enough to be the city's first impression and no more than that. Delegations are received here before they go anywhere else. The courtesy is genuine and the attention is total, and the officers see no contradiction between the two. The officers on duty are courteous and entirely unembarrassed about how closely they are paying attention.

Emergency Lockdown Control.description: The control position for the gate's emergency lockdown systems, able to seal the approach and the platform at short notice. Drills are run without warning. The control position sits behind armored glass with sightlines over the platform and the approach, its releases duplicated at a second station and tested on a schedule nobody outside the room is told. Operators run rehearsals without warning and without apologising for the disruption. Travellers caught in one are held where they stand, told nothing, and released with an explanation amounting to the word drill. The operators treat every lockdown rehearsal as live, on the reasonable assumption that one of them eventually will be.

The Relstaris Approach.description: The staging approach for Relstaris traffic, one of the gate's two direct destinations. Scholars, officials and traders move through it in both directions. It is a staging run with seating, water and a clerk's position, kept clear of the other destination's traffic so that the two never mix on the platform. The business being travelled on is frequently not stated and not asked after here. Relstaris matters to Ignivex politically, and this is where that relationship gets handled in person rather than at a distance. The political weight of the Relstaris connection is felt here first, in who is waiting to meet whom off an arrival.

The Dustfall Approach.description: The staging approach for Dustfall traffic, the gate's other direct destination. Cargo and hard-worn travellers pass through it constantly. The approach is plainer than its counterpart, laid out for cargo as much as for people, with load staging, hard benching and room to set a pack down without being in anyone's way. Travellers arrive worn and in working gear more often than not, and the flow runs heavier outward at some hours and inward at others. Gate staff treat this end of the job as the more honest one. The Dustfall line has a rougher reputation among gate staff, who describe it with something between complaint and affection.

The Arrival Hall.description: The hall where cleared arrivals wait, are met and begin moving inward toward the protected transit access. Heat hits newcomers here first. The hall is the first indoor space past the line, wide, high and deliberately unhurried, with benches, water points and staff who let people sit down before asking anything further of them. Locals wait along one side for the people they have come to collect. The city's heat arrives here before the city does, and how an arrival handles their first few minutes tells the staff most of what they need to know. Locals meeting visitors stand ready with water and the same warning about pacing themselves, delivered with varying degrees of patience.

The Watch Rooms.description: Monitoring rooms overlooking the platform, approaches and security line, where movement through the gate is observed and logged. The work is quiet and continuous. The rooms sit above the platform behind narrow shielded openings, dim, cool by local standards, lined with logs and live feeds covering the approaches and the security line. Watchers work quietly and write down more than they say. Nothing recorded here is discussed on the platform, and the staff below are not told what the rooms have noticed about the people they have just cleared. Under standing Dravon pressure, who came, who left and who met them is treated as information worth keeping.

Korrvane City.name: Korrvane City
Korrvane City.basicInfo: Korrvane City is the broad civic hub of the cliff metropolis, the layer where visitors first understand that open sky is road space and public training is ordinary. It presents a three-dimensional Starian metropolis built through cliff faces, elevated platforms, suspended civic layers and open sky corridors, without absorbing the work of the specialized locations around it. Storm-metal platforms and suspended walks stack above the cliff faces, banners snapping in constant wind, while residents read house colors and match histories as casually as street signs. Vertical streets climb between layers, suspended bridges cross the gaps, and rooftop landing pads take the arrivals that never touch a stair. The sky here is not empty space above the city; it is the main road system, sorted by speed and marked with directional lights. Ordinary life fills the rest: deliveries dropped onto terrace pads, children learning lane control long before anything resembling combat, families watching practice from balconies, and lifts and ramps carrying the many residents who do not fly. Most people here hold occupations that have nothing to do with competition. It is loud, airborne and communal without being a warzone, and wind conditions reorganize more of the day than any schedule does.
Korrvane City.hiddenInfo: The hub's real tension is that Korrvane measures everyone in public and then has to live with the results. Challenge boards and bracket displays are officially neutral, but posting order, board placement and display prominence are quiet political instruments, and someone is always arguing that a legal challenge was buried under three open-house notices. City Watch Perches log far more than unsafe challenges: obstruction reports, repeat aggressors and the slow accumulation of grudges that have not yet become matches. The watch answers to civic administration, not to Genesis directly, and its officers are not Dravon-style enforcers, which means their authority depends entirely on the crowd agreeing with them in the moment. On the residential terraces, families who have never fielded a competitor carry opinions about the ladder as strong as any house's, and retired contenders teaching at the learning terraces pass down old rivalries alongside lane etiquette. The gap between what the boards say and what the neighborhoods know is where most city rumors begin.

City Arrival Platforms.description: Broad landing terraces cut into the upper cliff for gate traffic, long-distance fliers and civic transit. Arrivals are held here long enough to receive lane guidance before entering denser airspace, and directional lights sort them by speed. The decking is layered stone over storm-metal, scuffed pale where landings have worn the surface treatment away, and the perimeter markings carry two generations of lane symbols at once. Attendants point newcomers toward the outer bands and remind them that couriers hold priority inside the marked cuts, while ramps and lift heads at the inner edge take everyone who is not going to fly. The first thing most visitors notice is the wind, and the second is that nobody else is using the safety rails.

Upper Flight Courts.description: Open public platforms where experienced fliers gather to stretch, warm up and drop into the high-speed city routes. Regulars trade route conditions and merge warnings while watching newcomers hesitate at the edge. The courts are bare working decks of heavy stone and bronze-black trim, with banner lines strung along the windward side so anyone can read the gusts before committing to a launch. Couriers cut through between jobs, off-shift civic workers use the far end for conditioning, and instructors bring older students up to practice merges under supervision rather than in live traffic. Launches are constant enough that the court has its own rhythm of shadows crossing the deck.

Mid-Level Civic Walks.description: Wide pedestrian and low-flight paths threading administrative offices, public halls, food access and district routes together. This is the city's connective tissue, busy at every hour, with low-speed lanes marked directly into the decking. Storm-metal railings run the outer edges, worn smooth where people lean to watch the drop, and suspended bridges carry the walks across the open gaps without ever leaving the wind. Residents move between levels, couriers descend to hand-height for a delivery and lift away again, families walk children toward the learning terraces, and drifting above the low-flight lane draws immediate commentary from the ground. Conversations here are half-shouted over the traffic and half-conducted by hand signal.

Windbreak Balconies.description: Sheltered civic balconies set behind storm-metal baffles, built for conversation, rest, family viewing and refuge when gust conditions turn dangerous. Older residents claim favored seats and hold them for years. The baffles are angled sheets pitted by years of grit, and behind them the noise of the city drops to something conversational, which is the entire reason the balconies exist. On ordinary afternoons they hold card games, homework, infants being fed and families watching practice on the courts opposite, and gust shelter here is a civic function rather than a courtesy. When the sirens call a hard-wind hold, these fill within minutes and the city goes unexpectedly quiet.

Mixed-House Residential Terraces.description: Lived-in housing layers for ordinary families, smaller houses, civic workers and retired contenders whose lives are not organized around the six major districts. Shared balconies, reinforced courtyards, neighborhood kitchens and slow access lanes make this the clearest view of everyday Korrvane. The buildings are heavy stone with bronze-black trim, built back into the cliff where they can be and out onto platforms where they cannot, and every courtyard is reinforced because somebody's relative eventually lands in it badly. Banners hang from the balconies out of loyalty rather than obligation, and residents who have never competed argue about the bracket as fiercely as anyone who has. Laundry lines and practice dummies share the same courtyard.

Civic Learning Terraces.description: Public school and youth-learning clusters teaching general education, house history, lane etiquette, movement safety and basic physical conditioning. These are schools first, not fighter academies, and teachers say so often. The terraces are stepped decks with low rails, sheltered classrooms cut back into the stone, and open floors where classes practice landing, stopping and holding position inside a marked band. Children learn to read directional lights and to yield to emergency descent before they learn any technique, and much of the rest is public conduct: how to decline a challenge, how to lose where others can see. Lessons are scheduled around tournament traffic because half the class will be at the Arena otherwise.

Public Challenge Boards.description: Officially maintained boards carrying legal challenges, public sparring requests, training invitations and open-house events. Postings are verified before they go up, and pulling one down without authority is itself an offense. The boards are broad storm-metal panels set into a sheltered wall, close enough to the low-flight lane that a courier can read the top rows without landing, and the surface around them is scarred from generations of leaning and arguing. Onlookers make sure a declared challenge names an approved space, and ordinary notices share the same frame: a house looking for a trainer, a school asking for volunteers. A crowd forms whenever an unexpected name appears beside a well-known one.

Local Bracket Displays.description: Citywide visual panels showing the running weekly bracket, prior results, public odds and ladder eligibility, rendered in symbols and portraits rather than dense text. They update mid-match, and the surrounding walkway noise rises and falls with them. The panels are mounted high on civic frontages and angled for readers on foot and in the low-flight lane alike, their reinforced glass replaced often enough that the newest are noticeably clearer than their neighbors. Vendors position themselves within sight of one, and off-shift workers stop to check a single line and stay for the next three. Arguments about a disputed result usually start within arm's reach of a display.

Civic Training Platforms.description: Open public exercise decks with training rigs mounted straight into the surrounding civic buildings, used for health, youth classes, physical education and non-professional sparring. Nobody here is preparing for the ladder. Older residents work through slow movement routines at one end while a school class occupies the other, and the middle belongs to whoever booked it. Practice bouts are agreed between partners with the exercise named in advance and either side free to stop, and the supervising instructors care more about control than outcomes. The impact marks on the walls are old, repainted, and treated as part of the finish.

City Watch Perches.description: Elevated observation posts for civic responders who break up unsafe challenges, clear lane obstructions and handle collateral damage. They are not enforcers in the Dravon sense; their job is to keep a physical culture from tipping into chaos. The perches are small storm-metal boxes bracketed onto structure where routes merge, fitted with signal lights, a clear view of several lanes and a bench nobody finds comfortable for a full shift. Officers watch for hovering in active merges, for deliberate wake disruption, which the city treats as hostile conduct, and for challenges that have not moved into an approved lane. Watch officers spend most shifts talking people down rather than intervening.

The Arena.name: The Arena
The Arena.basicInfo:
The Arena is Korrvane's cultural heart, cut into the rock below the Genesis cliff and far more than a combat floor. It is registration center, public forum, food district, betting market, historical archive and political stage at once, layered with spectator platforms under an open sky corridor. The Genesis Compound is visible above it from nearly every angle, which is entirely deliberate. Grounded visitors come up the broad ramps from the Lower Grounds while fliers descend through controlled arrival bands, and nothing resembling a fight is tolerated in the approach airspace. Heavy stone, storm-metal and reinforced glass take the punishment, and house banners move constantly in the wind above the tiers. District and open-entry qualifiers run throughout the week, registration and medical checks come before the public bracket opens, early rounds draw district-heavy attendance, and the weekly final becomes a citywide event before any ladder attempt begins on the judges' word. Between brackets the place still works: medics, cleaning crews, vendors restocking, and parents walking children through empty tiers they once competed in. Post-match traffic drains toward the Recovery Yards, the Commerce Layer and Luxaryn Quarter, and the food smoke stays in the seating long after the crowd has gone.

Work on offer here: Korrvane — Arena Night Crew; Korrvane — Fighting Your Way In; Korrvane — The Qualifier; Korrvane — The Main Bracket; Korrvane — The Genesis Ladder.
The Arena.hiddenInfo: The Arena runs on a weekly cycle that never fully stops. District and open-entry qualifiers grind through the week; registration and medical checks clear before the public bracket opens; early rounds fill with district crowds, mid-rounds pull the wider city, and the weekly final becomes a citywide event. Only after the judges name a champion does the Genesis ladder attempt begin, and the crowd's noise changes character when it does. Beneath that rhythm sit the pressures worth discovering. Betting odds sometimes move in ways nobody can account for, and a suspicious line is the cleanest investigation hook the city offers. Caelthorn objections arrive at the Judges' Dais with the paperwork already prepared. Vorreth results keep breaking prediction models, and no one can say whether that is method or accident. Medical clearances are occasionally optimistic, and the Medic Gate sees the consequences. The Victory Wall's record of Nina Castro's visit is kept in a deliberately disputed section: officially it established outside-entry precedent, unofficially it is remembered as the day she treated the ladder like a route to Ark's pantry. Post-match traffic drains toward the Recovery Yards, the Commerce Layer and Luxaryn Quarter, carrying the night's arguments with it.

Grand Arena Approach.description: A massive processional route linking the Lower Grounds, mid-level flight routes and public gate traffic to the Arena proper. Grounded visitors climb broad ramps while fliers descend through controlled arrival bands overhead. The ramp surface is heavy stone worn into shallow troughs along the most-used lines, and the bronze-black trim on the rails has been polished down by hands rather than by crews. Stewards work the merge points where the ramp traffic meets the landing bands, holding one stream while the other clears, and the emergency drop path along the outer edge is kept empty regardless of how crowded the rest becomes. On bracket days the approach becomes a slow river of house colors and vendor smoke.

Competitor Registration Hall.description: The formal sign-in space where registrars verify eligibility, medical clearance, declared equipment, challenge status and house authorization. Lines move by house and by qualifier route, and the clerks are unimpressed by reputation. The hall is deliberately plain, a long stone chamber with counters down one side and benches down the other, lit hard enough that nobody can hide a wince. Declared equipment is inspected on the counter in front of whoever is next in line, replacement entrants need judge approval before the public bracket opens, and Bostarix Orvantis is a familiar presence at the procedural counters. Refusing to disclose an active medical restriction here ends careers more often than any opponent does.

Challenger Waiting Galleries.description: Layered waiting tiers where fighters prepare while watching the matches ahead of theirs. Rivals sit close enough to talk, provoke, encourage or intimidate, and officials stand between them to prevent anything pre-match. The tiers are open to the combat volume, so the crowd noise arrives unfiltered and conversation happens in the gaps between it. Benches are worn through to bare metal at the front edge where people sit forward, house attendants circulate with wraps and water, and a trainer reviewing tactics competes with commentary echoing off the stone. The air smells of wrap resin, and the gallery falls silent whenever a name is called.

House Seating Tiers.description: Reserved public sections maintained by the six major minor houses as identity platforms rather than sealed boxes. Orvantis seating is old and carefully preserved; Zelvaris spare and covered in analysis slates; Caelthorn suspiciously comfortable; Aevon high and hard for non-fliers to reach; Luxaryn loud and ringed with food; Vorreth differently occupied every week. Families treat their tier as a gathering, arriving with food, children and long-running arguments, and neighbors who belong to no house at all are seated among them without comment. Banners are re-hung before every bracket because the wind takes them down. The tiers empty in reverse order of how invested their occupants are.

The Tournament Grounds.description: The main open-air combat floor, built for ground and aerial fighting alike. The floor is marked and the sky above it is a declared, controlled combat volume with its own boundary lights. Matches end on surrender, incapacitation, ring or airspace conditions, technical stoppage or judge ruling, and deliberate lethal escalation carries civic consequences severe enough that nobody treats it as a tactic. Weapons are not outlawed in the city, but they are tightly regulated on this floor, which visiting specialists learn at the inspection counter rather than here. Between bouts the surface crews sweep impact debris while the crowd noise resets for the next pairing.

The Aerial Ring.description: A suspended vertical combat zone used when altitude and open-sky control decide the match. Marker beacons define its walls, and spectators track fights by watching the lights the fighters cross. The ring hangs clear of the seating on storm-metal anchors, with safety observers stationed around its lower rim and an emergency descent path held open beneath it at all times. Wind moves through the volume constantly, so competitors read the banners on the nearest tier before committing to an approach. Judges can call the volume closed if conditions turn the boundaries unreliable, which is unpopular with competitors and accepted anyway. Aevon competitors perform especially well here, and they are not modest about it.

Genesis Ladder Staging Area.description: The distinct platform where the judges' weekly champion prepares to face the Genesis ladder. Crowd behavior changes at the threshold: casual tournament noise gives way to focused silence because everyone understands the power gap. The staging floor is bare, set where the cliff rises directly above it so the compound is in view from the mark, and the champion may accept or decline publicly with no loss of standing for declining. Attendants keep the space clear, medics stand ready rather than nearby, and the attempt begins only after the judges confirm the result behind it. Alcandrus is always the first gatekeeper, and no minor-house champion has beaten him.

Judges’ Dais.description: A raised tribunal platform for judges, rulekeepers, safety officials and technical observers. Disputed calls, unusual match conditions and formal objections are resolved in the open where the crowd can watch the reasoning. The dais is storm-metal over stone with a low bronze-black rail, deliberately placed so that anyone arguing before it does so in full view of the tiers. Protests over a medical stoppage are heard, and the fighter stays removed until cleared regardless of how the argument goes. Baalrix Caelthorn files here often, and Caelthorn representatives are here often enough that the officials know their filing habits by sight.

Public Commentary Perches.description: Mobile platforms that reposition as fights move vertically, carrying commentators who preserve history, explain tactics and stoke rivalries. Occasionally they coin a humiliating phrase that follows a fighter for years. The perches are light storm-metal cages on adjustable anchors, crewed by a commentator and whoever is keeping the running record, and they rock noticeably in a hard gust. Commentary reaches the tiers, the approach and the food ring alike, which is why the best line of the day is repeated across the district by evening. The perches drift on their own lane clearance, and inexperienced fliers are warned to stay well clear.

The Betting Stands.description: A row of public bookmakers posting odds on matches, upsets, ladder survival, aerial knockdowns and technical outcomes. Boards recalculate visibly and the crowd reacts faster than the numbers. The stands are heavy counters under fixed awnings, their frontages scarred where people have leaned on them for years, and each keeps its own written record that officials can ask to see. Regulars work several boards at once looking for a disagreement between them, and vendors, off-duty stewards and house attendants drift past for the numbers rather than the wagers. A line that moves without any apparent reason draws attention from more than gamblers.

The Cache.description: The Corsair trading post set near the main spectator route, selling fight-day goods, equipment, supplies and whatever the current operator hauled into the city. The sign by the entrance reads: Xyren Corsair — froze before he even made it through these gates. The shop is a deep bay cut into the stone behind a wide counter, stock stacked to the ceiling in no order anyone but the operator understands, and the inventory changes completely between visits. Sealed cargo arrives from the gate lockers on bracket weeks, and the operator will hold an item for a regular without anything being written down. Nobody working here confirms the story, and the sign stays up.

Arena Street Food Ring.description: A dense tournament-day food route of fixed stalls and carts attached to the platform edges, serving fast, heavy, high-energy meals. Luxaryn vendors hold the best positions and defend them through relationships rather than force. Qartessa Luxaryn's people work this route as well as the quarter's own, and they know the bracket schedule better than most competitors do. Queues form and dissolve with the match rhythm, families eat standing at the rail with the combat floor in view, and stall crews keep working through the loudest moments because the crowd will want feeding the instant it ends. The smoke drifts up into the seating tiers and gives the whole Arena its bracket-day smell.

Hannivex Corsair’s Stall.description: A stall retailing inferior Dravon-manufactured equipment as disposable gear, target material, running jokes and occasional projectiles. Hannivex knows exactly what he is selling and has built a stable business out of the punchline. The stall is a folding counter under a patched awning, its stock displayed with labels that make the joke explicit, and trainers genuinely buy from it because gear meant to fail is useful for drills. Visitors who assume the merchandise is meant seriously get an honest explanation before any coin changes hands. Buyers test-snap a strap at the counter and he laughs along with them.

Medic Gate.description: The direct route from the combat volume to emergency treatment and onward to the Recovery Yards. Severe injuries are stabilized inside the gate before transfer, with responders holding the lane clear. The gate is a wide reinforced passage kept permanently empty, its floor marked in a color used nowhere else in the Arena, and the emergency drop lane above it has absolute right-of-way through every layer of traffic. Families wait at the outer mouth because they are not permitted further in, and attendants there give the only information anyone is going to get for a while. Arena medics can stop a match outright, and a fighter who refuses required treatment risks suspension.

Victory Wall.description: A public record of weekly champions, historic upsets, famous losses, ladder attempts and moments the city refuses to forget. Losses are inscribed with the same care as wins, because Korrvane respects a clean defeat. The wall is worked stone with bronze-black lettering, cut deeper in the older sections and crowded in the newer ones, and people trace a name with a hand as they pass without breaking their conversation. Families bring children to find a relative's line, and retired contenders are asked to explain entries they would rather not discuss. One deliberately disputed section records Nina Castro's visit in two contradictory readings.

Genesis Ridge.name: Genesis Ridge
Genesis Ridge.basicInfo: Genesis Ridge is the mountainside above the compound, wind-exposed and severe, where House Genesis finds the altitude and privacy the city below cannot offer. Training routes worn across generations climb toward a summit sparring platform, and stone markers record old fights and family moments along the way. The city is visible from almost everywhere here, and the quiet is the point. Access runs through the restricted approach airspace, so the ridge holds nobody who was not invited or escorted, and the absence of an audience changes what happens on it. There is almost no built structure: bare rock, cut steps where the routes needed them, anchor points hammered into stone by people who are no longer alive to explain them, and a few stabilized sections where damage was repaired without being hidden. The wind is constant and shifts without pattern at the switchbacks, which is half of the training value and all of the risk. Matches here are private and serious, conversations here are the ones nobody wants overheard, and the old history the house carries is easier to speak about at this altitude than in any hall below it. The noise of Korrvane arrives thin, late and far away, and the ridge gives that noise back nothing at all.
Genesis Ridge.hiddenInfo: The ridge is restricted training and memory ground, reached through Genesis Approach Airspace where visitors need permission or escort. What happens here is deliberately unwitnessed in a city built on witnessing. Ark and Tacitus hold conversations on these paths that neither would have inside the compound. Sorvina uses the summit and the scar path to carry grief through training rather than around it, and her matches up here are private and serious in a way Arena bouts never are. Orvanus knows what most of the old training markers mean and decides case by case whether to explain them; several record injuries and losses the family has never made public. The Dravon Scar Path is the sharpest edge: its repairs deliberately preserve marks from the old conflict, giving the war memory a physical place to live so that the rest of Korrvane does not have to carry it. Anyone brought up here by a Genesis member has been trusted with something, and usually has not been told so directly.

Ridge Paths.description: Training routes worn into the mountainside across generations, branching by purpose: endurance, altitude control, aerial combat, raw movement under pressure. The footing changes with the weather and the wind shifts without warning at the switchbacks. Sections have been cut into steps where the rock refused to hold a line, and the anchor points along the steeper runs were set by hands nobody in the house can name any more. The routes are used on foot as often as in the air, because the house treats the climb as conditioning rather than as transport, and a session is judged by the state of the person at the top. Climbing them is itself the lesson before any sparring begins.

Summit Platform.description: The highest accessible sparring platform on the ridge, anchored into bare rock with the whole island spread below. Ark and Sorvina use it more than anyone else, and matches here are private and serious. The platform is unadorned storm-metal over stone, scarred in the center and scoured clean at the edges by the wind, with no seating and nothing resembling a spectator position. Terms are set between the two people involved and nobody else records the result, which makes this one of the few places in Korrvane where a fight is not also a public statement. Sound carries strangely at this altitude; the city noise arrives thin and delayed.

Old Training Markers.description: Stone markers set along the routes recording breakthroughs, old fights, injuries and family moments. They are not formal monuments and carry no inscriptions a stranger could read. Some are cut blocks, some are simply stones moved a short distance and left where they were meant to be, and the weather has taken the edges off most of them. A few stand where the wind makes it hard to linger, which is understood to be part of the record. Younger members walk past markers whose meaning they have not been told yet, and that is treated as a matter of timing rather than secrecy. Orvanus knows what most of them mean, and chooses when that knowledge is worth passing on.

Windscar Overlook.description: A quieter ledge facing Korrvane, used for reflection, hard conversations and watching the city without being watched by it. The wind cuts across it constantly, which is where the name comes from and why nothing is built here. The rock is scoured smooth in bands, and there is room for two people to sit with the whole vertical city laid out beneath them, the flight lanes reading as slow lines of light from this far up. People come here after a loss, before a decision, or when something has to be said that would be repeated anywhere else in Genesis territory. It is the one place in Genesis territory with no audience at all.

Dravon Scar Path.description: A damaged route whose repairs deliberately preserve marks left by the old conflict, stabilized but never smoothed over. It gives Sorvina and Orvanus a physical place to carry war memory without turning all of Korrvane grim. The stabilizing work is visible as newer stone set beside older damage, and the crews who maintain it are instructed to keep the difference legible rather than to finish the surface. Nobody trains for speed on this route. Orvanus explains what happened here when he judges the moment right, and Sorvina uses it without needing anything explained. Walking it is slower than the other paths, which is also intentional.

The Commerce Layer.name: The Commerce Layer
The Commerce Layer.basicInfo: The Commerce Layer runs through Korrvane's middle elevation as a dense band of trade and social life. Shops stack vertically, vendors clamp their stalls to platform edges, and goods move through both foot traffic and flight lanes at once. It is where the city shops, drinks, prepares for brackets, trades with Corsairs and argues about matches long after they end. Layered stone-and-storm-metal terraces carry the shopfronts, suspended bridges cross between them, and the whole band is strung with banners, awnings and delivery lines that move continuously in the wind. Couriers work the layer hard, dropping to counter height and lifting away without landing, while lifts and ramps bring up everyone arriving from the Lower Grounds with cargo or without flight. The rhythm follows the bracket: supply stalls swell before a major week, food routes fill when the Arena empties, and the bars stay loud until the arguments have been settled or abandoned. Away from that rhythm it is simply where people buy training clothes, replace a broken tool, eat between shifts and complain about the price of everything. Deliveries are refused politely when a manifest looks wrong, and everyone along the rail hears about it before the day is out.
The Commerce Layer.hiddenInfo: Information is the layer's most valuable commodity and the least regulated. The Public Rumor Rail moves news faster than official notices, which makes it useful to commentators, vendors and anyone who needs a story circulating before the judges rule. The Gray Area is Caelthorn's bar: the drinks are excellent, the prices fair, and the staff know more than they should, which is precisely the service being sold. Across the layer The Ascent carries the opposite crowd, Zelvaris fighters and technical regulars locked in a running argument over whether Caelthorn should remain tournament-eligible at all. Betting rumors, blackmail leverage and bracket-week price manipulation all pass through here before they reach anywhere that keeps records. The Corsair post rotates cargo that nobody inventories publicly, and the Bracket Supply Market's expansion before a major bracket is a reliable early indicator of how large the crowd expects the event to be. Luxaryn's grip on the food route is relational rather than legal, and it holds because breaking it would cost more relationships than it would gain.

The Ascent.description: A heavy, worn bar favored by Zelvaris fighters and serious combat regulars, built into a rising stack of platform decks. Technical arguments run constantly and loudly, most of them about form and measurement. The furniture is bolted down, the stairs between decks are narrow enough to bottleneck an argument, and the walls carry old impact marks that the owners have never bothered to finish over. Analysis slates are propped on tables between drinks, a disputed sequence gets replayed with hand signals across the room, and anyone who cannot support a claim with something measured is told so immediately. The primary unresolved debate is whether Caelthorn should remain tournament-eligible, and it has been unresolved for years.

The Gray Area.description: Caelthorn's suspiciously comfortable bar, where the drinks are excellent, the prices are fair and the staff know a great deal more than they should. Nothing about the place is technically wrong, which is exactly what unsettles first-time visitors. The seating is arranged in small separated groups, the lighting is warm, the noise never rises past conversational, and there is always a free table when someone useful arrives. Staff remember an order from a single previous visit and mention it pleasantly, and a guest who arrives angry is seated somewhere the anger will not carry. Nothing is written down anywhere a customer can see. Regulars arrive knowing they are paying in conversation as much as coin.

Short Shock Express.description: A Corsair trading post dealing components, supplies, travel goods and rotating cargo of uncertain provenance. A sign near the entrance reads: Xyren Corsair — so short he had to have his ship custom built so he could reach the controls. The shop is a narrow storefront with stock crowded to the ceiling and a counter that leaves just enough room to turn around, and the cargo behind it changes with whatever came through the gate lockers this week. Travelers come for replacement parts, repair crews come for fittings nobody else stocks, and both get the same shrug about what will be available next time. The local operator did not place it and has been asked not to remove it.

Platform Vendor Rows.description: Stacked commercial terraces selling training clothes, house banners, recovery goods, food, tools and ordinary civilian supplies. Stalls hang off the platform edges on reinforced brackets, and deliveries arrive by flight as often as by lift. Awnings snap all day in the wind and are re-tied several times before evening, the brackets are inspected on a schedule nobody trusts entirely, and the walkways between the rows are just wide enough for two people and a cargo frame. Families shop here for school clothes and replacement cookware with as much attention as anyone buying wraps for a bracket. The rows are the layer's spine; almost every route through the district touches them.

Bracket Supply Market.description: A tournament-focused market that swells in the days before a major bracket and contracts again afterward. It carries legal wraps, approved protective gear, house tokens, spectator supplies and analysis slates, with sellers who can quote the current equipment rules from memory. Temporary stalls clamp onto the permanent frames and come off again once the bracket closes, leaving bare mounting points along the deck. Sellers will refuse a sale outright if the item would not survive inspection at registration, partly from professional pride and partly because the complaint comes back to them. How far it expands tells the city how big the week will be.

Mid-Layer Food Flight.description: A continuous route of fixed stalls and hovering food carts threading the middle elevation, busy from early work traffic through to the post-match crowds. Luxaryn influence is strongest along this stretch, expressed through vendor relationships rather than ownership. Smoke and steam pull sideways off the stalls in the wind, the fixed counters have standing rails worn pale at elbow height, and the hovering carts hold station in a marked band so they never obstruct a live lane. Regulars order without speaking, shift workers eat at hours the rest of the city considers wrong, and families collect food to carry home rather than eat at the rail. The carts drift with the queue and reposition without ever quite stopping service.

Second Landing.description: A fixed café stall with attached seating on the food route, with a sheltered serving bay, a standing rail, a short seated counter, shared tables and a clear collection point. Seating faces inward so passing fliers do not take over the conversation, and there are places to rest bags and shopping. A baffle on the windward side keeps the cups where they are put, the shared tables get colonized by the same neighborhood groups at the same hours, and the collection point is marked plainly enough that nobody has to ask. Deliveries arrive at the back of the bay rather than across the seating, which is the kind of decision regulars notice and never mention. Its owner wants a dependable neighborhood café, not a landmark.

Public Rumor Rail.description: A long balcony where spectators, vendors, commentators and off-duty officials gather with a view over the layer below. Information moves faster along this rail than through any official notice, and everyone present knows it. The rail is storm-metal, polished bright by forearms along its whole length, with the drop on one side and a run of stalls on the other that exist mostly to serve people who came to talk. Betting lines, injury reports, seeding complaints and house gossip all pass along it in the same tone, and a claim gets challenged within minutes by someone who was actually present. A story that starts here is usually citywide before the judges have finished deliberating.

The Flight Lanes.name: The Flight Lanes
The Flight Lanes.basicInfo:
The Flight Lanes are Korrvane's roads. Marked bands of open air run between every layer of the city, lit by directional signals and sorted by speed, purpose and priority. Movement through them supports full scenes on its own: commutes, races, chases, disputes and the constant public display of skill that the city treats as ordinary. The sky is not empty space above Korrvane; it is the main road system, and it is regulated like one.
