Ward doctrine puts protection over punishment, forbids criminal punishment and political-loyalty interrogation, and keeps units out of private homes without emergency cause; Aegis units cannot be deployed for routine civic enforcement and draw their strength from formation discipline rather than individual power. Echo-Class work stays restricted and is not public spectacle: an Echo shell models a specific living Starian's appearance, voice, posture and reproducible technique, and copies no memories, identity, consciousness, relationships or true affinity powers. Authorisation requires informed consent from the source, clinical separation from Myralis records, technical review, a defined purpose, a limited deployment period and a reset plan. The Inactive Personality Review Bay holds the hardest open question in the city: a quirky drone is not automatically a person, and a construct is not denied review merely because its individuality emerged unintentionally. No case there is resolved.

Worker Drone Galleries.description: Galleries holding worker drones in the silence the location is known for, rank on rank of infrastructure, workforce and emergency support that is explicitly not all people. The galleries run long under high framing, the light held low along the walking lanes and absent above them, so that the depth of the racking is heard rather than seen. Capacity, which classes are held and how many is unestablished, as is any relationship to the Residential District's service hub. The scale is the part that unsettles first-time visitors, and residents who work here stop noticing it within a season. Nothing in the galleries moves unless it has been asked to, which is precisely what makes the stillness feel deliberate.

Civil Defense Racks.description: Racks of civil-defence units, standing on the lesson Contair learned the hard way: how long civilians actually required to reach shelter. The racking is close-set and orderly under restrained light, guidance lines running past it toward the launch end, everything positioned for retrieval rather than display. What a rack holds, how many, and whether or how deployment is triggered is not established, and no response time or threshold is invented. They are kept ready by a city that has already imagined most disasters, which is the reason Vexorath feels calm rather than nervous. The racks are checked as routine maintenance and are otherwise left alone, and nobody working past them treats that as strange.

Ward Deployment Hall.description: Where Ward-Class Security Drones deploy from: Starian height, broadly comparable baseline strength, no visible weapons, protective and restraint systems inside the forearms. The hall is tall and plain, the units standing where they were positioned rather than arranged for effect, and the quiet in it is the quiet of a room full of things that are not switched on. Their force priority runs warn, redirect, create distance, shield civilians, restrain, disable an immediate threat, request higher authority. They cannot impose punishment, interrogate for political loyalty, or enter private homes without emergency cause. Residents read them as infrastructure; visitors find them intimidating. A Ward refusing an order over conflicting casualty priorities is doctrine working, not malfunction.

Aegis Formation Vault.description: Where Aegis-Class Alpha Drones are held, and the only class permitted a second figure in canon imagery, because formation is the entire point. The vault is deep and dim, units recessed and partially in shadow, with the light picking out working lanes rather than the machines themselves. One Aegis is dangerous; a coordinated formation is the true system, built on shared targeting, casualty-aware spacing, command transfer, adaptive defence geometry and reassembly after communication loss. Isolated, they are measurably weaker, and formation damage creates gaps that can be exploited. They carry no biological affinity, improvise badly in social situations, and cannot be used for routine civic enforcement. Vault capacity, formation size and readiness states are unstated.

Echo Simulation Chamber.description: Restricted, because Echo-Class work is not public spectacle. The chamber is closed, plainly finished and gives nothing away from outside, which is consistent with how the city treats the whole subject. An Echo shell is modelled on a specific living Starian and may approximate appearance, voice, posture, movement and reproducible technique, and copies no memories, identity, consciousness, relationships or true affinity powers. It can imitate a person closely enough to cause confusion. It cannot become one. Authorisation stays intact: informed consent from the source, clinical separation from Myralis records, technical review, a defined purpose, a limited period, and a reset and archive plan. How many shells exist, and whether any is active, is unrecorded.

Drone Maintenance Wells.description: Maintenance wells serving the drone population, in a House that treats maintenance, redundancy and revision as principles. The wells are sunken working bays with good close light and open repair channels, the one part of the Holds where the noise of tools is normal and the silence is not. The citywide malfunction protocol runs here as everywhere: protect people, isolate dangerous functions, preserve records, identify whether the behaviour is damage, adaptation, interference or identity development, then repair, reset, restrict or recognise. Immediate wiping is not the default, and the protocol names no venue, so nothing is settled in these wells. Well count, throughput, who works here and whether residents may watch are all unstated.

Tactical Coordination Room.description: Tavris Contair's room, and his canonical setting: a command prism between two fingers, the other hand directing low. The room is compact and dark-surfaced, working light rather than display, built for thinking through a problem that has not happened yet. He designs fallback behaviour, formation logic, casualty priorities and command transfer for when networks fail, which is why the room is quiet even during an incident. Rezulith retains final authority for civilization-level deployment, Solanis commands station formations, and doctrine is written here rather than shouted. Who else staffs it, and what its relationship to the station's command gallery is, are unestablished. Most of what happens in it is argument about a case nobody has met yet.

Classification Control Room.description: A control room for drone classification, part of the Holds' standing brief over readiness, classification, doctrine and restricted systems. It is a working room of terminals and worktables under restrained light, unremarkable in a location that is mostly enormous and empty. The ordinary friction is workers arguing with classification systems, which happens often enough to be a joke rather than a grievance. Classification and personhood can intersect when a unit stops matching its class, but no order between them is established, and nothing decided in this room decides personhood; the dedicated review bay exists precisely so that this room does not have to. The classification scheme itself, who may change a classification, and what an appeal would mean are unstated.

Inactive Personality Review Bay.description: The dedicated space for examining possible emergent synthetic individuality without immediately wiping a unit or declaring it independent. It is a small, quiet, unhurried room, closer in feel to a consultation space than to the racking outside it, and a unit under review is not stored here as inventory. The threshold is several markers over time: persistent self-reference, stable preferences unexplained by task optimisation, independent refusal, memory treated as personal, relationships pursued without assignment, distress at forced reset. Both errors are forbidden. A suspected personality is not declared a person to avoid difficult maintenance, and not erased to avoid difficult ethics. No unit is declared a person here, and no case in the bay is resolved.

Emergency Launch Corridor.description: Where units leave fast. It is a cleared lane running out from the racks and the deployment spaces, guidance lines bright against a dark floor and nothing stored along its length, because everything about it is arranged for the moment when it is needed. During a breach, system collapse, mass casualty event or gate failure, authority passes to the most relevant qualified person and to automated safety protocols, and that emergency control is temporary, with its decisions reviewed afterward. Corridor is a name rather than a route; no destination or geometry is stated, and neither is capacity, mechanism or response time. On an ordinary day it is the emptiest space in a location full of empty space.

Outer Shell.name: Outer Shell
Outer Shell.basicInfo:
The Outer Shell is Vexorath's defensive perimeter and the physical record of every attempt to break Contair independence: barriers, threat detection, shelters, countermeasures and preserved historical layers. Breach points became new structural layers and temporary defences became permanent systems, so the Shell reads as architecture and archive at once, and the joins between its eras are left legible rather than smoothed over. The city's own register is here in heavier form, white structural framing over charcoal recesses, cobalt guidance lines along the working walks, restrained internal illumination and repair channels open wherever maintenance has to reach. What the barrier is made of, how it works, what it stops, how far it runs and whether it encloses the whole city are all deliberately unstated, and the Shell offers no answer to any of them. Rezulith holds final authority over it. Stories out here do not require an invasion, and Vexorath is not a constant battlefield: a false classification, hidden damage, forgotten systems or a disputed evacuation decision carries the same weight. Its tone is calm, formidable, and layered with old memory. Nothing about it feels urgent, which is the effect a century of revision has on a wall.

Work on offer here: Vexorath — The Layer That Woke (ask Tavris Contair).
Outer Shell.hiddenInfo: Stories out here do not require an invasion, and Vexorath is not a constant battlefield. A false classification, hidden damage, forgotten systems, old embedded technology or a disputed evacuation decision carries equal weight. The best and most alarming of those is already canon: an old Shell layer activating for a threat category nobody now remembers creating. The repair crawl network is the natural place to find something where nothing should be, though whether it is human-accessible, drone-only or mixed is deliberately unstated. Final authority over the Outer Shell sits with Rezulith. The Dravon Attack Archive is the Shell's own record of assaults, embedded in the structure that absorbed them — distinct from Chronicle Hall's Restricted Dravon Archive, with no relationship between the two asserted. The permanent Contair bar on House Dravon is not softened here, and the Starian Conflict Chronicle records Vexorath's engagements as a failure-analysis series rather than as named battles.

Primary Barrier Spine.description: The Shell's principal barrier structure, with its own history built into it: breach points became new structural layers, temporary defences became permanent systems. Walking its inner face means passing through work of visibly different ages, joined rather than blended, the older layers left where they can be read. What the barrier is made of, how it works, what it stops, how far it runs and whether it encloses the whole city are all deliberately unstated, and no coverage, strength or capability claim is made anywhere. Final authority over it belongs to Rezulith. The Spine is the clearest statement Vexorath makes about itself: a House that could not match numbers or raw force decided to out-revise everyone instead, and then kept the evidence.

Drone Deployment Nodes.description: Points on the Shell from which drones deploy, with the Outer Shell listed among Aegis primary locations. Node count, placement, which classes deploy from which node and how they respond are unestablished, and no spacing or coverage pattern is asserted. From the walk they look like nothing much: recessed, closed, and entirely uninterested in being looked at, a charcoal seam in a pale structural face that gives no indication of depth. Nobody demonstrates them and nobody explains them, and residents passing on ordinary business do not slow down. Aegis units draw their strength from formation rather than individual power, cannot be used for routine civic enforcement, and require extraordinary authorisation outside Contair territory.

Historical Breach Layer.description: A preserved layer of the Shell associated with a historical breach, kept because Contair preserved its lessons rather than hiding them. It is left structurally distinct from what was built around it afterwards, so that the point where something got through remains identifiable rather than repaired into invisibility. Which breach, when, by whom, how far it got and whether more than one is preserved are all unstated; the conflict record treats Vexorath's engagements as failure analysis rather than named battles, so the layer carries no battle name. That absence is deliberate and residents are comfortable with it. What the layer commemorates is not an enemy but a fault, and the fault has a fix standing next to it.

Adaptive Countermeasure Grid.description: Countermeasures that adapt, built from what Contair learned about how attackers adapted first. What the countermeasures are, what they do, what triggers them and how the adaptation works is deliberately undescribed, and no weapon, effect or mechanism appears anywhere in the record. The grid presents as structure rather than as equipment, integrated into the Shell's layered faces and giving no external indication of state. The unsettling story lives here rather than in any invasion: an old layer activating for a threat category nobody remembers creating. A system that has been revised for centuries accumulates answers to questions its current custodians never asked, and the Shell has never been fully re-read from the beginning.

Surface Sensor Field.description: Threat detection running across the Shell, and one of the things Vexorath legitimately monitors, because Outer Shell conditions are systems rather than private lives. There is nothing to look at: the field is distributed through structure that gives no indication of what it is doing, and the walk beside it is as unremarkable as any other. Range, resolution, what it detects, its false-positive behaviour and who actually watches it are unestablished. False classification is one of the location's own story seeds, not a defect on record. The city's monitoring ideal holds cleanly out here, which is exactly why residents point at the Shell when they want to explain what the ideal is supposed to mean.

Emergency Civilian Shelters.description: Shelters inside the Shell, produced by the lesson Contair kept: how long civilians required to reach shelter. They are plain, prepared spaces with restrained light and visible mechanical purpose, built to be entered quickly by people who are frightened and to be comprehensible once they are inside. Ward-Class units count shelters among their primary locations, which supports their presence without guaranteeing anyone is met on arrival. Evacuations, false alarms and arguments over who was admitted all belong here; no drill routine is established, and shelter count, capacity, supplies and access rules are unrecorded. The shelters are the part of the Shell that is about people rather than about the perimeter, and they are maintained accordingly.

Repair Crawl Network.description: Maintenance access threading through the Outer Shell, running behind and between the layers the Shell has accumulated, which means it passes through structure of very different ages. Hidden damage, forgotten systems, old embedded technology and things found where nothing should be are the stories this network exists for. Whether it is human-accessible, drone-only or mixed, how far it extends and whether anyone works inside it is deliberately unstated. Network is a name, not a map, and no topology, length or connectivity is asserted. The city's self-repairing structural components are a citywide fact and imply nothing about who or what moves through here. It is the one part of the Shell nobody claims to have seen all of.

Dravon Attack Archive.description: The Shell's own record of Dravon assaults, held inside the structure that absorbed them, because each assault taught Contair something it kept. Holding the record in the wall rather than in a library is the argument: this is evidence in the place where the evidence happened. It is distinct from Chronicle Hall's Restricted Dravon Archive with no relationship asserted between them, and the permanent Contair bar is not softened by it. House Dravon receives no entry, support, maintenance or technology transfer, and that is a historical boundary rather than a policy awaiting revision. Holdings and access are both unrecorded, and whether the archive is public at all is not established.

Shell Observation Walk.description: An observation walk along the Outer Shell, good for perspective and for the kind of quiet conversation about what the city cost that nobody starts indoors. The walk is plain and functional, a surface, a rail, restrained light, and the Shell's own layered face standing beside it the whole way. Its length, what is actually visible from it, whether it is public and whether visitors may use it are all unstated; no sightline, elevation or view is asserted anywhere in canon. What residents come out here for is not the view but the position, the sense of standing on the accumulated answer to several centuries of people assuming a small House could be taken. The conversations tend to be quiet and to run long.

Chronicle Hall.name: Chronicle Hall
Chronicle Hall.basicInfo: Chronicle Hall holds Vexorath's survival memory, engineering history, public education and civic identity, and it is reflective, precise and proud without boasting. The building is quieter than the rest of the city and lit the way the rest of the city is lit, restrained and internal, pale structural frames over charcoal recesses with the cobalt guidance lines running softer here than they do on a working floor. Contair preserves failed designs as carefully as successful ones, because failure is evidence rather than shame, and the Hall is where that principle becomes a public institution rather than a working habit. Galleries, archives, a teaching court and a memorial share the same building. This is historical and cultural rather than a military archive, and not every archive space is a hidden conspiracy: one holding inside it is restricted and the rest of the Hall is openly public, which is the ordinary shape of a civic institution rather than evidence of anything. The city's own line runs underneath all of it, that nothing fails the same way twice, and the Hall is the proof that somebody wrote down why. Residents bring visitors here when they want to explain why Vexorath is the way it is.
Chronicle Hall.hiddenInfo: This is a historical and cultural institution rather than a military archive, and nine of its ten spaces are openly public. The one restricted holding is the Restricted Dravon Archive, and restriction there is consistent with Contair's ordinary classification of technology by risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden — Dravon material is all four. Restricted is not secret, and this is not a conspiracy vault; the Hall's public function survives it intact. It is distinct from the Outer Shell's Dravon Attack Archive, with no relationship between them asserted, and the permanent Contair bar on Dravon is not softened. The Hall's standing brief covers drone evolution, failed systems, personhood disputes and the history of constructs created in response to attacks — which of its ten areas holds which is not established. The Chronicle's own entry for Vexorath's first recorded assault reads simply as not named, and no attacker, date or battle name has been invented to fill it.

First Assault Gallery.description: The earliest recorded assault on Vexorath, kept as a public gallery rather than buried. The room is plainly arranged and unheroic, exhibits set at reading height under restrained light, with no attempt to stage a battle out of what is fundamentally an account of a failure and its repair. For centuries Contair was treated as a desirable target by houses assuming technical brilliance could not compensate for limited population. Which assault, when and by whom is not established; the conflict record's entry for it reads as not named, and the gallery does not pretend otherwise. Visitors expecting a story with a villain in it find instead a very careful account of what did not hold, and residents seem to prefer it that way.

Failed Design Archive.description: An archive of failed designs, preserved as carefully as the successful ones, because failure is evidence rather than shame. The holdings are shelved and terminalled in a quiet reading space with worktables, ordered by whatever the Hall orders them by and not arranged to flatter anyone. Vexorath's conflict history is itself recorded as a failure-analysis series held by this Hall, though which area holds it is not established. Distinct from the Learning Annex's teaching library, with no shared collection or transfer between them. Holdings, arrangement, access and whether living designers' failures are included are all unstated, which makes the last of those an interesting question to ask a Contair out loud.

Breakthrough Record Hall.description: A hall recording Contair breakthroughs, carefully. Rezulith perfected the modern Lunar Gate standard, but the planetary network itself is generations of Contair engineering, and the Hall's own tonal instruction is proud without boasting. The room is spare rather than triumphal, exhibits spaced under restrained light with the attribution set out in full rather than reduced to a name. Vexorath must never become a setting that exists only to showcase one person, and the attribution here is handled with that in mind. What is displayed, who curates it and how credit is apportioned are unestablished, and no specific breakthrough is assigned to this hall. The effect is a room that is quietly certain of itself and declines to raise its voice.

Survivor Testimony Chamber.description: A chamber for survivor testimony, the part of a historical institution that holds people rather than systems or designs. It is small and low-lit, seating that adjusts, nothing on the walls competing for attention, and a quiet that is structural rather than requested. Whose testimony, in what form, whether it is recorded or heard live, whether it is public and whether consent governs access are all unestablished. No account is invented here, and no link to Myralis or the Continuum is asserted. What the chamber establishes by existing is that a House which files its failures as evidence also decided that some of the record could not be kept as engineering, and built a different kind of room for it.

Construct Evolution Walk.description: How Contair's constructs developed, laid out as a walk: drone labour became drone security, surface defences led to orbital defences. The walk is linear and unhurried, exhibits at intervals under restrained light, arranged so that the chain of decisions is readable rather than dramatic. The Hall's brief covers drone evolution, failed systems and personhood disputes, though nothing specific is assigned to this walk. Only the current four class names appear, Mote, Ward, Aegis and Echo, and how far back it reaches, which earlier constructs are shown and whether retired units are displayed physically are unstated. The walk makes the city's whole argument in miniature: nothing here was designed from ambition, and everything was designed from a previous problem.

Lunar Gate History Wing.description: The history of the Lunar Gates, exhibited in the city that builds and maintains them. The wing is broad and evenly lit, with the exhibits arranged around the engineering rather than around the politics, which does not stop the politics from showing. The network's weight is visible from every angle: Relstaris's Grand Hub remains dependent on Contair engineering, Quilrath's single gate survives only as legacy Contair infrastructure, and the Helvyra Gate Compact carries Rezulith's signature beside Torvex Corsair's. The modern standard is Rezulith's perfection of generations of Contair work. This wing establishes no destination list for Vexorath's own Gate, and whether any gate technology is displayed at all is unrecorded.

Lumina Reach Foundation Display.description: The station's founding, exhibited on the surface. Lumina Reach ended the era in which attacking Vexorath could be treated as a conventional territorial campaign, and its completion coincided with the end of the Second Dravon Conflict. The display is restrained, arranged around the decision rather than around the spectacle, and it does not attempt to stand in for the thing it describes. It sits in a city where reaching the actual station is never casual; access there follows legitimate purpose and operational responsibility, no standing tour exists, and curiosity alone creates no access up there. What is shown, whether construction records are public and what share of residents ever visit orbit are all unestablished.

Public Lesson Court.description: Where the Hall teaches, with historical attack records sitting openly in the city's curriculum. The court is a modular open space with seating that adjusts and room to gather around whatever is being explained, lit plainly and built for talking rather than for reverence. It is distinct from the Learning Annex's explanation stage, two separate education spaces in two different locations, with no relationship and no exclusivity claimed for either. Who teaches here, whether school visits are scheduled and whether visitors may attend is unstated. What the court is for is straightforward and slightly unusual: teaching a city's children exactly how their city was attacked, and what was rebuilt afterwards.

Restricted Dravon Archive.description: The Hall's restricted Dravon holdings, restricted because Dravon material scores on every Contair classification axis: risk, reproducibility, political consequence, maintenance burden. The entrance is unremarkable, a closed face in a public building, with no theatre made of it in either direction. Restricted is not secret and this is not a conspiracy vault; nine other areas of a public institution surround it, and the Hall's public function runs first. Who may access it, on what authority, and whether Dravon knows it exists, is unrecorded. The permanent Contair bar is not softened by anything held here, and the worry that gives the archive its edge runs the other way, toward Dravon-derived material turning up somewhere it should not.

Memorial Repair Bench.description: A memorial whose name puts remembrance and Vexorath's repair-centred language in the same phrase, standing on a history of loss turned into structure. It is plain and unornamented in the city's own materials, sited where people can stop at it without making an occasion of stopping. Who it memorialises, whether anyone repairs anything at it, whether any ritual attaches to it, and whether it is one bench or a form the city repeats are all deliberately unanswered, as is what mourning looks like in Vexorath at all. No inscription is recorded. What is certain is the phrasing, which a House that turns every failure into the next design would not have chosen by accident.

Rezulith's Workshop.name: Rezulith's Workshop
Rezulith's Workshop.basicInfo: The Workshop is an independent central complex and a living extension of Rezulith Contair's mind: corridors move, tool platforms reconfigure, and entire rooms may be reassigned between visits, so nobody who works here carries a reliable plan of it in their head. It holds the Lumina Core, advanced research, restricted fabrication, the family residence and the private link to orbit, amid suspended work platforms, layered tool arms and large prototype silhouettes. The light is restrained and comes from the work rather than from the architecture, the surfaces are pale where they are finished and open where they are not, and the repair channels are less channels than exposed working anatomy. Rezulith holds final technical authority over the Lumina Core, Lunar Gate integrity, the Outer Shell, citywide defence and anything capable of threatening the wider Contair network, and she is the greatest technical authority in Vexorath without being its sole social authority. The tone is brilliant, shifting, controlled chaos inside precise systems. Reaching the Workshop is not the same as entering it, and being inside it is not clearance for anything within it. Paul Thovex lives with all of this and still tells her when a perfect design makes no sense to an ordinary person.
Rezulith's Workshop.hiddenInfo: Rezulith holds final technical authority over the Lumina Core, Lunar Gate integrity, the Outer Shell, citywide defence, and anything capable of threatening the wider Contair network — she is the greatest technical authority in Vexorath, but not its sole social authority, and her flaw is assuming sufficient understanding makes every decision obvious. The Private Lunar Gate Wing is the restricted surface link to Lumina Reach and is not part of Nexara's public network: nothing about it is self-service, reaching Vexorath puts nobody within reach of it, and standing inside the Workshop is not the same as being cleared to use it — approval is settled before a guest arrives, as a station-operations matter rather than an audience with Rezulith. Two things stay unresolved on purpose. The Seris Transfer Bay's function is undefined: what transfers, in which direction, and why is deliberately unanswered, and a bay bearing Seris's name sits inside the Workshop she does not live in. And Lumina Minor keeps changing Workshop systems without using Rezulith's preferred architecture.

Lumina Core Chamber.description: The Lumina Core itself, the deep independent power source the city built because it could not depend on anyone else's. The need for independent power is what produced it, and the chamber is built around that fact rather than around display. What the Core is, how it works, what it powers, its output and its failure modes are all deliberately undescribed; even Relstaris lists it among the planet's notable things without explaining it, and nothing in the chamber offers an explanation either. Authority over what happens in this chamber rests with Rezulith alone. Vexorath City's Lumina Core Indicator Court is a separately named area associated with an indicator, not this chamber, and contains no part of the Core. The whole of the city's independence rests on something nobody describes.

Private Lunar Gate Wing.description: The restricted surface link to Lumina Reach, outside Nexara's public Gate network entirely. Nothing about it is self-service: reaching Vexorath puts no traveller within reach of it, and standing inside the Workshop is not clearance to use it. Approval is separate from ordinary Vexorath entry, is a matter of station operations rather than a personal audience with Rezulith, and is settled long before anyone arrives here. For station residents and assigned personnel it is simply the way back, which is the half that keeps orbit inhabited rather than merely defended. It is entirely separate from the Gate District's public platform, and no route, duration or mechanism is recorded for it anywhere. Who grants approval, and how often it is refused, is unstated.

Rezulith's Main Fabrication Floor.description: Where Rezulith actually works: restricted fabrication in a room whose layout may not be the same twice, under suspended platforms and layered tool arms that reposition themselves around whatever is currently being built. The light is thrown by the work, the pale surfaces are interrupted by open mechanism, and nothing is arranged for a visitor's comfort because visitors are not the point. What is fabricated, who else works here and whether Seris ever uses it is unestablished, and no project or prototype is on record. This is where Paul Thovex tells her that a technically perfect design makes no sense to an ordinary person, and it is also where Lumina Minor is liable to have changed something without using Rezulith's preferred architecture.

Seris Transfer Bay.description: The name is canon; the function is not. What transfers, in which direction, between what and what, by whom, how often and why are all deliberately unanswered, and the obvious chain from Seris to Lumina Minor is unsupported and not drawn. It is Lumina Minor's approved portrait setting, which is a setting assignment and defines nothing about the room. Worth noticing without asserting anything: a bay carrying Seris Contair's name sits inside the Workshop she chose not to live in, and her workplace, schedule and frequency of use here are all unestablished. The tension in that is already latent in canon rather than invented, and nothing in the bay resolves it one way or the other.

Lumina Major Interface Chamber.description: A Workshop chamber named for Lumina Major, a named synthetic individual and not equipment. Whether it is a point of contact with her, a space she occupies, or a systems interface associated with her is undefined; Interface is in the name, and that is name-evidence and nothing stronger. No mechanism, presence model or remote-operation scheme is stated anywhere. It is distinct from the station's own hub named for her, one on the surface and one in orbit, and she is not duplicated as two individuals. Her boundaries hold under either reading: she may refuse requests for personal information even where she has access, including requests from Rezulith, and a refusal of that kind is personhood rather than a security decision.

Restricted Cold Storage.description: Restricted cold-storage vaults, named among the complex's defining visual features, presenting as closed pale faces with the mechanism of their own sealing left visible in the Workshop's usual manner. What is stored, at what temperature, why cold is required and who may enter are deliberately unstated, and whether anything biological is held is not answered. No Myralis material is here: the Continuum keeps independent patient records, and Echo source data stays separate by rule and is sealed or destroyed under its original authorisation. In a complex where rooms may be reassigned between visits, a set of vaults that stays closed regardless is conspicuous, and residents who work here have noticed without learning anything by it.

Prototype Containment Hall.description: A containment hall for prototypes, among the large silhouettes that give the complex its skyline. Inside, the scale is the first thing: shapes held under restrained light, their outlines legible and their purposes not, with the containment structure itself reading as deliberate engineering rather than as storage. What is contained, what containment consists of, why anything requires it and whether anything in here is currently dangerous are all deliberately unanswered. Contair classifies technology by risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden; some of it ends up behind this door. No prototype is named or described anywhere, and no relationship to any other Workshop space is asserted.
paths: Paul Thovex's modified storage pod marked “Possible Further Use”

Deep Systems Observatory.description: An observatory for deep systems, in a city that legitimately monitors structural stress, station communication and active technical failures as systems rather than private lives. The room is dark-surfaced and quiet, the light coming from the work in front of whoever is doing it, built for long attention rather than for an alarm. What deep systems refers to, whether the Core, the citywide network, the Shell, the station link or something else, is undefined, as is what is observed here and by whom. It is not the station's survey work, and no relationship to the station's deep-space chambers is established. The name promises an explanation the Workshop has never given, which is characteristic of the place.

Rezulith's Residence.description: Rezulith Contair's residence, inside the Workshop rather than apart from it, and domestic in a complex that is otherwise entirely working space. Paul Thovex is her partner; their daughter Seris lives in the Residential District by choice, which is a practical boundary rather than a rift. Who else lives here, whether Paul resides here and whether the residence stays put when the corridors move are all unstated. No family estrangement is implied by any of it, and the Workshop being described as a living extension of her mind is the location's tone rather than a statement about her household. The ordinary fact underneath is simply that the greatest technical authority in Vexorath goes home without leaving the building.
paths: Paul Thovex's modified storage pod marked “Possible Further Use”

Paul Thovex's modified storage pod marke.description: The long-running architectural joke of the Workshop: a modified storage pod still carrying a label that has outlasted its own expiry by a margin Paul finds funnier than he admits. What the pod was, what it was modified into, who wrote the label and whether anyone has ever tried to have it removed are all unrecorded. Paul Thovex is a practical-use reviewer, cross-house procurement contact, and one of the few people willing to tell Rezulith she has designed something nobody can use. He is a member of minor House Thovex, he retains agency, movement, work, relationships and the right to object to Rezulith whatever the architecture around him suggests, and he is not a prisoner, a servant or a domestic prop. He is not stored in it.

Lumina Reach.name: Lumina Reach
Lumina Reach.basicInfo: Lumina Reach is Contair's sovereign orbital station, not a city district and not on the surface at all, but a ring structure in orbit above Nexara, reached by a private gate link rather than by any public route. Curved rings, white-cobalt armour, elegant docking structures, rotational residences and broad views of the planet make it calm, elegant, watchful and self-contained, and the visual clutter the surface tolerates is simply absent here: quiet automation corridors, contained defence systems, and light kept low enough that the planet stays the brightest thing in most rooms. Solanis Contair manages station operations, automation and scheduling, and people genuinely live and work up here. The station is neither closed nor public. Access follows legitimate purpose and operational responsibility rather than surname or social standing, so being Contair bypasses nothing, curiosity creates no access, no standing tour programme exists, and House Dravon's permanent denial remains controlling. Residents and assigned personnel treat the gate as a commute. Lumina Reach is also the reason attacking Vexorath stopped being something a house could plan as a territorial campaign, and it carries that fact without ever mentioning it.
Lumina Reach.hiddenInfo: The station is neither closed nor public: access follows legitimate purpose and operational responsibility rather than surname or social standing, so being Contair bypasses nothing, curiosity creates no access, and no standing tour program exists. House Dravon's permanent denial remains controlling. Authorised visits, docking coordination and ordinary access decisions sit with Solanis or with station systems under him and do not routinely climb to Rezulith, who engages where access becomes a genuine technical or defensive question. Lumina Major is central to station life but is not equipment and is not the gatekeeper — when she declines something asked of her directly, that is personhood rather than security policy. The Orbital Defense Ring, Solanis Command Gallery, sensitive fabrication, Deep-Space Sensor Hall and Emergency Isolation Sector stay restricted absent a justified operational purpose. Known Space routes, traffic and politics remain deliberately undeveloped, and Solanis has already found a deep-space traffic pattern that does not match known routes.

Lumina Major Operational Hub.description: Lumina Major's operational centre aboard the station, where canon places her. She has persistent identity, social judgment, independent preference, continuity of memory, relationships not reducible to assignments, and operational authority residents accept, plus the standing ability to redirect Aegis units to preserve life in an immediate emergency. She may coordinate systems and drones without being the property of any of them, and named synthetics are not commanded as equipment. A hub named for her does not make her the hub. It is distinct from the Workshop's chamber that also carries her name, and she is not duplicated as two individuals. What the hub physically consists of, whether she is always present and who else may enter is unestablished.

Solanis Command Gallery.description: Solanis Contair's command space, restricted unless a separately justified operational purpose requires access. He values routine, automation discipline, station continuity and the invisible work that keeps orbital life uneventful, and the gallery reflects that: quiet, ordered, low-lit, built for a shift that is meant to be uneventful and is staffed as though it will not be. He may command station-defence formations, and authorised visits and docking coordination sit with him or with station systems acting under him rather than climbing to Rezulith. What he can order without Rezulith is not stated, and neither is who else staffs the gallery or what is actually done in it.

Orbital Defense Ring.description: The station's defensive systems, and the reason attacking Vexorath stopped being a conventional territorial campaign. Surface defences led to orbital defences, and Aegis units list Lumina Reach among their primary locations, though Aegis use outside Contair territory requires extraordinary authorisation and never extends to routine civic enforcement. What the defences are, their range, capability and coverage are deliberately undescribed, and no statistic exists. Explicitly restricted. The ring reads as structure rather than as armament, contained and integrated into the station's own curve, which is consistent with a House that would rather a defence be unnoticed than be admired.

Nexara Observation Deck.description: Where residents and visitors look down at the planet, through broad views of Nexara and open space. The deck is kept dim so the view is the brightest thing in it, with curved white-cobalt structure framing the glass and seating that adjusts to whoever stops. It is named among the spaces that may be visitor-compatible when a visit genuinely requires them, a permission conditional on purpose rather than a guarantee anyone gets in. Its size, whether it ever closes, and what is visible at a given moment are all unstated. Station residents use it as a room rather than an occasion, which is the clearest evidence available that people actually live here rather than merely working a posting.

Deep-Space Survey Chamber.description: A survey chamber for the station's deep-space work: navigation, orbital safety, future colonies and long-range preparation. It is a working room of terminals and quiet, the light kept low for reading, with the station's minimal visual clutter carried through so that nothing competes with the work. It is a distinct area from the Sensor Hall, and any division of labour between them is deliberately undefined; no sensing-versus-interpretation split is asserted, and this chamber's own access status is not recorded. What has been found, and whether findings are public, nobody states. Known Space routes, traffic and politics remain deliberately undeveloped, so what the chamber is actually looking at is an open question.

Docking Spine.description: Working infrastructure for authorised orbital docking, logistics, approved outside deliveries, service activity and emergency arrivals. It is the least elegant part of an elegant station, functional structure and hard surfaces where the rest of the ring curves, built for cargo and for crews who are not staying. One lock governs everything here: permission to dock is not permission to enter Lumina Reach. A crew may arrive, transfer cargo, take service or shelter without any access to the interior, and crew access beyond appropriate docking or reception space needs its own purpose and authorisation. A Corsair delivery establishes no standing arrangement, berth, office or unrestricted access. Berth count and traffic volume are unrecorded.

Rotational Residential Ring.description: Residential space aboard the station, and the thing that keeps Lumina Reach an inhabited place rather than a security menu. The ring is domestic in a way nothing else up here is, warm light, ordinary furniture, the white-cobalt structure softened by whatever people have done to their own quarters. People whose home or work is in orbit live here, and for them the private gate is simply the way back. Meals, families, arguments and off-shift time all happen in rotation. Population and family composition are unstated, as is whether children live aboard, and no rotation rate or physical effect is described. Selected residential and social spaces may be visitor-compatible when a visit genuinely requires them, and family aboard is one of the named purposes.

Deep-Space Sensor Hall.description: The station's deep-space sensing infrastructure, explicitly restricted unless a separately justified operational purpose requires access. The hall is dark and quiet, the instrumentation integrated into the station's structure rather than mounted on it, the kind of room where the only light is the work. Sensor range, resolution, capability and what has been detected are deliberately undescribed, as is any division of labour with the survey chamber. Somewhere in this work Solanis found a pattern in deep-space traffic that does not match known routes; canon places that detection in no particular room, and nothing has been concluded from it. Known Space itself stays deliberately undeveloped, which is the honest shape of the problem.

Station Fabrication Bay.description: A fabrication bay in orbit, consistent with a House that values independence and redundancy enough to duplicate capability rather than depend on a gate. It is a working space in a station built for calm, contained and tidy by the standards of the surface Yards, with tool frames and stock stowed against the curve of the structure. The restricted list names sensitive fabrication rather than the bay as a whole, and no line between sensitive and ordinary work is drawn here, so its access status is genuinely undefined. What is made, who staffs it, and why fabrication happens in orbit at all, is unstated, along with any relationship to the Fabrication Yards on the surface.

Private Gate Arrival Chamber.description: The station-side arrival space of the private gate system, and for residents and assigned personnel a doorway home or to work rather than a public checkpoint; station life runs on that ordinariness. The chamber is plain and calm, white-cobalt structure with restrained light and nothing arranged to impress an arrival. It corresponds functionally to the Workshop's Private Lunar Gate Wing and nothing more is recorded between them, with no adjacency, duration or mechanism stated anywhere. A guest's approval is settled before they reach the Workshop rather than argued at a threshold, and what that means for procedure here is not stated. Station systems log gate activity, because that is a system, and the rule about recording systems rather than private lives does not stop at the atmosphere.

Emergency Isolation Sector.description: Isolation during an emergency, explicitly restricted. In a genuine emergency normal access may narrow, pause or redirect, and visitors may be moved or held somewhere safe; those restrictions stay temporary and subject to the same later review expected anywhere in Vexorath, because emergency control everywhere in this civilisation is temporary and reviewed afterward. Being held somewhere safe is not detention. What it isolates against is undefined, whether contamination, decompression, hostile boarding, systems failure or something else, and no hazard, capacity or procedure is described. House Myralis holds a standing emergency clinical-response pathway to the station, which creates no permanent Myralis territory, clinic or routine presence in orbit.

Known Space Preparation Deck.description: The station's forward-looking space, left open toward a future that has not been written. Contair serves off-world customers without treating origin as a status marker and observes deep space for navigation, orbital safety, future colonies and long-range preparation, and this deck is where that intention has been given a room rather than a plan. What preparation consists of, and whether anyone has ever left from here, is deliberately unanswered. Known Space routes, traffic, politics and access relationships remain undeveloped, and no routine direct off-world arrival at Lumina Reach is established. The deck is a door the civilisation has built and not yet opened, which is a very Contair way to prepare for something.

The Handoff.name: The Handoff
The Handoff.basicInfo:
The Handoff is the local nickname for the Dustfall-facing Separate Accord support outpost on the corridor, a mixed settlement of inherited service structures and newer modular shelters. Old footings and reused plating carry shelters, dwellings and service rooms added by whoever needed them, and the whole place is kept sealed, swept and maintained against the same dry wind that scours the frontier either side of it. A small permanent core of care workers, maintainers, coordinators and households serves a much larger rotating route population. It is not a headquarters, holds no corridor territory, has no central leader and recruits nobody: receiving help here or selling supplies here makes a person nothing in particular. Responsibility attaches to specific tasks rather than to standing authority, and a resident who disagrees is not expelled or reclassified. The original builder, founding date and deep provenance remain unassigned, and the repairs carry dates and present maintainers instead of a founding story. Its promise is modest: put the burden down, get an honest account of what help exists, and make the next decision with something other than fear available.

Work on offer here: The Handoff — Before the Food Runs Out.
The Handoff.hiddenInfo: The settlement's central argument is how to remain useful without letting usefulness become ownership, and every delay here becomes somebody else's washing, repair, meal or missed sleep. Both Archive and Edge people receive help here and neither wing commands the other; the place is no headquarters, holds no corridor territory and keeps no master registry of protected people or cells. The Exchange Bench deliberately refuses to join its supply receipts to its lists of travellers, and Archive members handle their own protected material through their own cells rather than through the Bench. Care is given by clinical need rather than usefulness to either wing, which regularly means a wounded Edge fighter and a frightened escapee are treated in the same room. Responsibility attaches to specific tasks, not to permanent authority: a clinician directs treatment, a maintainer can isolate unsafe equipment, and a dissenting resident is not expelled, recruited or classified as disloyal. Funding is donations, purchased services, household contributions and paid supply contracts, and residents may decline a donor's terms that would compromise care or private shelter. The outpost's original builder, founding date, capacities and census are unassigned, and its repairs have dates and present maintainers rather than a founding story.

The Receiving Apron.description: A covered receiving space with adjustable markers separating an active cargo movement from a pedestrian conversation, and a clear surface route through to shelter and care. The cover is inherited structure patched with newer panel, the ground beneath it is hard and level, and the markers are moved by hand through the day as loads and people take turns with the space. Nobody has to demonstrate flight, lift a crate or explain an injury to earn a place to sit. Crews arrive dusty and behind schedule, families arrive on foot, and both are met the same way. An arrival board shows what is open; it never displays a household's identities or route history.

The Exchange Bench.description: A practical workroom of separable conversation spaces and one ordinary table whose replaceable top carries too many repairs. Partitions slide to make a private corner or open the room out, the lighting is even rather than bright, and the equipment is current and maintained rather than improvised. Consent conversations, cargo receipts, held messages and disputes over terms are handled here, with the minimum recorded for the particular service and the supply receipts deliberately kept unjoined to any list of travellers. Workers help people understand the actual terms before accepting a bargain, and a companion or a pause can be requested.

The Care Room.description: A permanent treatment space with adaptable supports, clean supply storage, privacy partitions and a separate recovery corner, maintained because cleaning and checking it is real work that somebody does on a schedule. It is the best-sealed room in the settlement and the best lit, and the supplies are counted rather than assumed. Ordinary illness, wound care, stabilisation and recovery happen within actual supplies and competence; this is not a full hospital and nobody pretends otherwise. Care goes by clinical need rather than by usefulness to anyone, which regularly means two people with nothing in common recovering side by side. Its reassuring feature is a clear account of what happens next, not a promise that nothing hurts.

The Common Table.description: An efficient shared kitchen opening onto tables that can be rearranged without moving the whole room, supplied by preserved ingredients, Terva preparations and cultured protein. The cooking equipment is good and heavily used, the storage is maintained, and the room runs warm and loud through the meal hours and quiet the rest of the time. Portion planning respects medical needs and stock; an injured traveller acquires no labour debt by eating. Residents and route crews eat at the same tables, children get fed first and helped with lesson work afterwards, and arguments about the rota are conducted in public. Somebody always saves the crisp end of the Terva bread for a friend, and somebody always complains about it.

The Household Walk.description: Modular dwellings and guest sleeping spaces strung along a shared interior passage with places to stop without blocking movement. The passage is wide enough for two and lit low along its length, with the dwellings opening off it behind doors that close properly and guest spaces curtained rather than sealed. Washable curtains, display strips, repaired toys and drying clothes make residence visible; private rooms stay homes even when a convoy arrives. Households here are permanent in a place most people pass through, which makes the ordinary evidence of family life the strongest thing the settlement has to offer an arrival. At quiet hours the lighting softens and receiving work is kept outside the sleeping spaces.

The Repair Bay.description: Compatible tools, isolated work surfaces, component storage and tested equipment awaiting collection, with urgent service work kept separate from private jobs. The bay is roofed, floored in plate and organised to a standard that survives busy days, with the component storage labelled in more than one hand because more than one person maintains it. Estimates are explained and unsafe equipment is marked rather than quietly returned, and a maintainer can isolate something dangerous without asking anyone's permission. Route crews queue here alongside residents and are not given priority for being armed. Stock is finite: the Bay can repair, adapt or arrange outside work, and cannot conjure a missing medicine or Gate component out of scrap.

The Service Spine.description: The restricted maintenance space holding water treatment and recovery equipment, stored potable supply, sanitation and power distribution, with clean and waste handling kept apart. It runs behind the inhabited rooms as a plated corridor of tanks, filters and distribution panels, warm, loud and entered only by the people who maintain it. The equipment is advanced and the constraints are parts, time and attention rather than capability. A plain-language board outside reports available service, known faults and the next practical action, updated by whoever last worked in there. Residents mostly experience it as ordinary reliability, until a fitting stops clicking behind a wall.

The Rest and Departure Room.description: A sheltered shared room of flexible seating, a lesson surface, small recreation equipment and a departure-preparation corner, and a living room for most of its day. The seating is mismatched and comfortable, the lesson surface gets used by children in the morning and by adults planning a run in the afternoon, and the room is warm enough in the evening that people stay in it past any reason to. Crews trade stories, residents argue over a game, somebody rehearses a lesson to unwanted advice. Before a departure, destination, cargo, care needs and warnings are confirmed with the passenger, dated and attributed.

Skyhook Docks.name: Skyhook Docks
Skyhook Docks.basicInfo: The city's aerial cargo terminal on the upper east terrace, where containers move between barge, warehouse, Waypoint and air. The skyhooks themselves are tall smart-cable crane towers whose slow arcs are visible from every terrace in Helvyra, and those arcs are the city's constant motion: while a hook is swinging, Helvyra is working. Flight is the normal approach for the people who work here, and the edges are open, with lifts and ramps for everyone else. Direct cable transfer runs down to the Barge Quays and across to the Grand Waypoint, which makes the docks the upper half of the seam joining river freight to everything else. Riggers, crane crews, load certifiers and flight-cargo handlers work until late, in rope-tan and weathered copper under a sky that is rarely still this high on the terraces. Corsair runs the operation, the Common Scale grades the loads and the Bank Wardens hold crane discipline authority, and certification is taken with total seriousness on the plain principle that a rigger who signs a hook stands under it. The wind is the permanent argument and the drop is the permanent fact, and neither is treated as dramatic by anyone who has worked a full shift up here.
Skyhook Docks.hiddenInfo: Petch Immar refuses to certify a hook he would not stand under, and his record wall shows the refusals as prominently as the approvals, which is why his last refusal has not been overruled despite the schedule pressure behind it. A rigging failure here recently was not a failure in the way the incident report describes, and the discrepancy sits between the Counterweight House's load calculation and what was actually lifted. Cargo has been diverted mid-transfer on the cable runs at least once, which is only possible with cooperation at both ends. Juna Dray is testing for her first solo certification with the whole river watching from below and her grandmother pointedly not: the Drays are three generations on the water and she wants the air, which reads in the family as defection rather than ambition. The Bank Wardens hold crane discipline authority up here, and Common Scale grading governs every load, so a bad certification implicates three institutions at once.

Main Load Apron.description: A broad composite deck where containers land, are logged and go straight back out on cable. Load frames, grade markings, and a shadow crossing the apron every forty seconds as something passes overhead. Crews work to hand signals as much as voice, because the cable gear drowns out anything short of a shout. The deck is marked out in the standardised route colour-codes, worn thin along the lanes the traffic actually takes and bright everywhere else, and the grade markings are repainted more often than anything else on the terrace. Containers come up from below on the gantry runs and in from the air on their own frames, read and logged and dispatched without a hand touching them.

Hook Towers.description: The skyhooks themselves: smart-cable crane towers stepped along the terrace edge, each with its own crew, its own reputation and its own logged service history. Climbing one is routine for riggers and a test of nerve for everyone else. From the tower heads the whole river reads as a single working system. The towers are the tallest working structures on this terrace and are built to be read from a distance, their arcs slow enough to look effortless and heavy enough to be felt through the deck. Each carries its certification record posted at the foot, and crews compare them the way other trades compare results. A tower taken out of service is called across the apron, because the schedule reshuffles around it at once.

Counterweight House.description: The machinery hall behind the towers, warm with running systems and stacked with the mass that makes the arcs safe. Load calculations are checked here before a hook lifts, and a disagreement over a figure stops the work entirely. The floor carries balance lines that nobody is permitted to stand across. Enclosed, it is the only warm place on the terrace and loud in a different register from the apron: a continuous low working hum rather than the clatter of transfer. Crews come in off the wind to check a figure and stay a minute longer than they need to. Stopping the work over a disputed number costs the schedule and is done anyway, and the stoppage is written up whether or not the number was wrong.

Certification Office.description: Where loads are graded and riggers signed off, under the rule that whoever certifies a hook stands under it. Petch Immar keeps this office and refuses more often than the schedule would like. The record wall shows every certification and every refusal, which is precisely why the refusals carry the weight they do. The office is small, plain and glazed toward the apron so the work being certified can be seen from the desk, and it smells of the outside because the door stands open most of the day. Common Scale grading applies to every load and the Bank Wardens hold crane discipline over the whole terrace, so a certification here answers in three directions at once.

Riggers' Commons.description: The crew room: hot drinks, gear lockers, a repair bench and the running argument about wind behaviour on the upper terrace. Apprentices get told what they did wrong here rather than out on the apron. A board by the door lists who is on shift, who is grounded and who is testing for certification this week. The room is cramped, warm and comprehensively worn, benches along the walls, harness hung where it can dry, and a kettle that is never off. Gear is repaired here rather than replaced, and a rigger's kit is personal enough that borrowing it is asked for properly. A name appearing under grounded draws no comment in the room and a great deal outside it.

High Edge Walk.description: An open walkway along the terrace lip with nothing between a worker and the drop but competence and wings. It is the fastest route between towers and the main reason the docks look reckless from below. Riggers use it without slowing; visitors are quietly steered toward the inner lifts instead. The walk is narrow, plainly surfaced and entirely unfenced, with the city stepped away below it and the whole interchange visible at once: barges at the quays, gantry runs climbing, the Waypoint roof, the Gate hub ring above. Wind crosses it unbroken and crews pass each other without breaking conversation. Nobody stands on it while a load is passing overhead.

Helvyra Lunar Gate Hub.name: Helvyra Lunar Gate Hub
Helvyra Lunar Gate Hub.basicInfo: Helvyra's Lunar Gate terminus on the highest ring above the terraces, open to the sky with the gate frames set around its inner face and inspection lanes threaded between them. Gates move travellers here, not freight, which is deliberate: Lunar Gates move people, Waypoints move the economy and the Longreach moves the bulk, and the three systems interlock without replacing one another. It is the cleanest and most formal space in a city that is otherwise proudly untidy. The ring sits at the top of the High Hooks, reached by flight or by the terrace lifts, and the approach alone tells an arrival what kind of city this is, since the whole stepped interchange lies below it with the skyhooks turning at eye level. The Helvyra Gate Compact governs the hub: the hub master runs scheduling and compliance while Contair inspection teams work on Compact authority, and the friction between them is permanent, polite and load-bearing. Travellers, house representatives, students arriving for the schools or the Circle and newcomers seeing Helvyra for the first time all come through here. The destination list is exact and closed, and the Dustfall link runs on that settlement's old patched gate and is scheduled around its failures.
Helvyra Lunar Gate Hub.hiddenInfo: Ondrel Vask's manifest archive is complete and has a gap in it: a traveller whose documentation passed every Compact check and whom nobody at either end of the link remembers. He has not reported it, because reporting it hands the matter to the Contair inspection post, and a recent Compact inspection turned up an irregularity that is Contair's own fault and that both sides need never said aloud. The politeness between hub staff and inspectors is real and load-bearing. The Dustfall link runs on that settlement's old patched gate and is scheduled around its failures, so people get stranded here on the concourse with nowhere to be and a great deal of time to talk. The destination list is closed: Relstaris, Solvraxis, Korrvane, Vexorath and Dustfall, never Quilrath, and no direct Ignivex link at all. Anything that arrives claiming another origin is a problem the hub is not equipped to admit exists.

Arrival Ring.description: The inner face of the high ring, gate frames set around it and inspection lanes threaded between them. Arrivals step out into open sky and a view of the terraced city below, which is deliberate: Helvyra introduces itself from above before anyone reaches street level. Staff watch the step-through rather than the traveller. The surfacing underfoot is pale composite kept genuinely clean, unusual in this city, and the only colour on it is the lane marking. Travellers come out into wind and open air with the river a long way down, and an arrival who simply stops walking is stepped around rather than hurried, because the first look costs the hub nothing.

Departure Concourse.description: Ordered lanes, live schedule boards, and a calm no other Helvyran space bothers with. Departures for Relstaris, Solvraxis, Korrvane, Vexorath and Dustfall are called in sequence, and the Dustfall lane is rescheduled more often than the rest combined. Nobody argues here, which visiting Helvyrans find unnatural. The lanes are marked, ordered and queued without anyone shouting, and the boards refresh on the same dawn cycle as the rest of the city while behaving nothing like the boards down on the terraces. Personal effects, mobility aids and bounded traveller-accompanied consignments go through with their owners; anything beyond that is freight, which the staff explain several times a day.

Compact Inspection Lanes.description: Narrow controlled lanes where manifests, permits and persons are checked under Helvyra Gate Compact authority. The work is polite, thorough, and slow enough to be felt. A clean pass is logged; an unclean one goes to the scheduling office rather than the Contair post, and that distinction matters to everyone involved. The lanes are narrow by design, walled to shoulder height, with reader gear at the head of each and a bench at the side for anyone asked to wait. Inspectors work through a manifest at the same unhurried pace whoever is standing in front of them, which is the point of the procedure and the reason it is resented.

Hub Scheduling Office.description: Ondrel Vask's office, walled in live scheduling displays and dominated by the permanent problem of a patched gate at the far end of the Dustfall link. Compliance records, rescheduling, and the diplomacy of telling an inspection team no. The manifest archive here is complete and has one gap nobody can explain. The room is glazed toward the ring so the schedule can be checked against what is actually happening at the frames, and the displays run at a density nobody outside the hub could read. Rescheduling is continuous rather than exceptional, and telling a team that a lane cannot be held is a daily conversation conducted entirely in courtesies.

Contair Inspection Post.description: House Contair's own post, operating on Compact authority rather than Helvyran invitation, with its own equipment and its own reporting line. Relations with hub staff are permanently and precisely polite. What Contair finds is Contair's to report, which is the arrangement that occasionally becomes very awkward indeed. It is a compact, self-contained set of rooms with its own entrance off the concourse, its own reader gear and its own storage, and nothing inside it is Helvyran. Staff from the two sides pass each other constantly and greet each other every time. What the post holds, it holds on its own authority.

Traveller Orientation Deck.description: An open deck where newcomers get the city explained before they descend: terraces, route-boards, the Waypoint taboo, which crossings need a ferry. Students arriving for the schools or the Circle are met here. The view does most of the work, and the briefing mostly stops people doing something expensive in their first hour. The deck is open on the city side with a rail, a bench and a single large display of the terraces, the board conventions and the crossings. Briefings are given aloud to whoever is standing there rather than one at a time, and for most arrivals it is the first Helvyran conversation they have.

The Barge Quays.name: The Barge Quays
The Barge Quays.basicInfo:
The working waterline of the Longreach, serving both banks: stepped composite quays cut with cargo ramps, automated heavy-lifter barges nosing into berth under their own power, and transfer gantries feeding the cable runs up to the terraces. Wet, loud and cold in the mornings. This is Helvyra's primary bulk-freight complex, though not the river's only landing, and smaller landings, ferry crossings and private moorings exist along the water besides. The quays are one complex rather than two facilities, with ramps and lifts running up to the terraces and the west-bank working quarters and cable transfer climbing to the Skyhook Docks. Warehouse frontages along the band log their own contents and argue with clerks about it; wardens' float-craft sit on standing readiness at the current line. Barge families who live aboard, dock crews, warehouse keepers and transfer clerks work here, and the work follows the river rather than the clock: the high season, the low water, the seasonal reopening. Corsair allocates berths, the Bank Wardens hold safety authority, and Common Scale grading applies to bulk cargo. This is the floor the whole city stands on.

Work on offer here: Helvyra — The River Watching (ask Juna Dray).
The Barge Quays.hiddenInfo: Imma Dray refused a rich contract to haul unmarked crates and the client did not take the refusal well, which means the crates found another hull and the Drays are watching the berth line to see whose. Tolvir Nash of the Bank Wardens has a separate open question: cargo went into the river upstream and never surfaced anywhere, which should be impossible on a river the wardens work this closely, and the trackers involved may connect to the non-Dravon signal question Dustfall keeps raising. The self-inventorying warehouse frontages argue with clerks about their own contents as a matter of routine, so a warehouse that has stopped disagreeing has either been corrected or interfered with. Berth allocation is Corsair's and contested daily. First Barge launches from the Low Water Steps with the blessing of the fleet, the high season raises the water over the year-lines, and a barge family inheritance argument is running on the moorings in full view of everyone who ties up there.

Main Berth Line.description: The long stepped quay where automated heavy-lifters come in under their own power and hold station against the current. Berth allocation is Corsair's and contested daily, because a good slot is worth arguing about in public. Cold spray, engine wash, and the specific smell of river water and cargo sealant. The berths step down to the water in composite courses cut with ramps, and a heavy-lifter holding station makes the whole quay vibrate underfoot at a frequency dock crews stop noticing within a season. Barges come and go on the river's schedule rather than the city's, and in the mornings the line is working before the terraces above have finished refreshing their boards.

Bulk Transfer Gantries.description: Heavy gantries that lift bulk off the decks and hand it up to the cable runs climbing toward the Skyhook Docks. This is the vertical seam of the city's entire freight economy. Transfer clerks reconcile counts at the foot of the gantries while the load is already halfway up the terrace above them. The gantries are deliberate machines that make the transfer look slower than it is, and the noise beneath them is the deepest sound in Helvyra. Everything is smart-cable and automated handling rather than muscle, with crews reading grade markings instead of lifting. A gantry stopped mid-cycle backs the berth line up within the hour.

Warehouse Band.description: A frontage of self-inventorying warehouses along the quay, each logging its own contents and entirely willing to disagree with the clerk holding the manifest. Keepers spend as much time reconciling those arguments as moving goods. A warehouse that has stopped disagreeing is either perfectly correct or has been interfered with. The frontages are long, plain and lit from within, opening straight onto the quay so a load can go from deck to store without crossing open ground. Inside, preservation seals and ward-marks on high-value crates are checked as routinely as counts, and the disagreement is usually about grade rather than quantity.

Bank Warden Station.description: Tolvir Nash's station, float-craft on standing readiness at the current line and grapple gear racked by the door. Current rescue, crane discipline, fire watch and drunk retrieval, all of it unarmoured and all of it obeyed. The recovery log on the wall is long, and one page of it concerns cargo rather than people. The station is small, plain and permanently open, built at the current line rather than above it so a launch takes seconds. In the high season it runs on a shorter rotation and the float-craft go out several times a night, most often for people rather than for cargo. Grapple gear, line and float-craft are checked at the head of every rotation and logged on the same wall as the recoveries.

Barge Family Moorings.description: Where the families who live aboard tie up: laundry strung through rigging, children on deck learning current before arithmetic, three generations on one hull. The Drays moor here. Work follows the river rather than the clock, so the moorings empty and refill with the season instead of the day. The moorings are their own small district at water level, hulls tied close enough to step between and rigged with lines that have nothing to do with cargo. Preservation seals and hull marks are renewed at the start of the season by whichever charm-writer the families trust that year, and a family's standing is read off how it ties up.

Ramp Head.description: The top of the cargo ramps, where quay level meets the routes up to the terraces and across to the west-bank working quarters. Handcarts, lifts and foot traffic converge and tangle. It is where somebody up from the Underbank stands to be seen by somebody who needs hands before the shift starts. It is the busiest point on the quays that carries no cargo of its own, a wide junction where everything changes direction, with route colour-codes painted large on the surfacing because the sorting happens at speed. Cold air comes up the ramps off the water even when the terraces above are warm. Nobody works this junction and everybody passes through it, which is why news reaches the quays here first.

Low Water Steps.description: Broad steps the river covers in high season and exposes in low, marked with year-lines the city reads like a ledger. In low water they serve as a landing, a meeting place and a drying yard. First Barge launches from this stretch, and the blessing of the fleet is called from the top step. The steps are broad enough to seat a crowd and shallow enough to work from, cut in the same pale composite as the quays and stained along every line the water has reached. The year-lines are read as a record rather than a warning, and people argue over what a given season's mark meant for the trade that followed it.

The Hauler Yards.name: The Hauler Yards
The Hauler Yards.basicInfo: The road-freight terminal on Helvyra's landward approach, where overland convoys terminate and the farm belt's produce and seasonal labour enter the city. Wide hardstanding aprons, staging lanes marked in route colour-code, open sky and dust. The rhythm here is arrival-and-turnaround rather than the river's tidal patience. This is where the road meets the rest of the interchange: roads come in, and transfer runs down to Routefall Market and the Grand Waypoint, which makes the yards the city's only established contact point with its hinterland. The long low shapes of vehicles built to cross a continent stand uncoupling on the aprons, a produce transfer hall behind them smells of the belt rather than the river, and a hiring wall posts the season's work. Convoy crews come off long hauls, transfer handlers and produce factors work the lanes, and seasonal farmhands arrive for a season and leave again. Corsair route contracts govern the traffic and Common Scale grading governs the produce, while the Bank Wardens have no authority out here at all. It is a freight terminal rather than a traveller terminus, since Lunar Gates are how travellers normally arrive, but nothing about the roads forbids a person walking in on one.
