The shelters are built into the blocks themselves, heat-sealed, stocked and signed with ember-line guidance running to the doors from every direction a resident might come from. Wardens check stock and seals on rotation under Lysa Caldris's coordination. Places are assigned by household rather than taken by whoever arrives first, and a family that turns up at the wrong door during a drill is corrected on the spot and does not forget it. Children are taught the route before they are taught to read the signs on it.

The Fire Markers.description: Neighborhood fire markers stand at the corners of each row, carrying small maintained flames that identify a block and its muster point. They are both practical and traditional. Each marker is a worked stand of dark metal at a row's corner, carrying a small regulated flame and the marks that identify the block, and the nearest households keep the housing clean and the feed clear. Children are shown their own marker before they can reliably find their way home without it. Neighbouring rows notice one another's markers, compare them silently, and say nothing until one goes dark. A marker allowed to go dark is a genuine embarrassment to the households responsible for it.

The Drill Yard.description: An open yard used for civilian alert drills — muster, headcount, route practice and shelter timing. Drills run on a schedule and unannounced. The yard is open and plainly surfaced, muster lines marked into the paving and a warden's position at one end, sited so that every row it serves can reach it without crossing a blocked route. Headcounts are called by household. The timing is recorded and read back afterwards, which is the part residents grumble about and the part that has occasionally saved a row. Residents grumble about them constantly and still turn out, because enough of them remember a raid where the drill was the reason a row emptied in time.

The Supply Caches.description: Secured emergency caches of water, food, treatment kit and heat-safe gear, distributed through the rows and checked on rotation. Stock is logged openly. The lockers themselves are hardened and sealed, set where a household can reach one without crossing open ground, and marked so that anyone can tell at a glance which is which. The checking rotation is public and the list hangs where it can be read. Holding a cache key is a household honour and a household burden at once, which is exactly why it gets argued over. Who gets to hold a cache key is a small but persistent source of neighborhood politics, argued out at the Row Step like everything else.

The Heat-Safe Routes.description: Marked routes through the rows that stay passable when heat conditions spike, kept clear of obstruction by neighborhood agreement. They link housing to shelters and out to the wider city. The routes are marked into the paving and along the walls with ember-line guidance, kept wide enough for a crowd moving quickly and for a stretcher coming the other way. Neighbourhood agreement rather than any posted authority is what keeps them clear. Residents shift stored goods off them without being asked when conditions spike, and the ones who do not are shifted for, by neighbours who do not ask either. Blocking one with stored goods is the fastest way to make enemies of an entire block.

The Row Step.description: The communal step at the head of each row where neighbours settle disagreements in front of whoever is sitting out that evening. Most local grievances end here. It is broad stone, shaded and worn smooth, with room for a dozen people and no formality at all about who may sit on it. Whoever is present says what they think, and being right in front of witnesses counts for more than being right later on. Food usually appears partway through, which residents insist is coincidence and which reliably shortens the argument. The ones that do not become the kind of dispute that reaches the Smoke Court, and the Step usually knows which is which first.

The Low Flame.description: An evening social venue held in the Shared Courtyards on an agreed neighborhood tenancy: a small music floor, courtyard seating, a drink-and-snack counter and a quieter side room. An unnamed civilian host books local musicians for advertised sessions. The venue takes over a court by agreement on advertised evenings, its raised floor set against a wall and the tables arranged so that the through-routes stay clear. Sessions are announced ahead and end at an agreed hour, because the people living around the court have shifts in the morning. Families come early and leave before the later sets. Light is warm and controlled, and the heat-safe routes stay open throughout.

The Smoke Court.name: The Smoke Court
The Smoke Court.basicInfo: The Smoke Court is Ignivex's dispute-settlement chamber — a civic institution rather than a royal court, where people are expected to speak plainly and accept the heat of the truth. Citizens bring personal conflicts, family grievances, public insults, broken agreements and honor disputes here. The Court is a chamber rather than a palace: a level speaking floor with benches ringing it, side rooms for family matters, an antechamber hazed with warm smoke from low vents, and a record desk where what is said on the floor is written down. The stone is dark, the light is muted red, and the acoustics are built to carry a raised voice cleanly to the back rather than to soften it. Ordinary days bring merchants whose dispute outgrew a market bench, neighbours whose argument outgrew a row step, families with grievances they cannot hold at home, and citizens facing public accountability in front of people who know them. What the chamber asks for is plain speech and what it refuses is evasion: a party found at fault is expected to stand and say what they did rather than have it said for them. Proceedings generate records that go on to the city's archive vaults. Selyra Volen serves and speaks in the chamber, and she lets people shout.
The Smoke Court.hiddenInfo: Selyra's method is deliberate: anger reveals the truth faster than politeness, so she permits the shouting and waits. Once the truth surfaces she expects accountability immediately, and excuses do not survive long in her chamber — which is why some parties arrive having rehearsed and leave having admitted something they never meant to say. Ignivex culture backs this up; public argument is not shameful here, and it is normal for two people to shout at each other across the Speaking Floor and eat together afterwards if the truth was reached. The Court is also where the city's other frictions converge. Market disputes that outgrew the Dispute Bench, neighborhood grievances that outgrew the Row Step, and forge accusations of sabotage all arrive as private conflicts with political shadows attached. Proceedings generate records, and the city's archive vaults sit in Meravil Ash Hall, which connects here — meaning the house that counts casualties also holds what was said.

The Speaking Floor.description: The chamber's central floor, open and unraised, where both parties stand at the same level and say their piece. Nobody sits above anyone else. The floor is dark stone, unraised and unfurnished, with benches stepping up around it on every side so that the crowd always sits higher than the people speaking. There is no rail and nothing to stand behind. Parties are placed within arm's reach of each other deliberately, and the chamber treats a case where nobody raises their voice as either already settled or not yet honest. The acoustics carry a raised voice to every bench without distortion, which is the point — the Court is built to be heard, not to be dignified.

Selyra’s Chamber.description: Selyra Volen's own working room off the main floor, where she reads submissions, takes parties aside and decides what a case actually is. It is plain and warm. The room is small and warm, plainly furnished: a working table, submissions stacked in order, water, and seating that puts everybody at the same height. Selyra reads before she speaks and asks short questions. She lets people shout on the floor because anger reveals the truth faster than politeness does, and in here she expects the accountability that is supposed to follow it. People who expected her to be impressed by their standing usually revise that opinion within a few minutes of sitting down in it.

The Grievance Benches.description: Benches where citizens waiting to be heard sit with the people they are about to argue with. Cases are called in order. The benches are long, worn and deliberately undivided, set where the chamber's noise carries out to them. An attendant calls the order and nobody is told how long the wait will be. Water is brought round to everyone at once, which means both parties to a grievance are handed a cup by the same person at the same moment. A surprising number of grievances are settled on these benches before they reach the floor, purely because sitting next to someone for an hour is harder than shouting at them.

The Family Rooms.description: Side rooms used when a dispute is a family matter and a public floor would make it worse. Doors close, but the expectation of plain speech does not change. The rooms are small and screened, with a door that closes, low seating and no bench for spectators, used when airing a matter publicly would do more damage than settling it. A clerk sits in and records; nothing else about the procedure changes. Families who have refused to discuss surrender at their own tables discuss it here, because plain speech is easier to manage in a room that belongs to none of them. These rooms see the Court's hardest conversations, including the ones about surrender that families cannot have at home.

The Accountability Step.description: A single raised step where a party who has been found at fault stands to answer for it in front of the chamber. There is no ceremony to it. The step is a single block of dark stone set at the floor's edge, unmarked and unornamented, low enough that standing on it is visibility rather than elevation. No formula is recited and nobody prompts the words. The chamber simply waits, which is worse than being questioned, and the waiting is the whole of the procedure. Standing on the step and saying plainly what one did is treated as settling the matter; refusing to is remembered far longer than the original offence.

The Waiting Smoke.description: The antechamber, hazed with fine warm smoke from low vents, where parties wait and cool their tempers before being called. The haze softens every face in the room. The antechamber is warm and low-lit, its haze fed from vents at floor level, thick enough to blur a face across the room without ever making it hard to breathe. Benches line the walls and there is nowhere to pace. Parties, relatives and advocates share the space without separation, and the Court's position is that a temper which cannot survive a wait in here was never going to survive the floor. Advocates and relatives use the time to talk people down, with mixed and frequently audible results.

The Record Desk.description: The desk where proceedings are recorded, submissions logged and rulings written up before being sent on to the city's archive vaults. Attendants work steadily through the noise. The desk stands at the chamber's edge in dark wood with bronze fittings, submissions stacked by case, rulings written out in a plain hand before they leave the building. Attendants work through the shouting without looking up. A party may ask what has been written and will have it read back, which has settled more arguments about the record than any seal ever has. What ends up in these records is often the only account of an argument that anyone can later point to.

The Verbal Duel Ring.description: A marked ring where a dispute is settled by formal verbal duel — two parties, strict turns, and the chamber judging who held the truth. It is bruising and entirely legitimate. The ring is marked into the floor in ember line, wide enough for two people to stand apart and not wide enough for either to walk away mid-turn. Turns are strict, an interruption ends a turn, and the chamber judges on the weight of what was said rather than its volume. Duellists shake hands afterwards as a matter of form, sometimes while still furious. Ignivex treats a well-landed word here with the same respect it gives a clean strike in the Crucible Yard.

The Festival Kiln.name: The Festival Kiln
The Festival Kiln.basicInfo: The Festival Kiln is Ignivex's public celebration space: a massive civic ground built to handle controlled flame at scale. Festivals, flame dances, cooking competitions, firework displays, oath ceremonies and endurance games all happen here, drawing citizens from across the city. The Kiln is a single civic ground engineered to take controlled flame at scale: a vast central floor ringed by access ramps, stepped spectator terraces with heat shielding built into the seating, worked channels feeding the flame dance ring, elevated stands for the firework crews, and a sunken hollow at the edge where memorial burns are held apart from everything else. The construction is heavy and plain, dark stone and copper-bronze, and the ground stays warm long after an event has ended. Between events it is swept, checked and largely empty. When it fills, it fills from every district at once: families claiming terrace positions early, cooks setting up working lines, oath-takers waiting with their witnesses, mourners gathering at the hollow. The friction is the crowd and the calendar. The same ground also holds the memorial burns for Ignivex's dead.
The Festival Kiln.hiddenInfo: That double use is the Kiln's character rather than a contradiction — the city celebrates and grieves in one place, sometimes within the same week, and the transition between the two is handled by people who do it often. Emberwake is a citywide remembrance event, not a Kiln monopoly: controlled flames are lit across Ignivex for the dead, lost family, old battles, failed apprentices and past disasters, and the Emberwake Lighting Ground is only this district's part in it. The Cinder Run is likewise not owned here. It is an uncoursed route through heat-heavy districts, vent paths, forge roads, firebreak routes and public stairs, with no fixed start, finish, order or district sequence — the Endurance Ground serves the Kiln's endurance events generally and is not the Run's starting line, whatever competitors claim. Under standing Dravon pressure, a full Kiln is both a morale instrument and a very large gathering of civilians in one place, and both facts are understood.

The Kiln Floor.description: The vast central floor, engineered to take controlled flame at civic scale without damage, ringed by access ramps. Everything large happens on it. The floor is laid in heat-rated stone bedded deep, channel covers set flush into it and ramps rising to it from the terraces, and it is cleared and inspected before anything is lit. Crews mark out the evening's layout in the morning. Sound behaves oddly across a space this size, so callers work from set positions and the crowd learns where to stand in order to hear them. Empty, it feels disproportionate to the city; full, it makes complete sense, and citizens use that contrast to explain Ignivex to visitors.

The Flame Dance Ring.description: The ring where flame dances are performed, with worked channels feeding regulated fire that dancers move through and around. Performances draw dense crowds. Its boundary is raised just enough to read clearly from the terraces, and the cycle the fire runs on is fixed long before an event so that dancers can rehearse against it for weeks. Crews stand at the channel controls throughout with the authority to cut the feed, and they have used it, which the dancers accept without complaint. The dancers' timing is governed by the flame cycle rather than the music, which is why a mistimed step is instantly obvious to everyone watching.

The Great Heat Table Grounds.description: The grounds holding the Kiln's cooking competition, with long working lines and communal tables set beyond them. Cooks compete on heat handling as much as flavour. The grounds hold long working lines with geothermal cooking stations built into them and communal tables set out beyond, where everything produced is eaten by whoever is sitting at them. Competitors bring family recipes and firm opinions about heat rankings. Visiting merchants enter every year and are underestimated by nobody except themselves, because outsiders consistently misjudge what Ignivex means by hot. Spectators taste, judge loudly, and argue about the results for considerably longer than the competition itself lasts.

The Firework Stands.description: Elevated stands from which firework displays are prepared and launched over the Kiln, worked by crews who treat the schedule as sacred. Preparation takes far longer than the display. The stands are elevated platforms at the floor's edge, fenced, cleared and worked only by the crews who prepare them, with stock kept shielded and checked against a list before anything is loaded. Preparation runs for days and is visible from the terraces the whole time. Nobody but the crews is permitted on the stands during setup, a rule enforced politely and absolutely. Children sit along the terraces below during setup, which the crews pretend to find annoying.

The Oath Platform.description: A raised platform where oath ceremonies are spoken in front of witnesses, including the public commitments Ignivex civic life runs on. The wording is plain and the audience close. The platform is raised plain stone with room for the speaker, the witnesses and no one else, set close enough to the terraces that the front rows can read a face. Oaths are spoken in the taker's own words rather than from any set form. The Kiln's crews hold the platform clear beforehand, and a taker who arrives without witnesses is sent to find some rather than heard. An oath taken here is understood to be binding socially long before it is binding in any administrative sense.

The Endurance Ground.description: The Kiln's ground for endurance events generally, laid out for sustained heat trials and stamina competition. Competitors train for it year-round. The surface is marked into runs and stations, weighted equipment stored along the edges and medics posted where they can reach anyone who drops. Entrants are checked before they start and watched throughout. Heat adaptation makes these events possible without making them safe, and most years the medics withdraw competitors over the loud objections of the competitors themselves. It is not the start of the Cinder Run and never has been, though every year someone declares otherwise and is corrected by the crowd.

The Memorial Burn Hollow.description: A sunken hollow at the Kiln's edge where memorial burns are held for the city's dead, shielded from the main floor. Families stand close around the rim. The hollow is sunk below the Kiln's floor and screened from it, reached by a short flight of steps, with a worked basin at the centre and a rim where families stand close together. Nothing is amplified and nobody speaks from a platform. Attendance is by relationship rather than invitation, and people who did not know the dead stay up on the floor above. The hollow is quiet in a way the rest of the district never is, and the ground stays warm for a long time afterwards.

The Emberwake Lighting Ground.description: The Kiln's Emberwake ground, where controlled flames are lit for the dead, lost family, old battles, failed apprentices and past disasters. It is this district's part in a citywide remembrance, not the whole of it. The ground is a marked area kept clear for the lighting, with stands set out for the flames and space for the families who bring them. Preparation is communal and unhurried, and the crews do little more than keep the ground clear and the feeds safe. The Kiln's part of Emberwake is the largest single gathering of the night and not the important one, which is a thing citizens say to visitors and mean. Across Ignivex the same flames go up on the same night, in courtyards and doorways and forge floors.

The Spectator Terraces.description: Stepped terraces ringing the floor, built to hold a substantial share of the city at once, with heat shielding built into the seating. Crowds arrive early for the good positions. The terraces step up in heat-shielded stone with wide walkways behind each tier, water points along them and no assigned places, so position is a matter of arriving early and holding what has been claimed. Families spread along an entire tier. Food is carried in from outside, passed sideways down the row, and pressed on strangers who made the mistake of sitting beside somebody's grandmother. Terrace factions form around particular competitors and carry their loyalties from one festival to the next.

Genesis Compound.name: Genesis Compound
Genesis Compound.basicInfo:
The Genesis Compound is the seat of House Genesis, built partly into the cliff face above the Arena and visible from most of the city below. It is not a palace but a working facility: family residence, training center and administrative heart, finished in dark green, black and bronze-gold with storm-metal columns. Access belongs to House Genesis, its staff and invited guests. Corridors run back into the rock where the weather cannot reach them and out onto tribunal balconies where it does nothing else, and reinforced glass gives almost every room the same view of the combat floor below. Arrival is by rooftop landing pad through the restricted approach airspace, which visitors enter with permission or an escort and never at speed. The daily traffic is administrative before it is martial: staff carrying schedules, petitioners waiting on a ruling, suppliers delivering to the kitchens, crews costing out the next round of repairs to the training ground. Training spaces are built like working halls rather than showpieces, and the house treats visible strength as a civic obligation instead of a luxury. Genesis does not rule from a throne, and nothing here is arranged to suggest one. The compound sits where the ladder's standard is permanently in sight of everyone climbing toward it.

Work on offer here: House Genesis — Word for Word (ask Tacitus Genesis).
Genesis Compound.hiddenInfo: Korrvane is actually governed from a single office here. Tacitus handles minor-house disputes, Arena policy, infrastructure, Contair maintenance relationships, visitor problems and citywide emergencies from a desk that never clears, and the city works because he treats administration as seriously as combat. Ark's presence anchors the city's challenge culture but he does not manage daily rule, and the replacement scheduling for the training ground he keeps breaking is now a routine line item. The compound's deeper undercurrents are personal. Aela Castro cannot fight by meaningful Starian standards and is nonetheless central here, which is the clearest ongoing demonstration that Korrvane can recognize strength outside combat even when its instincts favor visible power. Her Castro ties run into a live rivalry that the house does not discuss casually. Old Dravon conflict resurfaces in the compound's records and in Sorvina's and Orvanus's memory, and challenger invitations issued from the Visitor Hall carry political weight that recipients rarely read correctly. Corvinus maintains the armory to a standard that assumes the next emergency is close.

Main Compound.description: The shared operational and residential center of House Genesis, where administration, family traffic and training schedules cross. Storm-metal columns frame corridors cut back into the cliff, and the drop to the Arena is visible through reinforced glass at every turn. Floors are heavy stone with bronze-black thresholds worn hollow at the busiest doorways, and the wind noise changes audibly whenever an outer door opens. Messengers arrive on the pads above, house staff move between the offices and the kitchens without ceremony, and a maintenance crew is almost always working somewhere in the building. Staff move through it constantly; it is a workplace before it is a symbol.

Ark’s Training Ground.description: A reinforced open training space engineered for Genesis-level force and rebuilt more often than anyone admits publicly. Ark breaks parts of it regularly, and replacement planning has become routine administration rather than a crisis. The floor is anchored stone plated with storm-metal where the loads concentrate, and the perimeter is set well back because the debris does not always stay inside it. Crews arrive with replacement sections on a standing schedule, quietly log what failed and how, and argue about which anchoring method will last longer this time. The surfacing carries layered repair seams like growth rings.

Tacitus’s Office.description: The room where Korrvane is genuinely governed. Minor-house disputes, Arena policy, infrastructure schedules, Contair maintenance relationships, visitor issues and citywide emergencies all land on this desk. It is plain, well used, and busier than anywhere else in the compound; petitioners wait in the corridor with their arguments rehearsed. The desk faces away from the view so the work gets done, and the wall behind it carries the current lane closures and repair schedules rather than anything commemorative. Contair complaints about impact damage arrive here, minor-house objections arrive here, and a house leader who wants something settled quietly discovers it will be settled in front of whoever is next in line.

Residential Quarters.description: Private family housing with enough space and structural reinforcement for Genesis residents who occasionally forget their own strength indoors. The rooms are lived in rather than ceremonial, full of personal clutter and repaired furniture. Doorframes are set into structural stone, the glass is the heavy kind used on the outer balconies, and more than one wall carries a patch that matches nothing around it. Meals get eaten at odd hours because the training and administrative schedules never agree, and the corridors carry arguments, laundry and the sound of someone else's early start. Nothing here is arranged to impress a visitor, because visitors do not come this far in.

The Armory.description: Functional Genesis equipment and combat gear maintained by Corvinus, organized for use rather than display. Everything on the racks is serviced, logged and expected to be taken out again. The room is cut back into the cliff, dry and cool, with storm-metal racking bolted through to the rock and a work counter where repairs are made rather than sent out. Corvinus checks returned gear himself, notes what failed and why, and has a standing opinion about the condition in which items come back to him. Nothing is arranged for effect, and the only ornament in the room is the wear on the tools. Corvinus keeps it to a standard that quietly assumes the next emergency is not far away.

Visitor Hall.description: A formal but comfortable meeting space overlooking the Arena and the city stacked below it. The view does the work a throne room would do elsewhere, stating Genesis position without anyone having to say it. Seating is arranged for conversation rather than audience, the glass runs floor to ceiling along the outer wall, and on bracket days the combat floor is close enough to follow without commentary. Guests arrive by escort through the restricted approach and are received without ceremony, which unsettles some of them more than ceremony would. Challenger invitations and political meetings both happen here, sometimes in the same afternoon.

Younger Member Training Court.description: A controlled court where younger Genesis members learn technique, restraint, public responsibility and what the ladder will expect of them. Instructors spend as much time on restraint as on force, because the family's mistakes are visible citywide. Lane discipline, challenge courtesy and the difference between a declared contest and a civic incident are taught here alongside stance and footwork, and a student who endangers someone loses the floor for the day. The court is enclosed on the cliff side and open to the drop on the other, which teaches its own lesson about where mistakes end up. Sessions end with a review of what would have looked bad from the Arena below.

Household Commons.description: The shared family space that carries meals, arguments, Aela's social presence, Orvanus's commentary and Zephyra's attempted improvements. It is also the site of the recurring mystery of Ark's missing food, which nobody has solved and several people have profited from. The room is warm, heavily furnished and repaired rather than replaced, with a long window onto the city and a kitchen loud enough to be heard from every seat. Conversation runs from bracket results to infrastructure complaints to whatever Orvanus has decided someone needs to hear, and Aela handles the house's gentle ribbing with a composure the rest of the family has learned to respect. The table seats more people than it was built for.

Genesis Embassy.name: Genesis Embassy
Genesis Embassy.basicInfo: The Genesis Embassy is House Genesis's compound on the Concourse, Korrvane's house presence in the capital, and a standing reminder that Castro dominance is stable but not unquestioned. It is physically imposing and unusually open, built around strength presented as service rather than luxury, with training courts for assigned representatives and defenders rather than public tournaments. It does not attempt to recreate the Korrvane Arena, and visitors expecting one are gently corrected. The compound occupies old ground and shows it: heavy Genesis-era footings and supports carry the current buildings, ancient star-metal stands exposed at the wall bases where later facing was deliberately stopped short, and old conduit channels run inside the modern lighting and muster systems. The palette is its own, dark structural stone and unpolished metal against the paler frontages nearby, and nothing about it has been softened to match the shared ground it faces. Corelight reaches the courts through the paving and the lane markings and moves with city routing, brightening as the work period opens and thinning through the maintenance window, which the drill schedule is written around. The public galleries and the court are free to enter, while the house pays for its own training staff, stores, residence and the standing readiness that makes its emergency role credible.
Genesis Embassy.hiddenInfo: Most of the embassy's real work is done by Tacitus while Ark's office stays maintained and largely empty, a protocol fiction the staff manage with practised diplomacy. The Emergency Muster Deck is genuinely operational: Genesis personnel assemble there during capitol emergencies, sometimes before the Republic has formally requested assistance, and that willingness to move first is admired by the public and watched carefully by the Protection Coordination Chamber. Inside the house there is an unresolved argument about whether a formal challenge is civic duty or personal pride, and young representatives arriving from Korrvane frequently treat Relstaris as if it operated by Korrvane rules, which the Formal Challenge Floor is partly designed to contain. Aela's Guest Residence connects Genesis and Castro family life in a way both houses value and neither wants examined politically, and the friendly Castro-Genesis rivalry produces more diplomatic anxiety in other compounds than open hostility would.

Genesis Embassy Court.description: The public entrance, framed by heavy structure and visible capability rather than ornament, with an open approach wide enough for a crowd. Visitors are met at the threshold, not screened at a distance. The court is meant to read as protection offered rather than force displayed. The paving is broad dark slab over much older footings, the base of the frontage original Genesis-era work left uncased where the newer facing stops. Light comes up through the approach markings and moves with the city's routing, so the court is at its brightest when the work period turns. Staff greet arrivals, direct petitioners to the delegation hall, and turn away nobody who has come to look. A set of deep marks in the paving by the inner arch is where the muster gear is dragged out during drills.

Korrvane Delegation Hall.description: The political and administrative heart of the embassy: representative offices, filing stations and staff rooms handling Genesis business in the Republic. The pace is brisk and the paperwork enormous. Korrvane's reputation for directness does not survive contact with capital procedure, and everyone here has adapted. The hall is plain fitting inside a heavy older shell, its structural ribs bare above partitions installed long after the walls. Its lighting follows the city's routing, and the hall works on well past the point where the light drops. Staff refuse filings that are not in the Republic's form and will redraft one at the counter for anyone who asks. A wall of filing slots by the door is labelled in two scripts, one of them faded almost out.

Formal Challenge Floor.description: A controlled space for house challenges and formal demonstrations, reinforced and overseen by officials who record terms before anything begins. Use is rare and strictly conditioned. Its existence channels the impulse toward challenge into something the capital can survive watching. The floor is original Genesis-era construction reinforced twice since, so the wall at the inspection hatch shows three distinct materials layered against one another. Its lighting is fixed and even, on a separate supply, so that nothing in the room changes while a contest is under way. Officials verify terms, refuse a challenge not filed in advance, and clear the floor entirely before it is opened. The surfacing is replaced in sections after use, and the newest section is always a slightly different shade.

Emergency Muster Deck.description: An open assembly deck where Genesis personnel form up during capitol emergencies, with equipment stores and launch clearance to the city lanes. Drills are frequent and unannounced. When the deck lights come on at night, neighbouring compounds start making enquiries within minutes. The deck is later construction on an ancient platform, the original setdown markings still faint under the current formation lines. Its lighting runs on the compound's own supply and does not dim with the civic maintenance window, which is the entire reason it was fitted that way. Stores are inventoried after every drill, launch clearance is requested through civic lane control, and refusals are accepted without argument. A painted muster line has been repainted so often that its edges have gone soft.

Representative Training Court.description: Daily training ground for assigned Genesis staff, worked hard from early morning, with rotation between conditioning, formation and rescue drill. Instruction is demanding and unshowy. Visitors are welcome to watch, which cuts against the assumption that Genesis training is a spectacle. The court is enclosed by old defensive walling whose upper courses were rebuilt in a plainer stone that nobody matched to the original. Its surfacing is heavy composite laid in panels and replaced piece by piece, so the ground is a patchwork of wear. Instructors run to a posted schedule, admit watchers to the edge only, and stop a drill outright rather than let a tired formation finish badly. A row of water butts along the wall is refilled by whoever finishes their rotation first.

Tacitus's Working Office.description: A practical office used when Tacitus handles serious Relstaris business, cluttered with active files and set up for long days rather than receptions. Aides come and go without ceremony. Most decisions attributed to House Genesis in the capital are actually made at this desk. The room is a plain fit-out inside an older corner of the building, with an original deep window recess that no amount of newer shelving has managed to disguise. The light through it moves with the city's routing, and the desk lamp goes on at the same point in the cycle every day. Files are paper as well as recorded, visitors are seen without an appointment when the door is open, and the door is closed when it is not. A chair in the corner is permanently occupied by a stack of folders nobody has filed.

Ark's Rarely Used Office.description: A formal office maintained because protocol insists, kept ready for an occupant with limited interest in occupying it. Staff dust it, update its files and quietly use it for overflow meetings. Its permanent emptiness is a running joke that nobody makes in front of visiting Korrvane officials. The room is the most formally finished space in the building, older panelling restored rather than replaced, and it sits oddly against the plain working rooms around it. Its lighting follows the city routing like the rest of the wing, so the room brightens and dims to an empty chair. Staff keep its files current, decline to reassign it, and book it out for meetings without recording that they have. The seat cushion is unworn while the visitor chairs opposite are not.

Genesis Residential Wing.description: Housing for visiting family and delegation staff, built solid and plain with communal eating spaces that stay busy late. Korrvane habits persist here more than anywhere else in the compound. Newcomers learn the capital's rules at these tables faster than from any briefing. The wing is heavy older construction refitted inside, its thick walls and small windows unlike the glassed frontages elsewhere here. Its interior lighting is warm and holds steady through the evening while the courts outside dim, which is why the tables stay full. Rooms are allocated by the house rather than let, food is provided at cost, and longer stays are charged against the delegation's budget. A long table in the main room has one leg braced with a plate that was clearly cut from something else.

Aela's Guest Residence.description: A separate residence connecting Genesis and Castro family life without turning that connection into a political instrument, kept deliberately informal and off the delegation schedule. Visits here are family matters. Both houses benefit from it and neither discusses it in front of their own representatives. The residence is a small later building against an older wall, plainly finished, without the structural display that governs the rest of the compound. Its lighting is on a domestic supply and stays low and constant rather than following the civic routing. Delegation staff do not enter without being asked, and arrivals are not recorded on the compound's visitor list. A pair of mismatched chairs in the entry hall sits where people stop to talk rather than to wait.

Old Genesis Core Memorial.description: A memorial recording former Genesis-backed Core holders and the defensive works they left behind, including structures still buried under the capital. Names of the defeated are included. The house presents the record as obligation rather than claim, which is a more careful position than it sounds. The memorial stands on exposed original footing, and the stone of the oldest panels is the same material as the works they describe. Its light is low, fixed and independent of the grid, deliberately unlike the shifting glow of the streets. Entry is free, unescorted and unattended, and the house declines requests to hold ceremonies here. A shallow basin at the foot of the panels collects the small objects visitors leave, and it is emptied into store rather than cleared away.

Public Strength Gallery.description: A public gallery of rescue, defence and challenge records that deliberately includes failures alongside victories, with accounts of what each cost. Schoolchildren from across the city visit. It is the clearest statement the embassy makes about what it thinks strength is for. The gallery is a long hall of heavy older structure with newer cases standing clear of the walls, the original stonework and its repairs left visible behind them. Lighting is even and cool across the cases and does not shift with the grid, so the accounts read the same at any hour. Entry is free, school visits are booked, and staff answer children's questions about the failures at the same length as the victories. One case holds an account with a name deliberately left unfilled, and the label explains why.

Grounded Conversation Room.description: A deliberately ordinary meeting room with plain chairs and no recording, used to stop every discussion becoming a spectacle. Tacitus favours it for difficult conversations. Delegates arriving expecting formality find themselves talking plainly within ten minutes, which is the entire design intent. The room is small and unremarkable, carved out of older service space, with a low ceiling and none of the structural drama the compound otherwise trades in. Its lighting is warm, domestic and steady, entirely unlike the courts outside. Nothing is served and nothing is minuted, and staff will not carry a message out of the room on anyone's behalf. The chairs are visibly a mixed set, and the least comfortable one is always the one left for whoever arrives last.

Deepcanopy Hunting Ground.name: Deepcanopy Hunting Ground
Deepcanopy Hunting Ground.basicInfo: A stretch of old-growth Nexaran forest where the canopy closes overhead and filtered light reaches the floor in shifting columns. Game trails cross between root buttresses and fallen trunks, and territorial Ridgewing calls echo from the upper branches.
Deepcanopy Hunting Ground.hiddenInfo: Trailhound packs hunt here in coordinated sweeps. Ridgewing nesting pairs defend canopy territory aggressively during Highfire. Fieldmoth swarms concentrate near fungal deadfall after rain. The Frontier Care House occasionally sends patrols to clear predator pressure from nearby route corridors.

Canopy Break Clearing.description: A gap in the overhead canopy where a massive trunk fell and opened the forest floor to direct light. Scrub growth and ground-cover fungi carpet the exposed soil, attracting grazing fauna and the predators that follow them. Good sightlines in all directions for the clearing's width.

Root-Buttress Trail.description: A narrow game trail threading between massive root buttresses, worn smooth by repeated animal passage. The canopy is dense here and visibility drops to a few metres. Sound carries unpredictably — calls echo off the trunks and make direction hard to judge.

Ridgewing Nesting Stand.description: A cluster of tall straight trunks where Ridgewing pairs have established nesting territory in the upper branches. Territorial markers — stripped bark, scattered feather-scale debris and whitewash — are visible from ground level. The birds react to movement below.

Stream Crossing.description: A shallow Nexaran forest stream where game trails converge at a natural ford. The water runs clear over dark stone and attracts drinking fauna at dawn and dusk. Tracks of multiple species mark the soft banks on either side.

Fallen Trunk Ridge.description: A massive fallen trunk, half-buried and colonised by bracket fungi, forms a natural elevated ridge overlooking the surrounding forest floor. A useful vantage point for observing animal movement below, and a sheltered rest position against the trunk's lee side.

Ashvent Hunting Flats.name: Ashvent Hunting Flats
Ashvent Hunting Flats.basicInfo: A stretch of volcanic clinker and hardened ash flows punctuated by active geothermal vents. Ventcrawlers colonise the warm fissures and Glassmidge swarms pulse above the thermal updrafts. The ground is treacherous — thin crusts over hollow tubes and sudden temperature gradients.
Ashvent Hunting Flats.hiddenInfo: Ventcrawler colonies defend vent clusters aggressively. The thermal updrafts attract Glassmidge swarms that can disorient travellers. Rare mineral deposits exposed by recent vent activity draw occasional prospectors from Ignivex. Some fissures connect to deeper geothermal systems and produce unpredictable steam bursts.

Active Vent Cluster.description: A cluster of steaming geothermal vents surrounded by mineral-stained clinker. The air shimmers with heat and carries a sharp mineral tang. Ventcrawlers have colonised the warm fissures between vents, their territorial markings visible as scraped channels in the mineral crust.

Cooled Flow Corridor.description: A corridor of hardened lava flow between higher clinker ridges, cooled enough to walk but still warm underfoot. The surface is rough and dark, broken into plates with sharp edges. Shelter from wind but limited visibility beyond the next ridge.

Glassmidge Thermal.description: An open flat where thermal updrafts from buried heat sources draw dense Glassmidge swarms into the air. The insects pulse in shifting columns of reflected light, beautiful and disorienting. The ground is stable here but the air itself is the hazard.

Crust Shelf Overlook.description: A raised shelf of hardened volcanic crust offering a broad view across the surrounding vent field. The surface is stable and wind-scoured clean. A good position for observing animal movement across the flats, and exposed enough that nothing approaches unseen.

Dunebreak Hunting Range.name: Dunebreak Hunting Range
Dunebreak Hunting Range.basicInfo: Open desert country where stabilised dune ridges alternate with hard-packed gravel flats. Slowhide Grazers move through the scrub-dotted troughs between dunes, and Dustrunner packs shadow the herds from the ridge crests. Wind-carved rock outcrops provide the only shade and shelter.
Dunebreak Hunting Range.hiddenInfo: Dustrunner packs use the dune ridges for coordinated pursuit hunting. Slowhide Grazers are territorial and dangerous when cornered in narrow troughs. Salvage teams from Dustfall occasionally cross this ground and leave cached water supplies in marked rock shelters. Sand conditions change with wind direction — a flat crossing at dawn can be dune-blocked by midday.

Gravel Flat.description: A broad hard-packed gravel flat between dune ridges, open to the sky and scoured by wind. Slowhide Grazer tracks cross the surface in well-worn paths between feeding grounds. Good visibility in all directions but no shade or cover.

Dune Ridge Crest.description: The wind-sharpened crest of a stabilised dune ridge, offering commanding views across the surrounding desert. Dustrunner tracks and scratchings mark the sand along the ridge — the packs use these high points for spotting prey below. Exposed to wind and sun.

Scrub Trough.description: A sheltered trough between two dune ridges where hardy Nexaran scrub plants have taken hold. Slowhide Grazers browse here, partially screened by the vegetation. The trough funnels movement and limits escape routes — a natural ambush corridor.

Rock Outcrop Shelter.description: A wind-carved rock outcrop rising from the desert floor, its overhangs and hollows providing the only real shade in the area. Marks of previous travellers — fire-blackened stone, water cache markers — suggest regular use as a rest point. Small fauna shelter in the crevices.

Blackrock Tidal Shelf.name: Blackrock Tidal Shelf
Blackrock Tidal Shelf.basicInfo: A broad tidal shelf of dark tilted rock slabs exposed at low water, colonised by Tideclaw populations and scavenging shore fauna. Rock pools trap marine life between tides. The cliff behind the shelf is sheer and wind-blasted, with Eavesdart colonies nesting in the upper faces.
Blackrock Tidal Shelf.hiddenInfo: Tideclaw colonies defend their feeding pools aggressively — groups of three or more coordinate to drive competitors away. Eavesdarts nest in the cliff face and dive-mob anything that approaches their ledges. Tidal timing is critical: the shelf floods fast on the incoming tide and the retreat route to higher ground narrows to a single scramble path.

Tideclaw Pool Flats.description: Broad dark rock flats pocked with tidal pools, each pool a small ecosystem of trapped marine life. Tideclaws patrol between pools, scraping and feeding. The rock is slick with salt spray and algae, and the pools themselves are defended territory.

Cliff Base Scramble.description: The narrow rocky scramble at the base of the sea cliff, the only reliable route between the tidal shelf and higher ground. Eavesdarts nest in crevices overhead and react to disturbance. Footing is poor and the path narrows at the waterline.

Eavesdart Cliff Face.description: The sheer wind-blasted cliff face above the tidal shelf, riddled with nesting ledges occupied by Eavesdart colonies. The birds launch in aggressive spiralling dives at anything that climbs within range. A challenging vertical environment with loose rock and salt-weakened handholds.

Exposed Slab Ridge.description: A ridge of tilted dark rock slabs rising above the tidal shelf, dry at all tides and wind-exposed. Provides a vantage point over the pool flats below and the open water beyond. The rock is sharp-edged and fractured — good footing but harsh on equipment.

Longreach Lurker Bend.name: Longreach Lurker Bend
Longreach Lurker Bend.basicInfo: A wide bend in the Longreach where the river slows and deepens against an undercut bank. Longreach Lurkers favour the still water beneath the overhang, and the opposite bank's gravel shallows attract drinking fauna from the surrounding forest. Barge traffic gives this bend a wide berth.
Longreach Lurker Bend.hiddenInfo: Longreach Lurkers are ambush predators that strike from beneath the undercut bank. The deep pool holds multiple adults. The gravel shallows on the far bank are a natural chokepoint — animals drinking there are vulnerable to both Lurkers from the water and Trailhound packs from the forest edge. Barge crews report sightings here regularly.

Undercut Bank.description: The deep undercut bank where the river has carved beneath old root systems and exposed dark soil. The water is deep and still here, its surface deceptively calm. Longreach Lurker territory — disturbance of the water draws attention from below.

Gravel Shallows.description: A broad gravel bar on the inside of the river bend where the water runs shallow and clear over rounded stones. Animal tracks converge from the treeline — this is a primary drinking point. Exposed position with the deep pool uncomfortably close.

Elevated Bank Trail.description: A worn trail along the elevated outer bank, high enough above the waterline to observe the deep pool and the shallows opposite. Root-braced soil provides stable footing. A good observation position but any descent to the water is steep and slow.

Forest Edge Blind.description: The treeline where forest meets the river bank, dense enough to screen observation but thin enough to see the gravel shallows beyond. Natural cover for watching animal activity at the waterline. Trailhound prints mark the soft ground between the trunks.

Summit Ridgewing Territory.name: Summit Ridgewing Territory
Summit Ridgewing Territory.basicInfo: High mountain terrain above the treeline where bare rock ridges and alpine scrub provide hunting territory for Ridgewing pairs. The air is thin and cold, the wind constant, and the views extend across the mountain spine to distant lowlands. Terrain is exposed and physically demanding.
Summit Ridgewing Territory.hiddenInfo: Ridgewing pairs are fiercely territorial at altitude and attack perceived threats with coordinated diving strikes. The thin air and steep terrain limit ground mobility for non-flying species. Weather changes rapidly — clear mornings can become whiteout conditions within an hour. A few sheltered rock hollows offer emergency cover.

Exposed Ridge Crest.description: A bare rock ridge crest exposed to constant wind, with views in all directions across the mountain country. Ridgewing pairs patrol this airspace and react to anything that breaks the skyline. No cover, no shelter, nowhere to hide from aerial attack.

Alpine Scrub Bowl.description: A sheltered bowl below the ridge crest where hardy alpine scrub has taken hold between rock outcrops. Small fauna shelter here and Ridgewings hunt the bowl from above. Partial cover from the scrub but limited escape routes — the bowl funnels toward a single exit gully.

Rock Hollow Shelter.description: A natural hollow in the rock formation below the ridge, deep enough to shelter from wind and aerial observation. Previous visitors have stacked loose stone into a windbreak. A defensible rest position with a single narrow approach.

Scree Slope.description: A steep slope of loose broken rock descending from the alpine bowl toward the treeline below. The footing shifts constantly and noise carries. Ridgewings use the thermal updrafts along this slope face for hunting runs. Descent is fast but uncontrolled.

Windgrass Grazer Plains.name: Windgrass Grazer Plains
Windgrass Grazer Plains.basicInfo: Rolling open grassland where Nexaran windgrass grows waist-high between scattered rock clusters. Slowhide Grazer herds move through the grass in loose groups, and Dustrunner packs shadow them from downwind. The terrain is deceptively open — the grass conceals ground-level hazards and approaching predators.
Windgrass Grazer Plains.hiddenInfo: Slowhide Grazers are herd animals that stampede when threatened, dangerous to anything in their path. Dustrunner packs coordinate attacks through the tall grass using sound and scent. The rock clusters serve as observation points and defensible positions. Fieldmoth swarms emerge from the grass at dusk in spectacular but disorienting numbers.

Tall Grass Corridor.description: A natural corridor through waist-high windgrass where Slowhide Grazers have worn a broad path. Visibility is limited to the path width — the grass walls conceal everything beyond arm's reach. Sound and scent are the primary senses here.

Grazer Watering Hollow.description: A shallow natural depression where rainwater collects and the grass grows shorter, creating an open area where Slowhide Grazer herds congregate to drink. The hollow provides clear sightlines but the surrounding tall grass can conceal Dustrunner approach from any direction.

Rock Cluster Vantage.description: A cluster of weather-worn boulders rising above the grass line, offering elevated views across the surrounding plains. A natural observation post and defensible position. Animal tracks circle the base where grazers use the rocks as scratching posts.

Dusk Emergence Flat.description: An open stretch of shorter grass where Fieldmoth swarms emerge from ground-level cocoons at dusk, filling the air with soft-bodied luminescent insects. The display is spectacular and draws both predators and prey. Visibility drops sharply during peak emergence.

Saltwind Route Waystation.name: Saltwind Route Waystation
Saltwind Route Waystation.basicInfo: An unmanned waystation along the coastal freight corridor where route teamsters rest and check loads. The station itself is a reinforced composite shelter with basic water supply, but the surrounding salt scrub attracts Tideclaws from the nearby shore and Trailhounds from the inland routes.
Saltwind Route Waystation.hiddenInfo: The waystation is officially maintained by Helvyra's route administration but visits are infrequent. Tideclaws scavenge dropped cargo and food waste. Trailhound packs treat the station perimeter as territorial boundary — they do not enter but patrol the approaches. Occasional smuggler crews use the station as a transfer point outside city jurisdiction.

Waystation Shelter.description: A reinforced composite shelter with a sealed water tap, cargo inspection platform and basic overhead cover. The structure is functional but weather-worn. Cargo marks and route team scratches cover the interior walls. A defensible position with clear sightlines from the entrance.

Cargo Staging Flat.description: A cleared hard-packed area beside the waystation where cargo is set down for inspection and redistribution. Tideclaw tracks and scratchings mark the surface where the scavengers investigate dropped loads. Open and exposed but close to the shelter.

Salt Scrub Perimeter.description: The ring of salt-tolerant scrub surrounding the waystation, dense enough to screen small fauna and low enough to see over. Trailhound packs patrol the outer edge at dawn and dusk. The transition zone between maintained station ground and open wilderness.

Perimeter Salvage Ground.name: Perimeter Salvage Ground
Perimeter Salvage Ground.basicInfo: The scattered salvage ground beyond Dustfall's maintained perimeter, where decommissioned cargo modules and stripped machinery slowly surrender to wind and sun. Dustrunner packs den in the larger wrecks, and Trailhound tracking teams from Dustfall periodically sweep the area for predator control.
Perimeter Salvage Ground.hiddenInfo: Dustrunner dens in the cargo wrecks are well-established and defended. Salvage teams from Dustfall claim specific wrecks and mark them with painted tags — interfering with a claimed wreck creates conflict with the salvagers, not the law. Some wrecks contain intact components that haven't been reached yet. The Perimeter Beacon patrols pass through at irregular intervals.

Stripped Module Row.description: A line of stripped cargo modules set on bare ground, their panels removed and interiors exposed to the elements. Dustrunner scratchings and den-marks are visible on the remaining structural frames. The modules provide broken cover and channelled movement between them.

Open Salvage Flat.description: A broad flat area of compacted ground littered with small salvage debris — stripped fasteners, cable remnants, broken composite panels. Clear sightlines but exposed. Trailhound tracking teams use this open ground for scent work.

Deep Wreck Cluster.description: A dense cluster of larger decommissioned machinery and cargo frames, some still partially intact. The interior spaces are dark, enclosed and defensible — Dustrunner pack territory. Navigation through the cluster requires squeezing between corroded frames and climbing over collapsed sections.

Longreach Farmland Edge.name: Longreach Farmland Edge
Longreach Farmland Edge.basicInfo: The boundary between maintained Longreach farmland and open wild ground, where cultivated fields give way to scrub and the problems of agriculture meet the problems of wilderness. Slowhide Grazers break through fencelines to eat crops, Fieldmoth swarms descend on ripening fields, and Field Hands work the boundary in ongoing conflict with nature.
Longreach Farmland Edge.hiddenInfo: The farmland edge is a constant low-level battleground between agricultural interests and wildlife pressure. Field Hands are armed with practical tools, not military weapons, and deal with crop pests through established methods. Slowhide Grazers that learn to breach fencelines become persistent problems requiring organised drives. Fieldmoth swarms during Highfire can strip a field in hours.

Fenceline Break.description: A section of agricultural fenceline where Slowhide Grazers have repeatedly broken through to reach cultivated crops beyond. The fence is patched and reinforced but the ground is trampled and the posts lean. Fresh grazer tracks lead in both directions.

Crop Field Edge.description: The last maintained crop rows before the farmland gives way to wild ground. The crops show signs of wildlife damage — trampled rows, stripped plants, Fieldmoth cocoon remnants on stems. Field Hand equipment and irrigation lines run along the boundary.

Wild Scrub Margin.description: The strip of wild scrub beyond the fenceline where wildlife shelters before and after raids on the cultivated fields. Grazer browsing keeps the scrub low, and predator tracks suggest Dustrunners use the margin for hunting grazers distracted by crop feeding.

Field Hand Rest Shelter.description: A simple composite-panel shelter at the field edge where Field Hands rest during boundary patrols, store pest-control supplies and coordinate response to wildlife incursions. Practical and functional — tools, water, a shaded bench and a clear view of the fenceline.

Dravon Forward Watch.name: Dravon Forward Watch
Dravon Forward Watch.basicInfo: A Dravon security outpost on the edge of Quilrath's outer blockworks, where grey composite structures give way to open volcanic rock. Ward-Class drones hold a perimeter grid while ground patrols sweep the approaches. The outpost monitors the eastern wilderness for unauthorized movement, smuggling routes, and Dustrunner incursions toward the city's outer districts.
Dravon Forward Watch.hiddenInfo: House Dravon uses this outpost as a staging point for sweeps into the wilderness east of Quilrath. The patrol rotation is undermanned in Deephold, and the eastern perimeter has blind spots that smugglers and Claimant scouts have learned to use. The drone grid has a maintenance gap every third cycle that a careful observer can time.

Patrol Staging Yard.description: A surfaced yard between two composite blockwork ranges, fenced with mesh and lit by overhead panels. Dravon security officers brief patrol teams here before sweeps into the eastern waste. A drone charging rack holds four Ward-Class units in standby. Equipment lockers line the southern wall. The yard is exposed to observation from the blockwork rooftops to the west.

Dravon Beacon Line.description: A line of beacon posts marking the boundary between Quilrath's built ground and the open volcanic rock beyond. Each post carries a light and a motion sensor. The gaps between posts are wide enough for a crouched person to cross, and the sensor coverage has dead angles where the terrain dips. Dravon patrols walk this line on rotation.

Observation Gantry.description: A raised metal platform bolted to the top of the outermost blockwork range, giving a clear sightline over the waste to the east and the route approaches to the south. A mounted optic and a comms relay sit at the forward rail. The gantry sways in high wind and offers no cover from above — a Ridgewing's territory begins two ridges east.

Eastern Scree Approach.description: Loose volcanic scree and fractured dark rock beyond the beacon line, sloping downward into the waste. Boot tracks and drone marks show where patrols have swept recently. A shallow gully runs north-south through the scree, deep enough to move through unseen from the gantry. Dustrunner scat and gnawed cargo strapping litter the gully floor.

Volen Firebreak Garrison.name: Volen Firebreak Garrison
Volen Firebreak Garrison.basicInfo: A House Volen garrison post along the basalt firebreak walls south of Ignivex, where wall routes run in long straight lengths between the city's thermal core and the volcanic waste beyond. Caldris-built fortification anchors the post. Patrols monitor the thermal ground for vent activity, unauthorized salvage operations, and movement along the desert approaches from the south.
Volen Firebreak Garrison.hiddenInfo: House Volen maintains this garrison partly for civic protection and partly to control access to the geothermal fields. The Caldris stoneworks that built the walls also built concealed monitoring points that Volen uses to watch the Corsair gate traffic without Corsair knowing. The garrison commander reports to both Volen and the city's civil protection office, and the two chains of command do not always agree.

Wall Gate Checkpoint.description: A fortified gate cut through the basalt firebreak wall, wide enough for a cargo hauler and reinforced with copper-bronze banding. Volen guards question travellers and inspect cargo. A heat-shielded booth sits on each side of the gate. Beyond the wall, the ground drops away toward the thermal plates and the desert.

Wall-Top Walkway.description: The top of the firebreak wall, wide enough for two abreast, running east and west in a straight black line. Patrol officers walk this route scanning the waste with hand optics. Fire vents glow along the southern horizon at night. The walkway is exposed to wind and to anything airborne, but the wall's height gives a commanding view of approach routes from the desert.

Thermal Observation Post.description: A shielded platform beyond the wall, built on basalt pilings above thermal ground that radiates visible heat shimmer. Monitoring equipment tracks vent pressure, ground temperature, and crawler gallery activity. The platform shakes when a vent coughs below. Ventcrawler galleries are marked with red stakes in a semicircle around the post.

Garrison Barracks Block.description: A low block of black stone behind the wall, heat-channelled from the geothermal tap below. Bunks, an armoury, a mess, and a comms station occupy a single level. Off-duty guards play cards at a stone table. The walls are thick enough to muffle the vent-rumble but not a Ventcrawler surfacing through the foundation — it has happened twice.

Ash Slope Descent.description: A steep path of loose grey ash descending from the observation post toward the open volcanic waste. Red stakes mark Ventcrawler galleries on both sides. The ash is deep enough to swallow a boot to the ankle, and the ground beneath it is warm. Vent steam rises in thin columns ahead. This is where Volen patrols turn back and the wild ground begins.

Pennant Freight Camp.name: Pennant Freight Camp
Pennant Freight Camp.basicInfo: A hidden camp in the freight country where the Black Pennant stages raids on corridor convoys. Worn pale rock and scattered freight debris provide cover for modular shelters rigged from salvaged cargo panels. The camp moves every few weeks, but the freight ground's maze of abandoned pallets and broken hauler chassis always offers another site.
Pennant Freight Camp.hiddenInfo: The Pennant uses this camp as a forward base for intercepting Dravon supply convoys heading south along the corridor. Rhex Vaereth's lieutenants rotate crews through on a cycle timed to convoy schedules leaked by a Dravon logistics clerk who believes they are selling to the Unbroken Accord. The camp's real purpose is restitution raids — reclaiming what House Vaereth lost.

Freight Debris Field.description: A spread of abandoned cargo pallets, broken hauler chassis, and twisted freight racking lying across worn pale rock. The debris provides concealment and improvised fortification. Lookouts perch on a tilted hauler frame with a sightline down the corridor approach. Dustrunner tracks circle the debris field at night.

Hidden Shelter Row.description: Three modular shelters assembled from salvaged cargo panels, set in the shadow of a freight stack where they read as more debris from the air. Inside: bunks, a water cache, a weapons locker, and a comms unit tuned to corridor traffic. Pennant crew marks are scratched into the inner panels — the displaced-house crest of Vaereth, crossed out and redrawn as the Pennant.

Ambush Corridor.description: A narrow channel between two rows of stacked freight debris, positioned where the corridor route bends around a shoulder of dark rock. Cargo nets strung between debris walls can be dropped to block a hauler. Firing positions are cut into the freight stacks on both sides. The ground is scattered with shattered composite from previous intercepts.

Supply Cache.description: A sealed cargo container half-buried in pale grit behind the shelter row, its locking mechanism replaced with a Pennant cipher lock. Inside: intercepted supplies — ration packs, medical kits, thermal wraps, and crates of drone parts stripped of Dravon tracking tags. A ledger records what was taken and what was distributed to the displaced communities in Dustfall.

Jackal Salvage Blind.name: Jackal Salvage Blind
Jackal Salvage Blind.basicInfo: An Iron Jackals outpost in the hummock waste between the corridor and the coast, used for intercepting salvage convoys and stripping Derelict Cargo Lifters that wander off the freight lanes. The hummocked black rock provides natural concealment, and the Jackals have improved it with camouflaged observation points and a processing yard hidden in a shallow depression.
Jackal Salvage Blind.hiddenInfo: Ralven Nox's second ledger records the salvage that passes through this blind — the material that was never purchased and never auctioned. Stripped drone cores, Dravon security components with serial numbers filed off, and cargo that fell off a lifter that was helped to fall. The Jackals consider this their territory and will negotiate before fighting, but they will fight.

Hummock Observation Point.description: A camouflaged hide built into the lee side of a black rock hummock, overlooking the freight lane to the east and the coast approach to the west. A mounted optic on a swivel tracks movement. The hide is invisible from the lane unless you know where to look. A signal mirror connects to the processing yard below.

Processing Depression.description: A natural depression in the hummock waste, deepened and levelled, where the Jackals strip salvage. Cutting tools, a portable forge, and racks of sorted components fill the space. A tarpaulin rigged on poles keeps the work out of sight from above. Two heavy hauler sleds sit ready for moving processed material back to Vossan Yard.

Lifter Intercept Lane.description: A stretch of flat dark rock between hummocks where Derelict Cargo Lifters pass on their way along the coast. The Jackals have placed debris to channel lifters toward a narrowing where a magnetic clamp can stop one. Stripped lifter shells lie at the edges of the lane — previous catches. The ground is stained with leaked hydraulic fluid.

Crooked Landing South.name: Crooked Landing South
Crooked Landing South.basicInfo: A Bent Halo waypoint along the faded southern corridor, where the worked surface has thinned to a used line over natural rock. Cargo and people moving outside official channels pass through here between Dustfall and the southern settlements. The waypoint is disguised as an abandoned route shelter.
Crooked Landing South.hiddenInfo: Saevik Ruun's network uses this waypoint for handoffs — refugees, medicine, restricted cargo, and information change hands here between Dustfall runners and southern contacts. The shelter's abandoned appearance is maintained deliberately. A hidden compartment under the floor holds emergency supplies and forged transit documents. Brannoc Kest has used it to move people on no manifest at all.

Abandoned Route Shelter.description: A small composite shelter set back from the corridor line, its panels weathered and one wall deliberately cracked to look derelict. Inside: a functional space with water, a charging point, and a concealed hatch in the floor. The shelter faces away from the corridor so its door is not visible to passing convoys. Bent Halo marks — a tilted circle — are scratched under the door frame.

Hidden Cellar.description: A dug-out space beneath the shelter floor, accessed through a hatch concealed under a cargo mat. Low ceiling, packed-earth walls reinforced with salvaged panels. Supplies: water canisters, ration packs, medical kits, forged transit papers in sealed pouches, and a short-range comms unit. Space for four people to wait. The air is stale and warm.

Corridor Watch Point.description: A position on a low rise of natural rock behind the shelter, giving a view up and down the corridor for half a kilometre in each direction. A ground cloth and a water flask mark a regular watching position. Signal flags in a pouch — colour-coded for convoy type, patrol, clear. The watcher can see the shelter door and the cellar hatch from here.

Steepfall Trailhound Run.name: Steepfall Trailhound Run
Steepfall Trailhound Run.basicInfo: Dense conifer forest on a steep pitch below the Quilrath highlands, used by Dravon patrol crews and Dustfall volunteer handlers for Trailhound training runs and fauna tracking exercises. The close timber and deadfall-covered floor make visibility poor and scent work essential. Ridgewing territory begins at the treeline above.
Steepfall Trailhound Run.hiddenInfo: Dravon security uses this ground to train Trailhounds for urban search-and-rescue — the steep, cluttered terrain simulates collapsed blockwork. Unofficial hunts happen here too: off-duty patrol officers tracking Dustrunners that have pushed into the timber from the east. The handlers keep this quiet because Quilrath's civic code technically prohibits recreational hunting within the city's patrol radius.

Trailhead Clearing.description: A small clearing where the timber thins enough for a handler to brief a team. Packed needle litter underfoot, a wooden equipment rack between two conifers, and Trailhound scratching posts worn smooth. Boot tracks and paw prints lead in three directions into the dark timber. A Dravon patrol marker post stands at the north edge.

Dense Canopy Track.description: A narrow game trail through close-standing conifers, the canopy so tight overhead that the light drops to a green-grey twilight. The trail is marked with handler blazes on the trunks — claw marks at hip height, Trailhound nose-level. Fieldmoth cocoons hang in clusters from the lower branches. The ground is soft, wet, and nearly silent underfoot.

Deadfall Gully.description: A steep gully choked with fallen timber, the trunks green with moss and treacherous underfoot. Water runs beneath the deadfall in a thin cold stream. Scent pools here — Trailhounds work this gully with focused intensity. A Dustrunner den has been dug into the bank beneath a root mass, the entrance screened by fallen branches.

Ridge Treeline.description: The timber thins and stops at a line of bare grey rock where the slope steepens toward the highland ridges above. Wind comes across the open rock in gusts that carry the smell of snow. Ridgewing territory markers — large pellet accumulations and talon-scored stone — line the treeline. Looking up, the sky above the ridge is watched.

Ventcrawler Plate Fields.name: Ventcrawler Plate Fields
Ventcrawler Plate Fields.basicInfo: Active thermal ground south of Ignivex where Ventcrawlers surface to breed and bask on crusted flow fields. Ignivex smiths come here to harvest shed carapace plates for heat shielding. The ground is unstable, the air shimmers with heat, and the crawlers defend their galleries with territorial violence. Red stakes mark known burrows but the map is never current.
Ventcrawler Plate Fields.hiddenInfo: The plate harvest is technically regulated by House Volen, but enforcement is sparse this far from the walls. Independent smiths and Refit Row dealers send their own crews, and the competition for prime shed plates has led to fights — between people, not crawlers. A deep gallery system connects several surface openings, and the largest crawler in the field has not been seen on the surface in two seasons, only heard.

Crusted Flow Shelf.description: A broad shelf of ridged black flow rock, crusted and cracked, radiating visible heat shimmer. Ventcrawler tracks — wide belly-drag marks and claw scores — cross the shelf in all directions. Shed carapace plates lie in scattered piles near gallery mouths, their edges still warm. The rock is hot enough to burn through thin boot soles after a few minutes of standing still.

Gallery Mouth Cluster.description: Three gallery openings in the crusted flow, each ringed with compacted ash and marked with red stakes. The largest opening is wide enough for a Starian to enter crouching. Warm air rises from below, carrying a mineral smell. A Ventcrawler's tail club is visible in the middle gallery — the animal is wedged across the opening, watching. Shed plates are thickest here.

Heat Shimmer Flat.description: An open flat of dark stone where the heat from below makes the air dance. Ventcrawlers bask here in Highfire — low, still, plated shapes that look like rock formations until one moves. The flat offers no cover and no shade. Lava shows in narrow red lines at the southern edge where the crust is thinnest. A harvester's abandoned tool bag sits near a cracked stake.

Deep Gallery Descent.description: A sloping tunnel into the Ventcrawler gallery system, the walls smooth from decades of belly-drag and warm to the touch. The air is thick with heat and mineral vapour. Bioluminescent growth on the walls gives a faint orange glow. The tunnel branches — one fork drops steeply toward a chamber where something large shifts in the dark. Shed plates line the floor like tiles.

Mesa Shadow Pack Ground.name: Mesa Shadow Pack Ground
Mesa Shadow Pack Ground.basicInfo: A cluster of dark mesas in the desert south of Ignivex where Dustrunner packs den in the shadow-side caves and hunt the mesa edges at night. The mesas provide shade, shelter, and elevation for pack lookouts. Salvage crews and corridor travellers who camp in mesa shadow without a watch rotation learn why the frontier says never sleep in Dustrunner country without a fire.
Mesa Shadow Pack Ground.hiddenInfo: Three packs share this mesa cluster in an uneasy territorial arrangement. The largest pack — twelve to fifteen runners — dens in the deepest shadow cave and controls the water seep at the mesa base. A smaller pack has learned to follow Derelict Cargo Lifters through the mesa gaps and strip whatever falls. The third pack is new, displaced from closer to Ignivex by Volen patrol sweeps, and is testing the other two.

Mesa Gap Approach.description: A sandy corridor between two dark mesas, wide enough for a hauler and shaded for most of the day. Boot prints and drag marks show traffic. Dustrunner scat and gnawed bone fragments line the base of both mesa walls. At dusk, green-white eyeshine appears at the mesa tops — the pack watchers have seen you before you see them.

Shadow-Side Den Caves.description: Shallow caves eroded into the sheer north face of the largest mesa, in permanent shadow. The cave floors are packed with shed fur, bone, and the torn remains of cargo wrapping. The largest cave goes back far enough that the rear is invisible from outside. A low growling resonates from within when anyone approaches. The smell is unmistakable.

Mesa Top Lookout.description: The flat top of the smaller mesa, reached by a crumbling natural ramp on the south face. The summit is wind-scoured and bare, with a commanding view of the desert in all directions. Dustrunner scat marks the edges — the pack uses this as a watch point. At night, the green-white eyeshine of the mesa-top watchers is visible from a kilometre away.

Water Seep Basin.description: A shallow depression at the base of the largest mesa where water seeps through the rock and collects in a palm-sized pool. The basin is the only water source in the mesa cluster, and the dominant pack controls it. Animal tracks from every species in the area converge here. The sand around the pool is churned with prints and stained dark. Approach at night is suicide.

Rubblefield Tide Pools.name: Rubblefield Tide Pools
Rubblefield Tide Pools.basicInfo: A stretch of broken volcanic coast south of Ignivex where black rubble fragments trap tidal pools in which Tideclaws breed in enormous numbers. Coastal salvage crews avoid this shore at night. The rubble field extends from the high-tide line inland, creating a maze of wet channels, trapped pools, and unstable footing where the claws have the advantage.
Rubblefield Tide Pools.hiddenInfo: An old salvage platform sits at the shore edge, abandoned after a tide-season infestation drove the crew out.
