The platform still has functional equipment — a winch, a cargo crane, salvage racks — but the Tideclaws have colonized the substructure. A big old specimen the size of a small cargo crate lives under the platform and has broken the ankle of the last person who tried to reclaim the site.

Rubble Maze.description: Black volcanic rubble fragments lying loose over solid shore rock, creating a maze of gaps, channels, and trapped pools at every tide. The footing is treacherous — fragments shift underfoot and the wet rock between them is slick. Tideclaw shells and claw fragments litter the rubble. At low tide the maze is navigable. At high tide the channels fill and the claws come up.

Tide Pool Cluster.description: A group of deep pools trapped in hollows between the largest rubble fragments, each pool home to a colony of Tideclaws of various sizes. The water is clear enough to see them — armoured shapes stacked on the bottom, great claws folded, stalked eyes watching. Reach into a pool and learn what the claw is for. The pools connect via submerged channels the claws use to move between colonies.

Abandoned Salvage Platform.description: A metal platform on pilings above the high-tide line, its deck still holding a cargo winch, a crane arm, and racks of corroded salvage tools. The platform is sound but the substructure has been colonized — the pilings are encrusted with growth and the spaces between them are Tideclaw territory. The big old crate-sized specimen lives directly under the winch housing. Equipment left on the deck overnight is dragged to the edge by morning.

Darkwater Ford.name: Darkwater Ford
Darkwater Ford.basicInfo: A river crossing where the forest meets the salt margin, marked with a warning post that nobody has maintained in two seasons. The ford is shallow enough to wade in Ironbreak and Deephold but deep and slow in Greenward — Lurker season. Barge traffic from Helvyra passes the ford mouth, and the current carries the smell of the city's quays downstream to everything that hunts here.
Darkwater Ford.hiddenInfo: A Longreach Lurker has claimed the deep pool below the ford and has taken two animals and a salvage drone this season. The warning post should read 'active' but the last route crew to check it was short-handed and marked it 'clear'. Helvyra's route maintenance knows about the discrepancy but has not sent a crew because the ford is technically outside their patrol radius. Trailhound handlers from the eastern settlements avoid the crossing and take the longer bridge route north.

Ford Approach.description: A muddy bank where the forest path meets the river, the trees thinning to stunted salt-tolerant growth at the water's edge. A wooden warning post stands at the bank — its painted status board reads 'CLEAR' in faded letters. Boot prints, animal tracks, and drag marks converge at the water line. The river here is wide, slow, and dark enough that the bottom is invisible from the bank.

The Ford Crossing.description: A stretch of river where the bottom rises to waist-depth over a gravel bar — the crossing point. The water moves slowly and the gravel is firm underfoot, but the deep pool is immediately downstream, a drop-off visible as a dark line in the water. Anything that enters the ford disturbs the gravel and sends a vibration downstream. In Greenward, when the water is high, the gravel bar is submerged and the crossing becomes a swim.

Upstream Bank.description: A quieter stretch of bank upstream of the ford, where the current is faster and the water shallower over exposed rock. A fallen tree spans half the river here, its trunk worn smooth by flood seasons. This is where a careful traveller crosses when the ford feels wrong — slower, harder, but out of the Lurker's territory. Trailhound teams use this route.

Far Bank.description: The opposite bank of the ford, where the ground rises steeply through salt-margin scrub toward open country. A trampled path leads up from the water to a flat resting area where crossing parties regroup. A cargo drone carcass lies half-submerged at the water's edge — stripped of its payload, hull punctured from below, one leg still gripping the bank.

Scrub Margin Grazer Flats.name: Scrub Margin Grazer Flats
Scrub Margin Grazer Flats.basicInfo: Open scrubland at the edge of Quilrath's built ground where Slowhide Grazers from the eastern holdings range onto wild pasture. The scrub is low and sparse — grey-green growth on gritty soil between dark rock outcrops. Holdings to the west send herds here in Greenward when the row pastures are grazed short. Dustrunner packs follow the herds from the waste.
Scrub Margin Grazer Flats.hiddenInfo: The grazer flats are contested ground between two holdings whose boundary was never formally surveyed. Both claim the water depression in the centre, and both run herds onto it. A Dustrunner pack — six to eight runners — has been working the boundary line, taking calves from whichever herd is least watched. The holdings blame each other for the losses.

Scrub Pasture.description: Low grey-green scrub on gritty soil, cropped short by grazing. Slowhide tracks — wide flat impressions — cross the ground in worn paths between water and shelter. Rock outcrops break the pasture into sections. A holding's ear-notched herd of eight grazers moves slowly through the scrub, a handler and two Trailhounds keeping the perimeter. Fieldmoth cocoons hang from the taller scrub stems.

Water Depression.description: A shallow depression in the scrub where water collects after rain, forming a muddy pool surrounded by churned ground. Both holdings' herds converge here, and the tracks overlap into a confused mess. Stakes from two different holdings mark the depression's edges. A dead calf's remains — picked clean — lie thirty metres east, dragged there by something that left narrow-footed prints.

Dustrunner Kill Site.description: A scattering of Slowhide calf bones and torn hide behind a rock outcrop, screened from the pasture by scrub. Dustrunner scat and dig marks surround the site. The pack has used this spot more than once — the bones are from different seasons. A handler's broken signal flag lies nearby, snapped at the shaft. The pack comes at night from the east, through a gap between two outcrops that neither holding watches.

Perimeter Outcrop.description: A cluster of dark rock outcrops at the eastern edge of the grazer flats, where the scrub gives way to open waste. This is the boundary between grazed country and Dustrunner territory. Trailhound claw marks score the rock at nose height — territorial marking by the holdings' guard animals. From the top of the largest outcrop, the waste stretches east toward the volcanic ridges, empty and watched.

Ashslope Vent Crossing.name: Ashslope Vent Crossing
Ashslope Vent Crossing.basicInfo: A treacherous traverse across loose ash slopes south of Ignivex where active vents open without warning and the ground shifts underfoot. Corsair route crews use this crossing to bypass the formal gate checkpoints on the wall routes. The ash is deep, grey, and featureless — a Glassmidge swarm rises here before every storm, and the crossing is impassable until the front has passed.
Ashslope Vent Crossing.hiddenInfo: Corsair smugglers maintain a cached rope line across the worst section of the slope, anchored to buried stakes that look like vent markers. The route bypasses Volen's wall gate entirely, which is the point. A Ventcrawler gallery system runs beneath the crossing, and the ash has collapsed into it twice this season — the second time with a Corsair runner on top. They survived. The crawler did not appreciate the visit.

Upper Ash Field.description: Deep loose ash on a slope steep enough that every step slides backward half its length. The ash is grey, fine, and warm. Vent steam rises in thin columns from cracks in the slope. A rope line — old, frayed, anchored to buried stakes — runs across the slope at chest height. Without the rope, the crossing is a controlled slide toward the vent cracks below. Glassmidge casings crunch underfoot.

Vent Crack Zone.description: A band of cracked ground across the middle of the slope where vents open in narrow fissures. Steam and heat rise from the cracks — some hiss, some are silent. The silent ones are worse: they open without warning when the pressure below shifts. The ash around active cracks is discoloured yellow-grey with mineral deposits. A burned boot lies beside a crack that was not there last week.

Collapsed Gallery.description: A section of slope where the ash has dropped into a Ventcrawler gallery below, leaving a ragged pit two Starian-lengths across. The gallery is visible at the bottom — smooth-walled, warm, glowing faintly with mineral deposits. A Ventcrawler's tail club is visible in the gallery, wedged defensively. Rope fragments hang from the slope above where the cached line broke during the collapse.

Lower Ash Runout.description: The base of the ash slope where loose material has run out into a fan of grey debris on flat dark rock. The Corsair route emerges here, marked with small cairns of dark stone that blend into the natural rubble. The formal wall routes are visible to the north as a dark line against the sky. Anyone standing here is visible from the wall-top walkway if the watch is looking south.

Old Flow Ambush Point.name: Old Flow Ambush Point
Old Flow Ambush Point.basicInfo: A bend in the old flow road where lava sheets narrow the corridor route to a single-hauler width. Every faction with corridor interests knows this bend — it is the most reliable ambush point on the southern route and has been used by the Black Pennant, the Claimants, and the Last Line Company at different times. Convoy escorts treat the approach with the respect it has earned.
Old Flow Ambush Point.hiddenInfo: The bend has changed hands four times this season. Currently the Claimants hold the high ground — a team of three with a contract to intercept a specific Dravon courier run. The Bent Halo has used the same bend to extract refugees from convoys by arrangement with sympathetic drivers. The Last Line Company has standing orders to clear any faction blockade here for paying clients, and has done so twice. Nobody owns this ground; they borrow it.

Flow Road Approach.description: The corridor route runs straight across old flow country — dark grey to black stone lying in long low rolls. The road surface is compacted ash over rock, firm and flat. Ahead, the road narrows where two lava ridges close in from either side. Fresh vehicle tracks show recent traffic. A Claimants waymarker — a cairn with a coloured rag — sits at the approach, visible only to those who know the code.

The Narrows Bend.description: The corridor narrows to single-hauler width between walls of frozen lava, the road curving sharply left around a ridge shoulder. A vehicle entering the bend cannot see what waits beyond it. Cargo nets, cable, and debris from previous blockades litter the margins. The walls are too steep and smooth to climb quickly. This is where convoys are stopped.

Ridge Observation Post.description: A position on top of the lava ridge overlooking both the approach and the narrows bend, reached by a scramble up a rough natural staircase in the flow rock. Shell casings and food wrappers mark long watches. The position gives a clear sightline in both directions along the corridor. A signal mirror, a water flask, and a rolled ground cloth sit in a crack in the rock — someone was here recently.

Lava Ridge High Ground.description: The top of the lava ridge above the narrows bend, a narrow spine of dark rock with drop-offs on both sides. From here, the entire corridor route is visible for a kilometre in each direction, and a person on the ridge can speak to anyone trapped in the narrows below. Faction graffiti from three different groups marks the rock — territory claims layered over each other in scratched paint.

Ashpan Coastal Flats.name: Ashpan Coastal Flats
Ashpan Coastal Flats.basicInfo: Low black ground running toward the coast, flat enough to walk and rough enough to turn an ankle. Tideclaws come up from the shore at night and Glassmidge swarms rise before storms. The flats sit between the volcanic waste inland and the coast, exposed to both the desert wind and the salt air. Salvage crews cross the flats to reach coastal wreck sites but avoid camping here.
Ashpan Coastal Flats.hiddenInfo: A dead Derelict Cargo Lifter sits on the flats, its chassis half-sunk into the ash pan. The lifter has been stripped of its cargo but the power core is still warm — Glassmidges cluster on it at night and Dustrunners investigate it at dusk. A salvage crew has tagged the hull for recovery but has not returned. Tideclaw tracks lead from the coast to the hull and back.

Ash Pan Crossing.description: Flat black ground stretching in every direction, the surface broken into irregular plates by thermal cycling. Ash fills the cracks between plates in pale lines. The ground radiates heat in daylight and cools fast after dark. Tracks are easy to read here — every passage leaves prints in the ash between the plates. The coast is a dark line to the south; the volcanic waste rises to the north.

Dead Lifter Hull.description: A Derelict Cargo Lifter's chassis, half-sunk in the ash pan at a slight tilt, its cargo clamps empty and its hull panels buckled. The power core hums faintly — not dead, not functional, leaking enough energy to draw Glassmidges after dark. A salvage tag is wired to the forward strut. Dustrunner claw marks score the lower hull where the pack has tested the seams for cargo residue.

Shore Approach.description: The ash pan thins to bare black rock at the coast, the transition marked by salt crusting and Tideclaw tracks — sideways drag marks and claw scores heading inland from the tide line. The rock is slick with spray. At low tide, a gravel beach is visible below the rock shelf. At high tide, the water reaches the rock edge and the Tideclaws come up.

Bare Shoulder Pass.name: Bare Shoulder Pass
Bare Shoulder Pass.basicInfo: A mountain pass through the bare grey shoulders east of Quilrath, where Ridgewing territory overlaps the route between the highland settlements and the coast. The pass is the fastest path through the ridge but crosses the Ridgewing pair's nesting band. Ground travellers are ignored; fliers are challenged. Route crews mark the territory boundaries with warning posts that the wind tears down every Longburn.
Bare Shoulder Pass.hiddenInfo: A Ridgewing pair has nested on the lee face above the pass for six seasons. The female is larger than average and her warning stoops have come closer to contact each year. A Quilrath flight instructor uses this pass as a final exam — students who can navigate the territory without triggering a stoop graduate. Students who cannot descend on foot. The pair produced a chick this Brightrise, and the male's territorial range has expanded to cover the eastern approach.

Western Approach.description: A trail of grey fractured rock climbing through blunt shoulders of bare stone, the wind funnelling through gaps between the rock formations. A warning post — tilted, repainted three times — marks the lower boundary of Ridgewing territory: 'ACTIVE PAIR — GROUND TRANSIT ONLY — NO FLIGHT IN PASS'. The trail is steep but walkable. Above, the sky is watched.

Pass Summit.description: The highest point of the pass, a narrow saddle between two bare shoulders with a drop on both sides. Wind is constant and strong. The sky is open and the Ridgewing nest is visible on the lee face of the northern shoulder — a mass of branch-like material and mineral plating wedged into a crevice. The female is usually visible, a large grey shape on the nest edge. Flight here triggers immediate response.

Sheltered Notch.description: A notch in the rock below the pass summit, sheltered from the wind and invisible from above. Large enough for three people to wait. Travellers caught by weather or waiting for a Ridgewing to settle use this notch. Scratched messages cover the inner walls — route advice, warnings about the pair's mood this season, a crude drawing of the female with measurements.

Eastern Descent.description: The eastern side of the pass descends in a series of rock steps toward the lower country. The trail is exposed to the sky for the first two hundred metres — the danger zone. A Ridgewing pellet accumulation at the first step marks the edge of the male's patrol range. Below the pellet line, the trail drops between rock walls and the sky narrows to a strip. Safe ground.

Sand Flat Waystation.name: Sand Flat Waystation
Sand Flat Waystation.basicInfo: A Corsair-maintained waystation on the broad sand flats south of the Ignivex approaches, marking a route junction where the southern corridor meets the desert crossing toward the coastal settlements. Water, shade, and a charging point for drones and equipment. The waystation is open to all corridor traffic but Corsair keeps the water supply and takes a use fee.
Sand Flat Waystation.hiddenInfo: The waystation's water comes from a buried pipeline tapped off the Ignivex geothermal system — House Volen knows about it and permits it because Corsair route crews maintain the section of desert road that Volen's own patrols refuse to walk. The Bent Halo uses the waystation as a handoff point for refugee movement, paying Corsair's fee without questions. A Dustrunner pack has learned the waystation's resupply schedule and raids the water cache on the nights between deliveries.

Waystation Yard.description: A cleared area of compacted sand around a prefab shelter and a water tank on a raised platform. A Corsair route marker — a painted post with distance plates — stands at the yard centre. A charging point for drones and equipment hums on a solar-thermal unit. The yard is swept clean but Dustrunner tracks cross it from the northeast, and the water tank's drain valve has been chewed.

Water Cache.description: A buried cistern accessed through a locked hatch behind the shelter, fed by a pipeline from the Ignivex geothermal system. The hatch shows tool marks from unauthorized access — both Dustrunner claw damage and pry marks from something with hands. Water level is low. A Corsair maintenance log on the wall records deliveries and discrepancies. The last entry notes 'cache short again — tracks NE'.

Desert Overlook.description: A low rise of weathered dark rock behind the waystation, giving a view across the sand flats in all directions. The southern corridor is visible as a dark line heading toward the coast. The Ignivex wall routes are a distant dark line to the north. At night, Ignivex's forge-glow lights the northern horizon orange. Desert wind carries fine sand that stings exposed skin.

Junction Marker.description: The route junction itself — a post with directional plates pointing toward Ignivex (north), the coastal settlements (south-west), and the Dustfall corridor (east). The sand around the junction is churned with vehicle and foot traffic. Corsair route signs give distances, hazard warnings, and water availability. A Bent Halo signal mark — a tilted circle scratched into the post's base — is visible only if you know to look.

Greywater Margin Hunting Grounds.name: Greywater Margin Hunting Grounds
Greywater Margin Hunting Grounds.basicInfo: Open ground and scattered timber stands along the forest margin where the continuous canopy breaks apart. The transition zone draws fauna from both forest and open country — Trailhounds work this margin with their handlers, Dustrunners probe from the waste, and Fieldmoth swarms drift from the beacon lines at night. The mix of cover and open ground makes it natural hunting territory.
Greywater Margin Hunting Grounds.hiddenInfo: Helvyra's route maintenance crews use the margin as a staging area for forest patrols, and an informal market in pelts, Dustrunner teeth, and Fieldmoth wing cases operates from a camp that no one officially acknowledges. The camp is technically on unclaimed ground, but a Dravon patrol has started visiting every second week, which the traders interpret as a protection arrangement and Dravon interprets as a census.

Forest Edge.description: The tree line — scattered conifers and scrub thinning to open ground. Game trails emerge from the timber and cross the margin toward water. Trailhound handler teams work the edge in pairs, tracking Dustrunner sign. Fieldmoth cocoons hang in the lower branches at the forest edge, dormant by day. The ground is a mix of needle litter, gravel, and the first grass-like growth.

Open Margin.description: Open ground between the timber and the waste — low scrub, exposed rock, and grass tussocks. Visibility is good in all directions. Dustrunner tracks cross the margin from east to west, following the game trails. A beacon post on the margin edge hums at night, drawing Fieldmoth swarms from the forest. The post's light is dimmer than it should be — something has been feeding on its charge.

Trader Camp.description: An informal camp at the margin where pelts, teeth, wing cases, and other fauna products change hands. Three shelters, a fire circle, and a drying rack for hides. The traders are frontier people — route crew, settlement volunteers, off-duty handlers. Prices are fair, provenance is not discussed. A Dravon patrol marker sits at the camp's north edge, planted two weeks ago. The traders have not moved it.

The Darkened Rows.name: The Darkened Rows
The Darkened Rows.basicInfo: Quilrath's outer housing belt where the red command-lighting has failed in the middle stretches and nobody has come to fix it. Prefab rows run in long unbroken lines, their panels of several different ages and none of them matched. External stairs are bolted on. People here live under Dravon's rules without Dravon's investment — rent collected, curfew enforced, maintenance deferred. The rows house shift workers, low-standing families, relocated populations and anyone whose Standing Grade keeps them out of the Gray Rings but off the open streets.
The Darkened Rows.hiddenInfo: The lighting failure is not neglect — it is policy. Nivarek records show the maintenance budget was reallocated to surveillance upgrades in the inner city three seasons ago, and the work order was closed as 'deferred pending review'. Residents have rigged their own lights from salvaged parts, which is technically an unauthorized modification. A Kathvar-linked black-market electrician runs a repair service from Row 14 that Dravon patrols know about and have not shut down because the alternative is total darkness in three blocks.

Row 7 Walk.description: A long ground-level walkway between two prefab rows, lit only by the residents' own rigged lamps — salvaged work lights, repurposed drone charging indicators, and strips of adhesive glow-tape along the stair rails. The official red command-lights are dead sockets above the doorways. Laundry lines cross between the rows at second-floor height. Children use the walkway as a play corridor after shift change. The composite underfoot is cracked and patched with a different shade of grey.

Stairwell Landing 4.description: An external stairwell bolted to the side of Row 7, its metal treads ringing underfoot and its railing wrapped in grip-tape where the original coating has worn through. The fourth-floor landing has become an informal meeting point — a bench made from a cargo pallet, a water flask on a hook, and a view down the length of the rows in both directions. Residents pass information here that they would not say at ground level where the patrol microphones might still work.

Row End Market.description: A small informal market at the junction where three rows meet, operating in the service gap between buildings where the roof overhang provides shelter. Stalls are cargo crates and folding tables. Goods are provisions, repair parts, secondhand clothing, and cooked food from a woman who has been here longer than the rows have. Prices are Standing-adjusted — residents below Grade 3 pay less, by quiet agreement. A Dravon patrol passes the market's mouth twice per shift and has never entered it.

The Unlit Stretch.description: A three-block section where every command-light has failed and the residents have not replaced them. The stretch is dark after curfew — navigated by memory, by the faint glow from windows, and by a system of tapped-wall signals the residents use to warn of patrol approaches. The darkness is deliberate: it is the one place in Quilrath where Dravon's surveillance has a genuine gap, and the residents maintain it by quietly discouraging anyone who tries to install a new light.

Upper Corridor.description: A fourth-floor enclosed walkway connecting three rows at their upper level, added after the original construction and showing it — the joins leak in Greenward, the floor flexes underfoot, and the transparent panels along one wall have hazed to near-opacity. Residents use the corridor as indoor social space when the weather is bad. A community notice board covers one wall: shift postings, lost-and-found, barter offers, and a handwritten curfew schedule that is more accurate than the official one.

The Curfew Corridors.name: The Curfew Corridors
The Curfew Corridors.basicInfo: Dense residential blockwork growing tighter as it approaches the inner city, where curfew gates stand across the through-routes and close on schedule. Grey panels four and five storeys tall, joined by enclosed walkways and served by stair towers at the corners. Everything here is controlled by the clock — the gates open at shift-start, close at curfew, and the time between is the only freedom of movement residents have. The corridors are Quilrath's most regulated residential ground outside the inner circle.
The Curfew Corridors.hiddenInfo: The curfew gate schedule has a deliberate fifteen-minute gap between the eastern and western gates closing, which Dravon uses to funnel late movement through a single monitored corridor. Nivarek installed the timing asymmetry and tracks who uses the gap — it is a loyalty test disguised as an administrative oversight. Three residents have been quietly relocated to outer housing after being flagged by the gap-monitoring system. The gate operators know about the asymmetry and consider it a professional hazard they cannot discuss.

East Curfew Gate.description: A heavy gate frame set into the building line across the main east-west through-route, its mechanism hydraulic and loud. The gate is open during authorized hours — a wide arch with scanner pylons on both sides logging everyone who passes. When it closes, the hydraulic arms pull a composite barrier across the route with a sound the entire corridor hears. A timer display above the gate counts down to the next opening. Guards stand at the gate during transition periods; at other times, the gate runs itself.

Central Corridor.description: The main through-route between the east and west curfew gates — a wide ground-level passage between blockwork walls, roofed by the enclosed walkways above. Red command-lights run the full length, functioning here because the corridor is a control point. Movement flows in both directions during authorized hours. The walls carry painted directional markers, standing-grade lane indicators, and official notices in Dravon's administrative style — precise, impersonal, and quietly threatening.

West Curfew Gate.description: The western gate, identical in construction to the eastern one but closing fifteen minutes later — a fact every resident knows and nobody mentions to Dravon. The western approach is narrower, with blockwork pressing close on both sides and the walkways overhead low enough to darken the route. Late-movement residents funnel through here in the gap between gate closings. The scanner pylons here are newer than the eastern ones.

Block 9 Stair Tower.description: A corner stair tower serving Block 9, its concrete steps worn smooth by decades of shift-change traffic. Landings at each floor connect to enclosed walkways running between blocks. The fifth-floor landing has a window with a view over the rooftops toward the inner city's star-glass towers — the only unobstructed sightline in the corridors. Someone has placed a small potted plant on the windowsill. It has been there for years and nobody has removed it.

Walkway Junction.description: Where three enclosed walkways meet at the upper level of Block 9, forming a covered intersection large enough to stand in. Residents pass through on their way between blocks. The junction has become an informal bulletin point — notes pinned to a board nobody installed, a water dispenser someone carried up three floors, and a small bench made from a door that came off its hinges. At curfew, the junction empties and the lights dim to standby.

Curfew Administration Office.description: A small ground-floor office beside the east gate where curfew exemptions, late-movement permits, and gate-timing disputes are processed by a Dravon administrative clerk. The office is a single room with a counter, a terminal, and a waiting bench that holds three people. Wait times average two hours. The clerk is efficient, not unkind, and bound by rules that permit no flexibility. A framed copy of the curfew schedule hangs behind the counter — the same schedule posted everywhere, but signed by a Nivarek records officer.

The Numbered Streets.name: The Numbered Streets
The Numbered Streets.basicInfo: Quilrath's eastern working district where streets meet at right angles and are known by numbers instead of names. Composite frontages, dark-toned and unbroken, with red command-lines dimmer than the inner city's. The grid was laid out for efficiency and has not been redesigned since. Residents here are industrial workers, maintenance crews, lower-grade administrators, and the families of people who were here before Dravon and have nowhere else to be. The district is orderly, functional, and forgotten by anyone who does not live in it.
The Numbered Streets.hiddenInfo: The street-numbering system was imposed by Nivarek during the first census after Dravon consolidated Quilrath, replacing the original neighbourhood names that residents still use among themselves. Street 14 is still called Ashwall Lane by everyone who lives on it, and the Dravon census clerk who processes that block's records has started using the old name without realising it. An Unbroken Accord contact operates from a repair shop on Street 22, running a document service that helps residents correct Standing Grade errors without going through the official appeals process.

Street 14 Block.description: A residential block on the street residents still call Ashwall Lane — dark composite frontage, recessed doorways, grated drainage channels running down the centre. The block is five storeys of identical units, each with a narrow balcony enclosed by the residents in mismatched materials for extra space. Ground-floor units have been converted to services: a laundry, a ration supplement shop, a repair counter. The street is quiet during shifts and crowded at changeover.

Street 22 Junction.description: Where Streets 14 and 22 meet at a precise right angle, forming a small square where a public water point and a civic notice board stand. The junction is the district's informal centre — shift workers cross it four times a day, market runners set up on the corners at dawn, and children gather at the water point after school hours. A repair shop on the 22 corner has been open longer than the current numbering system, and its owner knows everyone.

The Shift Canteen.description: A workers' canteen at the end of Street 14, serving three shift changes a day from a kitchen that has not closed in years. The food is institutional but hot — grain bowls, protein cuts, a thick broth that varies by season and by what the cook could find. Tables are communal and the room is loud at changeover. Off-shift workers come here because their units are cold. An unofficial job board covers the wall by the door — maintenance postings, favour trades, shift swaps written on scraps.

Patrol Kiosk.description: A small Dravon patrol kiosk at the northern end of the Numbered Streets, staffed by two officers per shift who process document checks, movement queries, and standing complaints. The kiosk is a prefab unit with a counter window and a door that locks from inside. The officers assigned here are typically junior — a Numbered Streets posting is not a career step. They know the district, they know the residents by face, and they enforce by the book because the book is all they have.

Drainage Works.description: A below-street maintenance access where the district's drainage channels converge at a junction chamber. The chamber is large enough to stand in and smells of chemical treatment and damp composite. Maintenance crews access it through a grated hatch on Street 14. The drainage system runs under the entire Numbered Streets grid and connects, eventually, to the inner city's sealed utilities — a fact that unauthorized travellers have occasionally exploited. The most recent attempt ended at a locked grate that was not there last season.

The Boundary Line.name: The Boundary Line
The Boundary Line.basicInfo: The outermost edge of Quilrath's built ground, where patched housing stops at a made road that follows the boundary without crossing it. Beyond the road: open volcanic rock, scattered scrub, and the beginning of the waste. Gates stand across the lane ends — some functional, some permanently open, some closed and forgotten. People who live on the Boundary Line are the last residents before the frontier, and they know it. Everything here faces inward, toward the city that barely acknowledges it.
The Boundary Line.hiddenInfo: The boundary road was never intended as a residential edge — it was a patrol route that housing grew up against. Dravon has no official plan for the Boundary Line because it does not officially exist as a district; the census records it as 'outer perimeter residential overspill'. Residents who need services travel inward to the Numbered Streets or the Gray Rings. An informal path through the boundary gates leads to a cache of supplies maintained by the Unbroken Accord for people who need to leave Quilrath without using a gate.

Boundary Road.description: A hard-surfaced road running along the edge of Quilrath's built ground, wide enough for a patrol vehicle and kept clear by regulation. On one side: the backs of the outermost housing blocks, their panels facing inward and their blank rear walls marking the city's edge. On the other side: open dark rock, sparse scrub, and the waste. Patrol vehicles pass at irregular intervals. Between patrols, the road belongs to the residents who use it as a walk, a market strip, and a meeting ground.

Lane End Gate.description: One of several gates set across the lane ends where residential streets meet the boundary road. This one is functional — a simple barrier arm and a scanner pylon, operated by a mechanism that responds to patrol override codes. The gate is closed at curfew and open during the day, though 'open' means 'unblocked' rather than 'unwatched'. Residents pass through it to reach the boundary road; non-residents are logged and questioned.

Edge Housing Block.description: The last housing block before the boundary road — three storeys of patched composite, the panels a patchwork of repairs spanning a decade. Ground-floor units face the lane; upper-floor units face the waste through narrow windows that residents have covered, curtained, or sealed depending on their relationship with the view. The block's interior corridor is dim and smells of cooking and damp composite. Community life happens in the corridor because the units are small.

Boundary Market.description: An informal market strip along the boundary road where residents trade provisions, secondhand goods, and services that the inner city does not provide at prices the boundary can afford. Stalls are ground cloths and folded tables. Trade is in standing-credits and barter. A food vendor sells grilled protein from a cart that moves along the road with the sun. The market operates during daylight hours and vanishes at curfew — nothing left but scuff marks on the road surface.

Rooftop Lookout.description: The flat roof of the edge housing block, accessed by a maintenance ladder that residents have fitted with better rungs. The roof gives a view over the boundary road to the waste in one direction and over the rooftops of Quilrath in the other. On a clear day, the star-glass towers of the inner city catch the light. Residents come up here for the air, for the view, and for conversations they do not want overheard. A salvaged chair and a water flask are permanently stationed by the waste-side parapet.

The Outer Yards.name: The Outer Yards
The Outer Yards.basicInfo: Quilrath's industrial perimeter — composite ranges set well apart with surfaced yards between them, fenced and gated at the road. This is where the city stores what it does not want near the centre: heavy equipment depots, salvage processing, drone maintenance facilities, and the cargo staging grounds that supply the outer districts. The yards are active during shift hours and patrolled at night. Red command-lights show on the gate posts and nowhere else along the fencing.
The Outer Yards.hiddenInfo: The Outer Yards handle the logistics that keep Quilrath's outer districts supplied, and the supply chain passes through hands that Dravon monitors but cannot fully control. A cargo staging master has been skimming medical supplies to the Boundary Line for two seasons, covering the shortfall with inventory adjustments that Nivarek's audit cycle has not yet caught. Three of the drone maintenance bays are used after hours by Balrath technicians running unauthorized upgrades on patrol drones — improvements that Balrath's official procurement cannot fund.

Cargo Staging Ground.description: A wide surfaced yard where supply convoys from the southern routes unload for distribution to Quilrath's outer districts. Cargo containers sit in ranked rows awaiting inspection and allocation. A staging office at the yard's edge processes manifests and assigns distribution routes. The work is heavy, constant, and underpaid. Staging crews know what is in every container and who it is going to, which makes them valuable to anyone who needs to know what Quilrath consumes.

Drone Maintenance Bay.description: A long composite shed housing drone repair and maintenance for Quilrath's outer patrol fleet. Ward-Class security drones hang from ceiling racks in various states of assembly. Diagnostic stations line the walls. The bay runs two shifts and the backlog is visible — deferred repairs stacked in the corner, parts-waiting drones tagged with dates that are weeks old. The bay smells of ozone, lubricant, and the particular frustration of technicians working without the parts they need.

Salvage Processing Shed.description: A shed where salvage from the waste and the southern routes is sorted, assessed, and either allocated to city maintenance or auctioned to licensed buyers. The shed is part warehouse, part workshop — cutting tools, weighing plates, a materials analyser that gives approximate readings. Salvage crews bring in what the frontier produces: broken drone chassis, stripped hauler parts, mineral samples, and occasionally something unusual enough that the processing foreman locks the shed and calls upward.

Equipment Depot.description: A secure compound within the yards storing heavy equipment — construction machinery, barrier components, gate hardware, and the replacement parts that keep Quilrath's infrastructure functional. The depot is fenced within the fence, locked with Balrath security codes, and inventoried by Nivarek. Access requires a work order and a gate pass. The depot master is a retired Balrath engineer who runs the inventory from memory and has not been wrong yet.

Perimeter Fence Line.description: The outer fence of the Yards district — chain-link topped with sensor wire, broken by vehicle gates at intervals. Beyond the fence: the boundary road and the waste. The fence is maintained where it faces the road and neglected where it faces empty ground. A section near the salvage shed has been repaired so many times that the original mesh is unrecognizable. Patrol drones fly the fence line at intervals; the gap between passes is predictable.

The Patrol Runs.name: The Patrol Runs
The Patrol Runs.basicInfo: Quilrath's outermost security belt — patrol roads running in long surfaced lines, linked by turning loops, with low composite sheds and chain-linked holding yards between them. This is where Dravon processes what the outer perimeter catches: unauthorized movement, curfew violations, smuggling attempts, and the occasional Dustrunner pack that gets too close to the built edge. The patrol runs are functional, bleak, and staffed by officers who consider the posting a punishment.
The Patrol Runs.hiddenInfo: The holding yards process more curfew violations than actual security threats, and the patrol officers know it. A quiet understanding exists between the run commanders and the Boundary Line residents: minor violations are processed with a warning and a standing-grade note rather than detention, because the detention facility is at capacity with smuggling cases and there is nowhere to put a curfew violator. Two officers have been reassigned for excessive leniency; the replacement officers adopted the same practice within a week.

Patrol Road South.description: A long surfaced road running south from the yards toward the waste, kerbed on both sides and marked with reflective lane paint. Patrol vehicles drive the road in loops; foot patrols walk the stretches between vehicle gates. The road surface is cracked from thermal cycling and patched with darker composite. Marker posts at intervals carry direction plates, distance readings, and patrol-shift identifiers. At night, the road's red reflectors are the only light.

Turning Loop Station.description: A turning loop where patrol vehicles reverse direction, built around a small composite station housing a comms relay, a rest shelter, and a charging point for drone handsets. The station is unattended most of the time — officers stop here to log position, refill water, and sit in a chair that is not a vehicle seat. A logbook on the shelf records patrol observations in increasingly terse shorthand. The most recent entry reads 'clear' in handwriting that suggests the writer did not get out of the vehicle.

Holding Yard 3.description: A chain-linked yard between patrol roads where detained individuals and confiscated materials are held for processing. The yard contains a covered waiting area, a processing desk under a corrugated roof, and a secured storage container for confiscated goods. The processing desk has a terminal, a scanner, and a stack of standing-grade forms that never seems to decrease. Detainees wait on a bench that holds six people; the average wait is four hours.

Watch Shed.description: A low composite shed at the junction of two patrol roads, serving as the local command post for the eastern patrol runs. Inside: a duty desk, a comms board, a drone monitoring screen showing four feeds from the perimeter, and a cot for the night-shift officer. The shed is warm in Deephold and stifling in Highfire. Maps of the patrol routes cover one wall, annotated in three different handwriting styles from three different commanders who each reorganized the routes and none of whom improved them.

Glass Threshold Market.name: Glass Threshold Market
Glass Threshold Market.basicInfo: The commercial transition between Quilrath's inner star-glass district and the outer composite city. Shops and services line the ground level where star-glass frontage gives way to grey composite, catering to residents who can afford more than the Numbered Streets but less than the inner city. Licensed vendors, approved service providers, and the occasional establishment that has survived three changes of regulation. Surveillance pylons line the planted strips between buildings, watching everything.
Glass Threshold Market.hiddenInfo: The Glass Threshold is where Dravon's economy meets its population. The licensed businesses here pay fees that fund inner-city maintenance, and the fee schedule is calibrated to extract the maximum that each business can survive. A Kathvar-backed lending service operates behind a licensed provisions shop, offering standing-grade improvement loans at rates that keep borrowers paying for years. The surveillance pylons record everything but the footage is reviewed only when Nivarek requests it, which means most transactions here are watched but not seen.

Threshold Arcade.description: A covered shopping arcade running along the ground level of the last star-glass building before the composite begins. The glass frontage overhead throws refracted red command-light across the arcade floor. Shops sell regulated goods: approved clothing, personal equipment, communication devices, and provisions at controlled prices. The arcade is clean, orderly, and monitored — the transition from the inner city's polish to the outer city's function happens one shop at a time.

Threshold Plaza.description: An open plaza where the star-glass frontage ends and the planted strip begins, with benches, a public water point, and a surveillance pylon at each corner. The plaza is a crossing point between the inner and outer city — residents moving inward for work pass residents moving outward after shift. A public address system plays civic announcements at intervals. The plaza's design is deliberate: open sightlines in every direction, no blind spots, no place to gather that is not observed.

Licensed Provisions Hall.description: A large provisions store where outer-city residents buy staples at regulated prices. The hall is functional — shelving units in rows, a weighing counter, a payment terminal, and a standing-grade verification scanner at the entrance that determines which price tier each customer pays. The provisions are adequate and unvaried. Behind the counter, a back room serves as the front for a Kathvar lending operation that most customers know about and the hall manager pretends not to.

Pylon Walk.description: A planted strip between the glass threshold and the outer composite blocks, lined with surveillance pylons at regular intervals. The plants are low, squared, and maintained by a civic crew that works on schedule. The pylons record movement, conversation proximity, and standing-grade transponder data. Walking the Pylon Walk is the fastest route between the Threshold and the Numbered Streets, and residents do it quickly, heads down, without stopping.

The Bridged Blocks.name: The Bridged Blocks
The Bridged Blocks.basicInfo: Residential blockwork where covered walkways bridge between upper floors, creating a layered district with ground-level streets and an upper-level network that residents know better than any map. The blocks are low composite — cleaner and closer-set than the Darkened Rows, older and plainer than the Gray Rings. People here have moderate Standing Grades and the kind of stability that comes from not being noticed. The walkway network is the district's real infrastructure — social space, trade corridor, and information channel rolled into one.
The Bridged Blocks.hiddenInfo: The walkway network was built for maintenance access and has been quietly repurposed by residents into the district's primary social infrastructure. Dravon's surveillance covers the ground-level streets thoroughly but the upper walkways have camera coverage only at the major junctions. Residents conduct sensitive conversations on the walkways between junctions, and the district's informal economy — tutoring, repair services, document assistance — operates primarily at upper level. A Nivarek audit noted the surveillance gap two seasons ago; the recommended cameras have not been installed because the installation budget was allocated to the inner city.

Ground Street.description: A ground-level street between two rows of low composite blocks, paved and drained, with red command-lights at the intersections and darkness between them. The street is a transit corridor — residents walk it to reach the block entrances and the walkway stairs, but they do not linger. Surveillance cameras cover the full length. A civic notice board at the intersection carries official postings: curfew times, standing-grade clinic hours, and a water-system maintenance notice dated two months ago.

Walkway Stair.description: A staircase built into the junction between two blocks, leading from the surveilled ground street to the upper walkway network. The stairs are concrete with metal rails, worn smooth by traffic. The transition from ground to walkway is the transition from watched to unwatched — residents straighten up on the stairs and relax at the top. A small shelf at the landing holds a communal water jug that someone refills every morning.

Upper Walkway.description: A covered walkway connecting three blocks at second-floor level, enclosed on both sides with panels that cut the wind and muffle the sound from the street below. The walkway is the district's living room — residents stop to talk, children do homework on the floor, and the repair woman at the walkway's midpoint fixes anything brought to her for a standing-credit and a favour owed. Camera coverage exists only at the junctions; the stretches between are private by omission.

Block Courtyard.description: An interior courtyard shared by four blocks, accessible through ground-floor passageways. The courtyard is too small for a vehicle and too overlooked for privacy, but it gets light, which the ground streets do not. Residents have planted it — small containers of herbs, a climbing plant on the southern wall, a flat-leafed scrub that survives Quilrath's air. Children play here under the supervision of whichever household has the courtyard-facing window open. The planting is technically unauthorized.

Walkway Tea Room.description: A converted unit at the walkway's western end, its door permanently open during waking hours, serving tea and small meals from a counter built across what was once a residential doorway. The tea room has four tables, mismatched chairs, and a view through a cleaned window onto the courtyard below. The owner is an elderly woman whose standing grade has not changed in twenty years and whose opinion on district matters carries more weight than the patrol kiosk's. Payment is flexible.
